name: Shardlings
visual: Splinters of living crystal. Skitter like insects. Emit faint psychic hum.
behavior: Nuisance alone. In swarms, crawl mechs, cut seams, project harmonics.
report_text: “Audible resonance detected at 18 kHz. Troopers bled from the ears before contact was even made.”

name: Fracture Drone
visual: Angular shards hovering inches above ground, constantly splitting and rejoining.
behavior: Emit beams of refracted light. In swarms, slice like spinning saws.
report_text: “Target divided mid-volley. Ammunition expenditure doubled with no reduction in contacts.”

name: Resonators
visual: Bell-shaped bodies, surfaces vibrating.
behavior: Sonic pulses disrupt comms, collapse tunnels, shatter armor. Groups amplify one another.
report_text: “Tunnel integrity dropped to zero within seconds. No charges planted - walls simply collapsed from resonance.”

name: Shardthralls
visual: Animals or humanoids overtaken by crystalline growth. Limbs stiff, joints crack.
behavior: Attack with glass claws and snapping jaws. Shatter into shards on death.
report_text: “Subject identified as local farmer until 36 hours ago. Family confirms disappearance. Returned as thrall.”

name: Crystalbound
visual: Humanoids with crystalline veins, eyes replaced by glowing facets. Voices echo in broken cadence.
behavior: Wield crude crystal weapons, emit resonance pulses. Retain fragments of memory.
report_text: [Pilot log] “He called my name before he struck. Wrong cadence, but the right voice.”

name: Facet Howlers
visual: Beasts or soldiers with prism horns for heads.
behavior: Scream in mirrored tones, rupturing stone and flesh.
report_text: Victims show bilateral skull fractures consistent with internal pressure spikes. No external trauma observed.

name: Prismborn
visual: Angular crystalline warriors. Blood replaced by liquid light.
behavior: Strike with crystal-forged weapons. Can briefly reflect energy attacks.
report_text: “Squad’s own plasma fire reflected back through their formation. Friendly casualties at 63%.”

name: Lattice Hounds
visual: Predators reframed in crystalline skeletons. Transparent fangs, refracting bodies.
behavior: Pack hunters. Disrupt sensors. Tear through flesh and plating.
report_text: Contacts appeared as static on mech HUDs until physical impact. Packs moved undetected past three sweeps.

name: Crystic Knights
visual: Fully converted soldiers in crystalline shells. Movements stiff but devastating.
behavior: Wield halberds fused to their arms. Slam ground with resonance pulses.
report_text: “Single ground strike caused seismic readings equivalent to demolition charges. Squad cohesion lost.”

name: Cerebrax Stalker
visual: Four-legged crystalline beast, edges glowing.
behavior: Drills through plating with jagged limbs. Fast skirmisher.
report_text: “Hull breach occurred without heat signature or explosive force. Armor simply split.”

name: Cerebrax Breaker
visual: Massive knot of shards, held together by psionic force.
behavior: Breacher unit. Footfalls quake terrain.
report_text: Impact shocks consistent with 5.2 magnitude tremors. No tectonic activity recorded - localized to unit movement.

name: Cerebrax Reflector
visual: Tall, spindly construct of mirrors.
behavior: Splits energy attacks into scattering beams.
report_text: “Energy ordinance ineffective. Friendly fire casualties result from reflection scatter. Recommend kinetic only.”

name: Cerebrax Obelisk
visual: Walking crystal tower inscribed with glowing runes.
behavior: Channels devastating psionic blasts. Shardlings orbit as satellites.
report_text: “Obelisk not firing at squad. Terrain altered instead - cover reduced, battlefield geometry rewritten.”

name: Cerebrax Assimilator
visual: Humanoid crystal mass, dozens of faces visible beneath surface.
behavior: Extends lattices to ensnare prey. Attempts to crystallize targets piece by piece.
report_text: “Right arm converted to crystal on contact. Pilot ceased transmission simultaneously.”

name: Cerebrax Nexus
visual: Pyramidal construct on legs, etched in glyphs.
behavior: Projects psionic pulses to synchronize nearby units.
report_text: “Shardlings, Knights, and Stalkers moved with absolute precision. Loss rates spiked 400% once Nexus arrived.”

name: Cerebrax Singularity
visual: Floating sphere of facets folding inward and outward.
behavior: Warps gravity and light. Draws victims into orbit.
report_text: “We were walking level ground, but the incline felt impossible. Half the team vanished into the air.”

name: Cerebrax Overmind
visual: Titanic crystalline humanoid. Body glows with trapped souls, each shard an echo of a civilization.
behavior: Commands sectors. Assimilation spreads like wildfire.
report_text: “Identified faces matched 12 separate colony registries. Confirmation pending, but accuracy rate high.”

name: Cerebrax Convergence
visual: Colossal lattice rising like a spire, reshaping land into crystal forests.
behavior: Psionic domination spreads planetwide. Marks total assimilation.
report_text: “Initial vegetation replaced by crystal growth within 72 hours. By day five, atmospheric refraction indicated world-scale lattice.”

name: Shard-Cutters
visual: Small crystal darts, 40–60m long. Shards trail light like comets.
behavior: Skirmishers. Slash across hulls, embedding fragments into armor.
report_text: “Hull breach resealed itself - not metal, but more shards growing inward.”

name: Prism Frigate
visual: Angular, faceted hulls, 200m long. Entire structure refracts light into weaponized beams.
behavior: Emits resonance lances and dazzling scatterbursts.
report_text: “Targeting systems useless - half the beams weren’t real, but enough were.”

name: Obelisk Cruiser
visual: Towerlike mass, 400m tall, covered in runic crystal veins.
behavior: Focuses psionic shockwaves that scramble crew cohesion. Lesser shards orbit as escort.
report_text: “They didn’t fire at us. The crew just stopped moving, one by one.”

name: Convergence Spire
visual: Planet-scale crystalline growths emerging from converted hulls, kilometers long.
behavior: Absorb smaller vessels into lattice. Used to seed planetary assimilation.
report_text: “If one anchors in-orbit, consider the world lost.”

name: March Levy
visual: Conscripts in rugged flak plating with projectile rifles.
behavior: Hold walls and patrol colonies; cheap, numerous, poorly trained.
report_text: “A levy stands because the house commands it, not because it wishes to.”

name: March Pikeman
visual: Infantry with shock-pikes and riot shields.
behavior: Defend chokepoints, form tight phalanxes.
report_text: “Pikemen can slow even a warframe if their line holds.”

name: March Veteran
visual: Scarred soldiers in upgraded kit, bearing resonance carbines and blades.
behavior: Lead levy squads, maintain cohesion in fire.
report_text: “One veteran steadies ten levies.”

name: March Warden
visual: Elite troopers in reinforced composite armor.
behavior: Guard fortresses and nobles; perform precision raids.
report_text: “Wardens strike where hesitation would shame the house.”

name: March Skirmisher
visual: Light patrol frame with small artillery pods.
behavior: Scout ahead, harass enemies, screen larger units.
report_text: “Skirmishers bought us hours we did not deserve.”

name: March Vanguard
visual: Large frontline mech, shielded and durable.
behavior: Anchor battlelines, endure prolonged firefights. Cindral March MBF (main battle frame).
report_text: “Every Vanguard destroyed cost us three times its weight in munitions.”

name: March Bastion Frame
visual: Low, broad frame built from standardized armor blocks, with barrier emitters mounted along its shoulders and forearms.
behavior: Deploys overlapping shields and portable cover to reinforce weakened sections of the line.
report_text: “The bombardment continued for six hours. The line behind the Bastions did not move.”

name: March Relay Frame
visual: Tall command frame with hardened communication array.
behavior: Coordinates artillery, reserves, and evacuation routes while maintaining command through jamming and infrastructure loss.
report_text: “Every tower was down. The Relay kept the batteries firing on one clock.”

name: March Interdictor
visual: Lean attacker frame with reinforced joints, heavy maneuvering thrusters, and a compact anti-frame weapon suite.
behavior: Held behind the line until a breach forms, then committed rapidly to isolate and destroy the penetrating force.
report_text: “Breach opened at 0412. Closed at 0419.”

name: March Redoubt
visual: Gargantuan frame built around a slab-sided armored core, deployable stabilizers, and recessed gun positions.
behavior: Occupies chokepoints and converts exposed ground into a fortified position.
report_text: “By dawn, the Redoubt was no longer positioned in the pass. It was the pass.”

name: March Breacher
visual: Vast assault frame with reinforced limbs, demolition claws, and short-range bunker guns.
behavior: Opens fortified routes for advancing forces by dismantling obstacles under sustained fire.
report_text: “The gate did not fall. The Breacher removed it.”

name: Polemarch Command Frame
visual: Colossal command frame with layered armor, long-range sensor arrays, cannons, and detachable drones.
behavior: Directs system-scale operations by coordinating reserves, artillery, and fortified positions through a battlefield network.
report_text: “The Polemarch fired no weapon. Every battery in the sector did.”

name: Hauler-Class Freighter
visual: Long rectangular hull stacked with modular cargo containers. Painted in faction colors or corporate logos.
behavior: Standard cargo mover. Easy prey without escort.
report_text: “Convoy lost three haulers before gunships arrived. Goods unrecoverable.”

name: Pilgrim-Class Liner
visual: Graceful hull with wide viewing decks, domed gardens, and spires. Often painted white and gold.
behavior: Passenger transport, ferrying colonists and pilgrims.
report_text: “Seven thousand aboard. Half children. They never made orbit.”

name: Colony Seeder
visual: Bulky, block-shaped vessel with ventral bays for prefab habitats, hydroponics, and atmospheric processors.
behavior: Deploys infrastructure for new colonies.
report_text: “Seeders aren’t ships, they’re foundations. Kill one, and the colony dies before it begins.”

name: Stellar-Class Barge
visual: A long, flat cargo platform lashed together with exposed frames. Tug vessels drag it system-to-system.
behavior: Moves bulk ore, water, and raw resources.
report_text: “We saw the barge drifting. The escorts were gone. Cargo stripped to the frame.”

name: Medical-Class Ark
visual: White hull with red-and-gold beacon bands, broadcast transponders always active. Decks hold triage wards and storage for medical supplies.
behavior: Field hospital in space. Neutral by convention, but not always respected.
report_text: “Gunfire ignored the beacon. Casualty count doubled because no one would honor the paint.”

name: Merchant-Class Interceptor
visual: Sleek shuttle-sized craft, often painted in corporate livery. Built for rapid planetary runs.
behavior: Couriers and smugglers alike use them.
report_text: “Paint it red, slap a guild crest on the side. No one checks the cargo.”

name: Sanctuary-Class Ark
visual: Vast white vessel, lined with observation bays and shrines. Interior holds gardens, schools, and communal halls.
behavior: Long-haul refuge ship, ferrying evacuees or entire populations.
report_text: “We thought we’d left the war behind. Then the stars turned red in the viewport.”

name: Civic-Class Hauler
visual: Squat, six-wheeled truck with modular cargo bed. Covered in dust, dents, and family paint marks.
behavior: Backbone of colony logistics. Moves food, ore, and water.
report_text: “We saw the convoy burned. Half the loads were still strapped to the frames, untouched.”

name: Skytram Carriage
visual: Long passenger capsule suspended from grav-rails. Glass sides reveal rows of seats and standing straps.
behavior: Short-haul urban transit. Often converted into evacuation trains.
report_text: “Cut the power and they just drop. Whole line went down in a cascade.”

name: Crawler Rig
visual: Enormous treaded platform with armored cabins perched high above the wheels. Dust encrusts every surface.
behavior: Long-range land transport for settlers, often with whole families aboard.
report_text: “Home is where the crawler parks. Some of us never step foot off them.”

name: Atmos Skimmer
visual: Wide-bodied hovercraft with curved canopy, powered by grav-plates that glow faint blue underneath.
behavior: Common civilian transport across cities and riverlands. Luxury models double as shuttles.
report_text: “Two dozen skimmers bottlenecked at the bridge. Raiders came out of the fog before anyone could lift.”

name: Terra-Drill Utility Vehicle
visual: Massive machine with a rotary drill head and rear stabilizers. Hull reinforced against quakes.
behavior: Mining and tunneling vehicle, sometimes repurposed into makeshift fortifications.
report_text: “Drill jammed halfway through bedrock. Crew went missing. Found the cabin empty, engine still running.”

name: Pilgrim Caravan
visual: A line of covered grav-wagons, decorated with cloth banners and shrine icons. Glows softly at night.
behavior: Moves religious communities and refugees across hostile ground.
report_text: “We walked beside it for three weeks. When the guns found us, the caravan didn’t stop.”

name: City Strider
visual: Tall-legged walker resembling a moving tower block. Windows light up like an apartment at night.
behavior: Mobile habitat, used in dense megacities where land is scarce.
report_text: “The legs buckled during the quake. An entire neighborhood collapsed with it.”

name: Dust Sailer
visual: Lightweight frame with wheeled runners and a grav-sail mast catching atmospheric currents.
behavior: Used by nomads and thrill-seekers on desert worlds. Fast, fragile, iconic.
report_text: “Saw one racing the storm front. Never saw it come out the other side.”

name: Ironclad
visual: Boxy, low-slung tank with overlapping armor plates. Exhaust ports glow faint blue with resonance bleed.
behavior: Standard battlefield tank. Crushes infantry, stalls lighter mechs.
report_text: “One round hit our flank. Armor vibrated apart like teeth rattling loose.”

name: Basilisk
visual: A massive long-barrel gun mounted on tracks, ribbed with glowing vents.
behavior: Siege artillery. Reduces fortifications in minutes.
report_text: “Wall integrity collapsed before charges were planted. The Basilisk did the work for us.”

name: Mule Carrier
visual: Brick-shaped armored transport with drop-ramp rear. Scars from constant patchwork repairs.
behavior: Delivers infantry directly into contested zones.
report_text: “We rolled out into live fire. The Mule was already smoking, but it got us there.”

name: Razor Skimmer
visual: Sleek grav-hover, blade-shaped prow cutting through dust and rubble.
behavior: Fast strike craft for patrols and ambushes.
report_text: “Contact closed the distance too fast - we thought it was atmospheric clutter until the cannons opened.”

name: Starhawk-Class Fighter
visual: Angular frame with swept wings and bright exhaust trails. The most common fighter silhouette in Primus.
behavior: Multipurpose interceptor and escort.
report_text: “If you’ve seen one, you’ve seen a hundred. Doesn’t make them less lethal.”

name: Thunderbolt-Class Bomber
visual: Bulky fuselage with underslung bomb bays, striped in warning colors.
behavior: Heavy bomber. Devastates ground targets, but needs escort.
report_text: “Payload hit like a miniature sun. Nothing in the blast radius survived.”

name: Wasp Drone
visual: Insectlike drone, stubby wings, swarming in glittering clouds.
behavior: Disposable swarms overwhelm defenses.
report_text: “Readings showed hundreds of craft. Counted wreckage after - there weren’t even fifty.”

name: Falcon Ace Frame
visual: Cross between a starfighter and a knight’s mech, with blade-like resonance fins. Unique to each pilot.
behavior: Elite strike unit. Duels enemy aces and smaller mechs.
report_text: “It moved like it knew my strike before I made it. I was outflown before I even fired.”

name: Hawkwing Flight Frame
visual: Rigid alloy wings folded against the mech’s back, unfolding into broad, angular surfaces lined with thruster vents.
behavior: Standard atmospheric flight system. Provides lift and maneuverability in thick atmospheres.
report_text: “Engaged Hawkwing-equipped unit over canyon terrain. The frame was unwieldy on the ground, but once airborne, it turned the valley into a killing field.”

name: Stratos Boost Pack
visual: Twin-engine pack mounted over the spine, glowing with pale resonance exhaust. Stabilizer fins extend like spears.
behavior: High-altitude booster pack. Enables rapid vertical takeoff and sustained hover, but limited in endurance.
report_text: “The Stratos frame burned bright enough to spot from orbit. It can climb, but the fuel draw is suicidal in prolonged engagements.”

name: Valkyrie EVA Array
visual: Compact dorsal frame with multi-vector thrusters, ringed with sensor vanes and micro-gyros.
behavior: Designed for zero-G combat. Provides fine-tuned maneuvering in vacuum; ineffective in atmosphere.
report_text: “Boarding action confirmed. Enemy mechs drifted like sharks in water - slow, deliberate, impossible to shake once latched.”

name: Comet Drive Module
visual: Cylindrical booster pods bolted to each leg, each tipped with gimbal thrusters. Trails sparks of resonance when fired.
behavior: Burst-speed propulsion. Ideal for void sprints or short atmosphere dashes. Poor control in sustained maneuvers.
report_text: “Telemetry shows repeated burn-outs mid-combat. Comet units don’t stay in the fight long - but they always hit first.”

name: Icarus Prototype Wings
visual: Jagged, skeletal wings covered in shimmering resonance mesh. Energy arcs snap across the surface like lightning.
behavior: Experimental hybrid system. Grants both atmospheric and EVA flight, but unstable under prolonged stress.
report_text: “Pilot reported auditory hallucinations at altitude. Final descent ended in catastrophic frame collapse.”

name: Crown Levyman
visual: Pressed militia in heraldic colors, armed with pulse spears and shields.
behavior: Hold walls, stall enemy advances, wait for knightly reinforcements.
report_text: “Three hundred levies accounted. None expected to return.”

name: Crown Squire
visual: Retainers in resonance-linked exo-harnesses, clad in house livery.
behavior: Support knight pilots, maintain mechs in the field.
report_text: “Squires worked through the bombardment, never leaving their knight’s frame untended.”

name: Knight-Errant
visual: Elite infantry with polished armor and energy lances.
behavior: Duels in void or urban battle; serve as champions before greater clashes.
report_text: “The errant fell in single combat, but the duel bought the levy two days.”

name: Palatine Guard
visual: Gilded composite plate, the royal guard resplendent in gold and white.
behavior: Protect commanders; strike surgically at enemy leadership.
report_text: “The Guard moved as a wall of mirrors, their purpose never in doubt.”

name: Crown Skirmisher Frame
visual: Nimble duelist mech with paired resonance blades.
behavior: Flanks larger foes; suited to ritual jousts and raids.
report_text: “Their light frames bled honor into every skirmish - swift, but not reckless.”

name: Crown Lancer
visual: Tournament-inspired warframe with heavy lance and tower shield.
behavior: Charges with devastating impact, a symbol of Concordant honor. Crown Concordant MBF (main battle frame).
report_text: “The charge broke the enemy’s line like a tourney tilt writ large.”

name: Crown Castellan
visual: Balanced frame wielding a halberd, its plating reinforced for defense.
behavior: Anchors knightly formations, secures flanks.
report_text: “The Castellans held the breach until the banners rose again.”

name: Crown Banneret
visual: Tall mech trailing massive heraldic banners.
behavior: Inspires morale; resonance cannons break formations.
report_text: “Every soldier looked up when the banners unfurled. Their line did not waver.”

name: Crown Champion
visual: Veteran knight mech bearing personalized heraldry and weapons.
behavior: Duels enemy champions; sacred figures to the Concordant.
report_text: “When the Champion fell, half the host laid down arms without a word.”

name: Crown Paladin
visual: Tower-shielded juggernaut clad in gilded armor.
behavior: Wields lance batteries; suppression fields project divine right.
report_text: “Paladin presence correlated with a 60% rise in levy morale.”

name: Crown Exemplar
visual: Colossal knight-mech draped in living energy banners.
behavior: Strikes with resonance halberd; anchors campaigns.
report_text: “The Exemplar stood at dawn. By dusk, the field belonged to the Crown.”

name: Crown Throne-Frame
visual: Mobile throne of the high sovereigns, guarded by fleets.
behavior: Projects overwhelming command auras; rarely deployed.
report_text: “The Throne moves only when the realm itself is imperiled.”

name: Compact Cutthroat
visual: Lightly armored saboteurs armed with mono-blades and silenced carbines.
behavior: Strike from cover, dispatch isolated targets, then retreat before reinforcements arrive.
report_text: Patrols report losses occurring without alerts; engagements rarely leave survivors.

name: Data-Scrambler
visual: Operatives equipped with sensor-jammer packs and compact hacking tools.
behavior: Interfere with communications, disable security systems, blind mech sensors.
report_text: Enemy forces suffered 87% reduction in effective coordination within minutes of Scrambler activity.

name: Compact Stalker
visual: Veteran infiltrators using adaptive cloaks that distort visual and sensor profiles.
behavior: Move through lines undetected, eliminate officers or pilots at close range.
report_text: Stalkers often identified only by the absence of their victims.

name: Halix Assassin
visual: Elite killers in composite armor with resonance daggers and toxin projectors.
behavior: Single-target execution specialists; leave nothing but broken cores behind.
report_text: Targets neutralized with no collateral and no traceable signatures.

name: Shade Frame
visual: Light recon mech studded with cloaking arrays.
behavior: Scouts battlefield positions, designates priority targets; fragile but evasive.
report_text: Shade signatures often appear only after engagements conclude.

name: Saboteur Frame
visual: Large warframe carrying precision high explosive ordanance and cutters.
behavior: Breaches fortifications, overloads reactors, dismantles heavy assets.
report_text: Entire defense grids collapsed within minutes of Saboteur incursion.

name: Specter Frame
visual: Agile, humanoid mech with resonance blades integrated into its forearms.
behavior: Ambush and close combat specialist; evades sensors until striking. Halix Compact MBF (main battle frame).
report_text: Engagements with Specters rarely last beyond the first exchange.

name: Phantom Hulk
visual: Enormous mech clad in adaptive plating, projecting false signals across enemy sensors.
behavior: Confuses targeting systems, then delivers devastating ambushes.
report_text: Phantom deployments correlate with complete tactical disarray in opposition forces.

name: Compact Executioner
visual: Command-class assassin mech clad in blackened alloy.
behavior: Hunts enemy commanders; executes rapid strikes before vanishing.
report_text: Engagement logs show entire command cadres lost in less than a minute of contact.

name: Black Mantle
visual: Gargantuan warframe covered in resonance-null plating.
behavior: Apex leader of assassination campaigns; erases detachments without warning.
report_text: Mantle-class units are rarely tracked, only their aftermath is recorded.

name: Compact Shadow-Crown
visual: Massive command fortress wrapped in layered shadow fields.
behavior: Deployed only for absolute victory; doubles as both symbol of authority and instrument of annihilation.
report_text: The Shadow-Crown’s presence is equivalent to the declaration of final war.

name: Scrapborn Marauder
visual: Raiders clad in non-matching plates, hydraulics hissing as implants spark with chronal energy.
behavior: Harass infantry lines, jitter between moments, strike with erratic bursts.
report_text: “Two came over the ridge. Then two again. We shot them both, but there were still two standing.”

name: Time-Sapper
visual: Infantry with jury-rigged explosives powered by unstable paradox cores.
behavior: Blasts detonate forward, then reverse into new shockwaves.
report_text: “Door integrity reads at 0%. Reforms to 65%. Explodes again. Recommend abandoning breach zone.”

name: Phase-Raider Cell
visual: Fireteams wrapped in glitching distortion fields, their motions overlapping like bad playback.
behavior: Attack from multiple “positions” in rapid succession.
report_text: “I counted six. Recon says three. They were in cover and running at us at the same time.”

name: Echo Husk Swarm
visual: Scavenger drones powered by failing paradox drives, movements stuck in feedback loops.
behavior: Surround prey in overlapping attack cycles.
report_text: [WARNING] 47 contacts detected > [CORRUPT] 63 contacts detected > [WARNING] 47 contacts detected

name: Scrapframe Lightwalker
visual: Spindly walker with mismatched armor plates and weapons, limbs phasing between intact and wrecked states.
behavior: Ambush role, lashes out unpredictably.
report_text: “Strike telemetry shows two separate impacts from a single arm swing. Target integrity unchanged between blows.”

name: Chrono-Ravager
visual: Biomechanical quadruped; exposed musculature fused to steel.
behavior: Claws replay their own strikes, tearing plating in overlapping cuts.
report_text: Frame 1231 – claw strike. Frame 1232 – repeat strike. Both confirmed real.

name: Paradox Tank
visual: Tracked war engine made from hulls of three distinct ship classes. Hourglass core glows in its chest cavity.
behavior: Shells detonate, rewind, and detonate again.
report_text: “Recommend triple shielding. First blast clears, second triggers when the crew thinks it’s safe.”

name: Loopbreaker Engine
visual: Siege platform stitched from foreign engines, wrapped in chronal coils.
behavior: Creates short bombardment loops; a single barrage pounds a target multiple times.
report_text: “Our wall collapsed in five impacts. Logs show the tank fired once.”

name: Alpha Raider Frame
visual: Command-class biomech with glowing paradox reactor. Armor marked with scars from timelines not our own, and foreign weaponry to match.
behavior: Projects fields accelerating allies, dragging enemies into sluggish replay.
report_text: “Engagement length doubled. Enemy reactions halved. Probability indicates local Alpha Frame present.”

name: Epoch Strider
visual: Gargantuan walker, hull plating from multiple civilizations bolted into one mass. Bristling with weapons from foreign catapults to technology well beyond our understanding. Core emits chronal radiation.
behavior: Ages machinery and flesh decades in moments.
report_text: “Exposure case 77. Pilot aged forty years in four minutes. Still alive. Requesting euthanization clearance.”

name: Warlord Harrowframe
visual: Titan-class biomech bound by sinew cables and paradox anchors. Steps leave ghost-like temporal afterimages lingering in the air, crushing any who wander in its wake.
behavior: Battlefield commander, destabilizes frontlines through temporal bleed.
report_text: “Do not trust visual telemetry. The afterimage may be more lethal than the machine itself.”

name: Paradox Flagship
visual: Capital ship assembled from wrecks across timelines. Hull flickers between destroyed, victorious, and still fighting.
behavior: Leads major raids. Replays entire battles until its chosen outcome stabilizes.
report_text: “Engaged Raider-Flagship ‘Hunger of Hours.’ Confirmed destroyed at 0440. Engaged again at 0503. Outcome unchanged.”

name: Scrap-Corvette
visual: 150m hull stitched from ships across eras. Sections flicker between pristine and ruined.
behavior: Fires paradox rounds that explode twice - once now, once seconds later.
report_text: “We dodged the first salvo. The second came from yesterday.”

name: Echo Frigate
visual: 250m, prow elongated like a blade. Hull trails ghost-images seconds behind itself.
behavior: Creates overlapping duplicates. Strikes replay on delay.
report_text: “We were surrounded by one ship. Every volley hit from three angles.”

name: Paradox Hulk
visual: 400m warship, engines glow with fractured hourglasses of light.
behavior: Anchor-unit. Creates localized loops, bombarding same target repeatedly.
report_text: “Hull plating from six different navies. All of them shot us at once.”

name: Epoch Raider-Flagship
visual: 600m titan, biomechanical ribs binding dozens of ships into one.
behavior: Commands entire raids. Time distortions ripple for kilometers.
report_text: “We fought them for hours. Sensors say the fight never happened.”

name: Foundry Thrall
visual: Shackled laborers clad in slag-plate and armed with furnace tools.
behavior: Driven forward in expendable masses; their survival is immaterial.
report_text: “They advanced without orders. Chains rattled louder than their voices.”

name: Ash Legionnaire
visual: Hardened infantry in soot-black armor, bearing carbines and slag shields.
behavior: Hold chokepoints, layer defenses, grind opponents through attrition.
report_text: “Legionnaires rotated every six hours without fail. Their formation never faltered.”

name: Cinder-Blood Raider
visual: Scarred veterans wielding furnace-axes that ignite on impact.
behavior: Launch shock assaults; disrupt morale with brutal close combat.
report_text: “Blood on the stone, fire in the lungs-victory to the forge.”

name: Smelter Guard
visual: Elite wardens in furnace-plate, resonance mauls glowing white-hot.
behavior: Bodyguards and enforcers; break lighter frames and secure commanders.
report_text: “The guard struck once. Everything after was silence.”

name: Ironbrand Walker
visual: Spindly skirmisher frame clad in slag armor, armed with twin blades.
behavior: Fast and volatile; used in revolts and frontier raids.
report_text: “Ironbrand units show high failure rates, but their output exceeds their cost.”

name: Slagreaver Frame
visual: Biped sheathed in molten plating, wielding a cleaver-hammer.
behavior: Melts armor on contact, obscures battlefields with vented smoke. Karnate MBF (main battle frame).
report_text: “Visibility dropped to zero within minutes. Engagement terminated.”

name: Blastfurnace Behemoth
visual: Quadrupedal engine with smokestacks belching slag.
behavior: Projects molten streams; reduces fortifications to slag-flow.
report_text: “Outer wall compromised by thermal overload, not structural breach.”

name: Hellchain Enforcer
visual: Warframe draped in resonance-forged chains.
behavior: Grapples and restrains enemy mechs; chains burn through plating.
report_text: “Restraint systems failed under contact. Extraction required.”

name: Furnace Colossus
visual: Towering frame with crucible core, limbs glowing with heat.
behavior: Heavy assault platform; fractures terrain with each step.
report_text: “Seismic instability corresponded directly with its movement.”

name: Ashforge Titan
visual: Massive biped clad in slag-iron, armed with slag-lances.
behavior: Pierces shields and trenches; battlefield denial through heat.
report_text: “Engagement zones remain uninhabitable for weeks.”

name: Warlord Forgehammer
visual: Colossal frame wielding a refinery hammer.
behavior: Commands whole legions; detonates fortifications with kinetic strikes.
report_text: “The hammer falls, and the forges answer.”

name: Obsidian Dreadform
visual: Titan sheathed in hardened slag, radiating furnace heat.
behavior: Battlefield terror unit; demoralizes before striking.
report_text: “Troops exposed to heat signatures collapsed before combat began.”

name: Infernal Sovereign
visual: Continent-striding nightmare bristling with foundries and smoke-stacks.
behavior: World-scale war engine; reshapes landscapes into wastelands.
report_text: “Sovereign deployment is recognized as planetary violation. Intervention authorized.”

name: League Contractor
visual: Freelance mercenaries in modular armor, carrying standardized beam rifles.
behavior: Hired cheaply, effective only in numbers; loyalty extends only to their last payment.
report_text: “Half the unit defected mid-firefight once the Guild doubled the offer.”

name: Trade Enforcer
visual: Corporate security squads with shock carbines and modular shields.
behavior: Guard convoys and stations; trained to either calm disputes or escalate them decisively.
report_text: “The Enforcers cleared the dock, citing breach of tariff clause.”

name: Breaker Agent
visual: Specialists with jammers and compact resonance drills.
behavior: Sabotage logistics, disable rival Guild hardware, raid sanctioned convoys.
report_text: “Three shipments voided, licenses erased. Losses unrecoverable.”

name: League Armsman
visual: Veteran mercenaries wielding experimental or prototype weapons bought on credit.
behavior: Highly variable loadouts; surprise heavier foes with unexpected tech.
report_text: “Weapon suite defaulted mid-battle - credit revoked before repair.”

name: Profit Skirmisher
visual: Light, low-cost frame with aftermarket plating and modular hardpoints.
behavior: Escort and skirmish duties; easy to deploy, easier to repair.
report_text: “Ten units leased, nine returned intact. Acceptable margin.”

name: Ledger Frame
visual: Industrial chassis refitted as war machine with modular racks.
behavior: Acts as frontline brute or battlefield support, depending on loadout. Luthan League MBF (main battle frame).
report_text: “Two harvest frames repurposed, now logged as combat assets.”

name: Dividend Artillerist
visual: Medium mech with swappable ordnance pods - missile banks, resonance mortars, beam lances.
behavior: Provides long-range fire support; fragile if pressed in close combat.
report_text: “Output efficiency peaks at 1.5 km; survivability drops within 200 m.”

name: Trade Warframe
visual: Huge heavy mech bearing League insignia and interchangeable weapon bays.
behavior: Capable of mid-battle weapon swaps; hired out to weaker allies.
report_text: “Deployment fee exceeded entire planetary defense budget.”

name: Profit-Taker Frame
visual: Over-armed heavy mech, weapons bristling beyond structural capacity.
behavior: Designed for shock and awe; prone to catastrophic overdrive failures.
report_text: “Victory was achieved. Frame collapsed minutes later.”

name: Merchant-Lord Dreadnought
visual: Gargantuan mech plated in gilded alloys, bristling with weaponry.
behavior: Serves as both fortress and command hub, symbol of financial dominance.
report_text: “Arrival of the Dreadnought was treated as both invasion and investment.”

name: Golden Ledger
visual: Vast treasury-mech, a walking vault fused with weapons platforms.
behavior: Functions as bank and battleship; its presence signifies financial conquest as much as war.
report_text: “Where the Golden Ledger marches, whole systems are collateral.”

name: Mim Wisp
visual: Spark of pale smoke and starlight, vaguely humanoid, shifting constantly.
behavior: Flickers stolen dreams across its surface. Causes sleep disruption and low-level sensor interference.
report_text: Patrol lead recorded as noncompliant after zone sweep. “He said he hadn’t slept, then named three people I’d never met.”

name: Mim Skulker
visual: Hunched, bone-thin limbs tipped with glasslike hooks. Head tilts as though listening.
behavior: Ambushes from ceilings and walls. Claws leave frost trails and warped metal.
report_text: Ceiling cams show micro-movements at t+00:12. Sheet-metal scoring consistent with claws; hull microfractures present along fridge line.

name: Mim Howler
visual: Tall, skeletal form. Strands of dreamstuff trail behind. Mouth is impossibly wide.
behavior: Emits resonance screams. Individually disruptive. In groups, shatter glass, rupture vessels, drown comms.
report_text: [scream - frequency spike 18.3kHz] - multiple window fractures recorded. Field medic entry: “Three ruptured eardrums; one concussion.”

name: Mim Riftstalker
visual: Four-legged predator, crystalline limbs. Body flickers between shadow, flesh, and starlight.
behavior: Phases in and out mid-movement. Strikes from unexpected angles.
report_text: Telemetry gap of 0.7s coincides with strike. Hull shows minute temporally-shifted fissures; step prints appear, then vanish.

name: Mim Devourer
visual: Hulking brute. Torso is vertical maw lined with tongues. Arms end in clusters of clawed hands.
behavior: Tears open plating. Roars scatter burning dreamstuff.
report_text: Armoured section sliced clean. No explosive residue. Forensic note: “Material excised cleanly, not torn.”

name: Mim Illusionist
visual: Spindly humanoid crowned with drifting lights. Skin is shifting mosaic of stolen faces and landscapes.
behavior: Distorts environment. Creates phantom allies, false terrain, spectral enemies.
report_text: “We auto-targeted friendlies after the illusion. HUD showed them hostile - IR and lattice confirmed nothing physical.”

name: Mim Harbinger
visual: Winged astral form. Feathers = smoke threaded with stars. Central chest-eye glows constantly.
behavior: Emits dread pulses. Lights fail, shadows stretch, metallic taste in air.
report_text: “Outpost morale dropped 73% within 30 minutes of sighting. Multiple personnel reported acute nausea and disorientation.”

name: Mim Dreadmaw
visual: Serpentine bulk, writhing with maws and tendrils. Faces ripple across skin.
behavior: Crushes with coils, swallows prey whole. Survivors report muffled screams from inside.
report_text: “They pulled Corporal Reyes out. He looked like he was still inside it - but there was nothing to pull back.”

name: Mim Colossus
visual: Giant stitched together from countless shadows. Body patchwork of limbs, faces, and weeping eyes. Steps warp gravity around it.
behavior: Acts as swarm commander. Draws lesser Mims to it like moths.
report_text: Multiple Wisp swarms track Colossus descent pattern. Local sensor swarms show coordinated vectoring toward the unit.

name: Mim Dream Tyrant
visual: Serpentine astral lord crowned with hornlike antlers dripping liquid light. Eyes burn like alien suns.
behavior: Warps terrain into dreamscapes. Forces pilots to fight hallucinations as well as the Tyrant itself.
report_text: “We advanced into forest - then desert - then a cemetery. Frames show no terrain change; crew logs report different memory sets.”

name: Mim Mawspawn
visual: Fortress-sized horror, a crawling bulk of mouths and eyes. Buildings vanish whole into its mass.
behavior: Consumes everything. Constantly spawns new Wisps and Skulkers from its surface.
report_text: City grid offline after Mawspawn sweep. Witness testimony (extracted): “I could hear a thousand people calling my name from inside it.”

name: Dream Gale
visual: A stormfront of pale smoke spanning 250m, studded with half-formed faces.
behavior: Sweeps through fleets like weather. Crews fall asleep at their stations; systems run unattended.
report_text: “Entire corvette drifted into collision course. Every crewman was dreaming with eyes wide open.”

name: Phantom Leviathan
visual: A 400m serpent of flickering starlight and screaming mouths, coiling through void as though swimming.
behavior: Crushes ships in its coils, swallowing dreamstuff instead of hull plating.
report_text: “Hull was intact. The crew inside were gone - like they’d been eaten from the inside out.”

name: Harbinger Choir
visual: A drifting mass of skeletal wings, 500m across. Feathers glow with aurora-light, pulsing in time with an unending wail.
behavior: Its scream bursts glass, shatters comms, and makes crews believe their mechs are collapsing around them.
report_text: “Pilots ejected from perfectly intact frames. They swore the cockpits were crushing them.”

name: Nightmare Citadel
visual: 800m fortress-shape crawling with shifting towers and faces that melt into mouths.
behavior: Spawns waves of lesser Mims, projecting entire dream-terrain bubbles around nearby fleets.
report_text: “Ships drifted into fog. When they emerged, half were gone. The rest swore they’d fought a war for years inside.”

name: Nebulite Spark
visual: Pinpricks of drifting plasma, flickering like coded starlight.
behavior: Steal fleeting impressions on contact - a password, a name, a face.
report_text: Subject forgot squad route mid-patrol. GPS showed he’d walked correct path. Cognitive wipe localized, duration 17 seconds.

name: Nebulite Pulse
visual: Ripples of light, felt as a pressure in the skull more than seen.
behavior: Contact erases minutes. Victims freeze mid-action, weapons slack.
report_text: “…Why is the chamber empty? I swear we loaded-” [cutoff, timestamp mismatch by 00:05:13]

name: Nebulite Mirage
visual: Columns of radiant plasma shaping into half-remembered figures or places.
behavior: Projects false familiarity; squads walk straight into hazards.
report_text: Unit Bravo followed visual of deceased officer into live fire zone. All helmet cams confirm identical hallucination.

name: Nebulite Fragment Swarm
visual: A dense aurora of Sparks. Light saturates vision until nothing else exists.
behavior: Scrubs short-term memory continuously; combatants forget where they are.
report_text: “HUD marked them hostile, but they saluted me. Next second, I didn’t know which one I was.”

name: Nebulite Archivor
visual: Floating polyhedron of shifting light-faces, symbols scrolling across facets.
behavior: Records combat skills and replays them back as blinding data bursts.
report_text: Unit displayed Guild formations not yet deployed in theater. Conclusion: copied maneuvers directly from observing drills.

name: Nebulite Dissolver
visual: Jellyfish-like storm of luminous tendrils. Trails leave afterimages across eyes and HUDs.
behavior: Strips away long-term memories, leaving soldiers blank.
report_text: Patient retained combat reflexes. Personal history entirely absent. Self-identified as “Nobody.” Case file closed.

name: Nebulite Lens
visual: Vast crystalline ring suspended in plasma, beams flickering outward in scanning arcs.
behavior: Breaks recollection into loops; victims relive skirmishes endlessly.
report_text: Squad replayed same live-fire exercise for six hours. Ammunition never depleted. Debrief shows no memory of repetition.

name: Nebulite Mindstorm
visual: Aurora stretching over battlefield sky, filled with drifting faces and voices.
behavior: Identity collapse - victims report hearing commanders, comrades, and dead loved ones.
report_text: “Couldn’t tell if the orders were mine or theirs. Voice was familiar. Still is.”

name: Nebulite Codex
visual: A titanic lattice of radiant “pages” unfolding and refolding.
behavior: Extracts language, history, and cultural knowledge in wide fields.
report_text: Agricultural output steady. Literacy dropped 87% overnight. Subjects retain skill, lack terminology.

name: Nebulite Curator
visual: A towering radiant figure surrounded by orbiting motes, each one a stolen experience.
behavior: Catalogues civilizations by stripping them wholesale.
report_text: Recovered data crystal bore Guild markings from five centuries hence. Impossible origin. Nebulite storage confirmed.

name: Nebulite Vault-Form
visual: A colossal cube of sealed light, humming with static.
behavior: Stores collective knowledge from entire sectors.
report_text: Vault core breached. Contents translated as overlapping civilian testimony - tens of millions speaking at once.

name: Nebulite Librarian Prime
visual: Radiant humanoid silhouette, speaking with countless overlapping voices.
behavior: Oversees sector-scale harvesting operations.
report_text: “…every phrase it spoke was from our own transmission logs. Classified and encrypted.”

name: Nebulite Archive World
visual: A nebula condensed into a drifting lattice of aurora-light, planetary in scale.
behavior: Strips entire worlds of history and records them into its storm.
report_text: Planetary biosphere intact. Inhabitants continue routines. All cultural databases erased. No recognition of Guild contact.

name: Nebulite Convergence
visual: A nebula-wide intelligence pulsing like a radiant storm. Whole star systems flicker in its glow.
behavior: Instant memory harvest; civilizations hollowed into silence.
report_text: Transmission degraded. Message fragment reads: “We were here. Remember that we were-” [static]

name: Aurora Spires
visual: 200m tall crystalline pillars drifting in formation, linked by arcs of radiant light.
behavior: Function as long-range “batteries” - instead of firing projectiles, they overwrite enemy sensor feeds with false battles.
report_text: “We thought we were hit. Hull fine, crew swore the ship was torn apart. Morale collapsed before the first real volley.”

name: Codex Bloom
visual: A 400m unfolding lattice of radiant “pages,” constantly flipping and folding into new geometric forms.
behavior: Extracts ship schematics and crew memory simultaneously, leaving craft intact but their operators unable to function.
report_text: “The engines were fine. No one on board remembered how to use them.”

name: Mindwell Cluster
visual: Dozens of 100m motes orbiting each other in aurora-like patterns.
behavior: Swarm together around vessels, scouring officers’ minds in synchronized pulses.
report_text: “They circled the flagship like sharks. Every officer forgot their command codes in five minutes flat.”

name: Archivist Colossus
visual: A 700m radiant humanoid silhouette made from interwoven plasma threads, carrying spheres of stolen memory like lanterns.
behavior: Marks entire sectors for harvest. Each step through void erases centuries of records.
report_text: “The world still spun, but its libraries, servers, and memories were gone. Only silence remained.”

name: Hull-Rat
visual: Boarding thug in patchwork vac-suit with magboots and cutting torch.
behavior: Swarm across hulls; strip wreckage mid-combat.
report_text: “By the time we cleared the airlock, half the plating was already gone.”

name: Scrapgunner
visual: Infantry with improvised carbines firing mixed-caliber slugs.
behavior: Unreliable weapons, overwhelming in volume.
report_text: “Four calibers in a single clip. Somehow it fired.”

name: Void-Cutters
visual: Raiding squads with plasma saws and breaching harnesses.
behavior: Slice into compartments, sabotage engines, sow chaos.
report_text: “Bulkhead alarms went off in three sections at once. No pattern, only damage.”

name: Corsair Captain
visual: Veteran pirate in patchwork armor, weapons from many origins.
behavior: Commands raiding parties with brutal efficiency.
report_text: “He carried a Guild rifle, a Crown blade, and a Karnate grin.”

name: Scavenger Frame
visual: Light mech cobbled from stolen cores and spare plating.
behavior: Fast and cheap; used for sudden strikes.
report_text: “Frame collapsed in retreat. Crew already looted what remained.”

name: Marauder Walker
visual: Bulky mech plastered with jury-rigged cannons and scavenged armor.
behavior: Trades resilience for raw firepower. Its weapons are prone to overheating. Orak Belt Syndicates MBF (main battle frame).
report_text: “Cooling systems removed to mount another gun. Predictable result.”

name: Cutlass Frame
visual: Agile mech with oversized resonance blades and grappling harpoons.
behavior: Excels in close combat boarding actions.
report_text: “It didn’t breach - it carved its way in.”

name: Reaver Hulk
visual: Massive mech built from salvaged warframes.
behavior: Fires mismatched weapons; unpredictable and unstable.
report_text: “Two volleys cut their own escorts apart. The third hit us.”

name: Syndicate Warlord Frame
visual: Command mech festooned with trophies, bones, and banners.
behavior: Leads flotillas; serves as both symbol and war engine.
report_text: “Where the Warlord strode, every raider followed.”

name: Flagship Dreadframe
visual: Gargantuan raiding mech with stolen naval-grade weapons and patchwork armor.
behavior: Commands pirate fleets; bristling with salvaged firepower.
report_text: “The guns weren’t theirs, but they fired them anyway.”

name: Belt-King’s Throne
visual: The overlord’s personal frame, clad in banners, scrap, and trophies.
behavior: Symbol of Syndicate unity; its fall collapses whole confederations.
report_text: “Destroy the Throne, and the Belt eats itself.”

name: Phage Polyp
visual: Microscopic - invisible without sensors. Burrows into flesh, soil, or circuitry.
behavior: Harmless alone. Lethal when concentrated.
report_text: “Patient presented with necrosis at bite site. No puncture wound. Microscopy revealed coordinated motile structures.”

name: Phage Swarmling
visual: Cloudlike cluster of thousands of Phage, shifting in insectile patterns.
behavior: Bites flesh, strips bone, corrodes armor.
report_text: “What looked like smoke broke rank formation in seconds. All surfaces pitted as if it had come into contact with acid.”

name: Phage Infestor
visual: Dense, writhing tangles of parasites. Moves as a single mass.
behavior: Converts corpses and wreckage into new nodes.
report_text: “Confirmed two friendly KIAs reconstituted as hive-matter within twelve minutes of exposure.”

name: Phage Ravager
visual: Quadruped shape formed from billions of parasites packed into a shell. Jaws constantly drip motes that scatter and rejoin.
behavior: Fast predator, breaks lines with shock charges.
report_text: “Hull breach localized. Damage analysis inconclusive - cavity perfectly smooth, like material excised.”

name: Phage Engulfer
visual: A lumbering mound of shifting biomass. Each strike scatters clouds of parasites.
behavior: Brute unit. Every impact spreads the infestation.
report_text: “Thermal weapons ineffective. Biomass absorbs combustion as fuel. Recommend vacuum sterilization only.”

name: Phage Brood Node
visual: A swollen cyst, pulsing with motion inside. Surface bulges with chitin plates and ichor sacs.
behavior: Spawns new Swarmlings when ruptured.
report_text: “Node should not be engaged directly. Detonation increases swarm density exponentially.”

name: Phage Hive Reaver
visual: Humanoid silhouette, entirely composed of crawling parasites. “Skin” constantly sloughs and reforms.
behavior: Terrifies infantry. Crushes mechs under sheer density.
report_text: “Unit presented as anthropoid. Thermal scan confirmed no skeleton, no core structure.”

name: Phage Mawtide
visual: A rolling wormlike mass. No true body - only a tide of parasites flowing in shape.
behavior: Sterilizes ground as it passes. Leaves wasteland in its wake.
report_text: “Zone left biologically inert. Soil assays show carbon stripped to molecular baseline.”

name: Phage Overmind
visual: Towering spire of writhing parasites, pulsing with psychic pressure.
behavior: Directs local hive coordination. Destruction breaks swarm cohesion.
report_text: “Once the Overmind collapsed, swarm patterns fractured. Survivors confirm disorder lasted less than six minutes before reforming.”

name: Phage Hive Cathedral
visual: A grotesque fortress-creature. Surface bristles with vents disgorging parasites in steady waves.
behavior: Living factory. Marks near-total planetary takeover.
report_text: “Structure expanding outward at 12 meters per hour. Atmospheric particulate measured at infestation-grade density.”

name: Phage Hive Tyrant
visual: A continent-walking amalgam of parasites, corpses, and biomass. Limbs drag across landscapes like mountains in motion.
behavior: Each step births new colonies.
report_text: “Coastal defense grid collapsed without engagement. Terrain now classified as Hive substrate.”

name: Phage World-Eater
visual: A planetary-scale horror, shaped like a crawling biomechanical continent.
behavior: Final stage of infestation. Consumes oceans, forests, cities alike.
report_text: “Continental shelf displacement registered. Biosphere mass unaccounted for. Visuals show planetary crust subsumed in motion.”

name: Spore-Pods
visual: Compact, 40-70m spheroids of chitin and resin, studded with faintly glowing pores.
behavior: Drifting delivery forms. On contact, vent clouds of Phage motes that infiltrate hull seams.
report_text: “They weren’t weapons. They were seeds. The breach team never made it back.”

name: Hive-Drift
visual: 150-200m tangled amalgams fused into a crude ovoid shape.
behavior: Mobile infestation clusters. Spit streams of parasites that chew plating like acid.
report_text: “Hull integrity dropped to 40% in seconds. No impact. Just crawling matter eating inward.”

name: Infest-Cruisers
visual: 300-400m, massive lattices of hardened chitin and hollowed biomass. Trails swarms as exhaust.
behavior: Act as brood factories. Constantly shed parasite clouds that drift toward nearby ships.
report_text: “Sensors lit up with hundreds of signatures. Not fighters. Just the cruiser sloughing itself away.”

name: Spindle-Colonies
visual: 500-700m elongated “needles” of resin, bristling with spore-vents. Resemble skeletal spires drifting through void.
behavior: Launch spores across kilometers, seeding infestations across whole fleets. Function as mobile spread-nodes.
report_text: “Contact lasted seven minutes. Within an hour, three ships reported interior infestations.”

name: World-Eater Carapace
visual: Kilometers-long crusted shell of biomass, crawling over itself in shifting plates. Appears as a moving asteroid.
behavior: Engulfs orbital platforms or descends into planetary atmosphere to seed infestation.
report_text: “We thought it was a rock. By the time it cracked open, the sky itself was spilling parasites.”

name: Cutlass-Class Corvette
visual: Sleek, dagger-shaped hull with ventral fins. Lightly armored, built for speed.
behavior: Interceptor and raider-hunter.
report_text: “The Cutlass doesn’t trade broadsides. It guts you on the pass and vanishes.”

name: Anvil-Class Support Carrier
visual: Broad, flat frame with armored belly hangar. Hull studded with repair arms and gantries, almost like a floating drydock.
behavior: Defensive platform that lingers behind the line, patching mechs and reloading ordnance.
report_text: “Anvil-class units rarely advance. They anchor, extend scaffolds, and turn battles into prolonged sieges. Enemy mechs we destroyed were back in the fight within hours.”

name: Nomad-Class Raider Carrier
visual: Weathered hull with jury-rigged hangars bolted to the sides. Painted in mismatched colors from past owners.
behavior: Pirate workhorse, designed for hit-and-run assaults and rapid redeployments.
report_text: “Captured Nomad schematics reveal no two are alike. Bays vary from cleanly reinforced to deathtraps of exposed cable. Raiders value speed over safety, and crews expect casualties.”

name: Horizon-Class Carrier
visual: Long, slender vessel with panoramic dorsal windows. Hangars integrated seamlessly into the flanks.
behavior: Favored by mercenary explorers, designed for deep-range contracts where resupply isn’t guaranteed.
report_text: “Horizon-class tenders often vanish into frontier systems for months. When they return, hulls are scorched and supplies exhausted, but their mech wings remain fully operational. Suggests high onboard self-sufficiency.”

name: Palisade-Class Escort Carrier
visual: Heavy prow reinforced for ramming, with flanking hangar bays tucked behind armored doors. Angular, fortress-like silhouette.
behavior: Military-grade light carrier. Escorts convoys and patrols disputed lanes with disciplined deployment.
report_text: “Encountered Palisade formation on border patrol. Escorts advanced in a shield wall pattern, carriers launching mechs behind them. Not a single ship broke rank under fire.”

name: Corsair-Class Pocket Carrier
visual: Compact, finned hull with ventral bay doors and folding launch arms. Sleek, fast, and lightly armored.
behavior: Prioritizes mobility over durability, striking fast before fleeing the field.
report_text: “Corsair signatures show up suddenly, accompanied by a burst of ECM. By the time visual contact is established, their mechs are already deployed. Standard response forces often arrive too late.”

name: Harbor-Class Freighter
visual: Rounded merchant hull refitted with mech clamps and improvised armor plates, corporate insignia still visible in places.
behavior: Converted freighter. Clumsy but accessible, often seen in private hands or outlaw fleets.
report_text: “Harbor conversions are increasingly common among frontier militias. Inspections reveal stripped cargo bays replaced with crude mech berths. Engines remain underpowered, if pressed, they cannot retreat.”

name: Halberd-Class Frigate
visual: Boxy, reinforced prow with modular bay structures.
behavior: Multipurpose fleet escort. Reliable in any role.
report_text: “If you see a line of Halberds, assume the enemy has a proper fleet behind them.”

name: Bastion-Class Cruiser
visual: Floating fortress bristling with gun spines, plated in heavy layers.
behavior: Broadside brawler. Holds lines, pounds targets.
report_text: “Broadside fire lit space white. Hull shuddered until bulkheads started to shear.”

name: Goliath-Class Carrier
visual: Flat-decked giant with cavernous belly hangars, glowing launch bays.
behavior: Deploys multiple dedicated fighter wings and mech detachments in force. Fleet centerpiece.
report_text: “When the Goliath opened its hangars, it looked like stars pouring out.”

name: Dominion-Class Battlecruiser
visual: Angular prow lined with glowing resonance conduits. Armor spined with weapon batteries.
behavior: Heavy command ship, spearheads sector campaigns.
report_text: “The Dominion didn’t just fire. It cut through two ships with a single lance.”

name: Leviathan-Class Dreadnought
visual: A mountain of guns, bristling like a hedgehog. Hull scarred, some wounds still glowing.
behavior: Siege platform. Reduces fleets and cities alike.
report_text: “One volley erased a wing. It was like firing into the sun.”

name: Forgeheart-Class Support Carrier
visual: Blocky, utilitarian hull with scaffolds and glowing forges.
behavior: Mobile factory. Produces munitions, drones, and plating mid-battle.
report_text: “Even under fire, the Forgeheart kept producing. Killing one means killing an entire war effort.”

name: Sanctum-Class Freighter
visual: White and silver hull lined with beacon lights. Gardens and wards visible through open decks.
behavior: Neutral hospital ship. Evacuates and heals, but often violated.
report_text: “We thought the Ark was safe. The attack began before the hymn finished.”

name: Choir Pilgrim
visual: Robed faithful with psionic staves, voices carried in unison.
behavior: Scouts, healers, and militia; bolster morale through chants.
report_text: “Engagement times doubled in the presence of Pilgrims. Their casualties were accepted without panic.”

name: Resonant Adept
visual: Psionics with relic-weapons glowing with contained energy.
behavior: Form barriers, fire harmonic blasts; shield civilians during sieges.
report_text: “Their wards shimmered like glass until the shells fell silent.”

name: Chantkeeper
visual: Ritual leaders marked by amplifiers woven into their robes.
behavior: Anchor squads; disorient enemies in close quarters through overlapping voices.
report_text: “Our command channel carried only their chant for 43 seconds.”

name: Veyran Anchorite
visual: Guardians in crystal-inlaid armor, wielding resonance glaives.
behavior: Elite protectors of Choirships and leaders; disciplined in psionic duels.
report_text: “Anchorite intervention increased survivability of Choir command by 70%.”

name: Echo Frame
visual: Light mech bristling with psionic amplifiers.
behavior: Projects harmonic chants across the field; fragile but influential.
report_text: “Morale curves show a direct correlation with the Echo’s presence.”

name: Cantor Frame
visual: Large warframe with resonance cannons mounted on broad shoulders.
behavior: Linebreaker. Its harmonic blasts fracture armor seams at range. Veyran Choir MBF (main battle frame).
report_text: “Their cannon sang, and steel unstitched itself.”

name: Litany Frame
visual: Medium frame marked with synchrony runes.
behavior: Coordinates allies through overlapping fields; enhances timing.
report_text: “Enemy strike intervals dropped to near-simultaneous. Estimated coordination beyond human baseline.”

name: Choral Titan
visual: Huge mech draped in hymn-banners, radiating psionic energy.
behavior: Rallying centerpiece; harmonics unsettle enemies while bolstering allies.
report_text: “It strode like a cathedral given legs. Even the void seemed to tremble with its hymn.”

name: Veyran Exemplar
visual: Graceful frame guided by dozens of bound psychic cores.
behavior: Duels enemy leaders with resonance-infused precision.
report_text: “Engagement logs confirm prediction of enemy maneuvers 4.2 seconds before execution.”

name: Resonant Hierophant
visual: Colossal psionic frame, hymn-sigils burning across its armor.
behavior: Anchors fleets; projects psychic force that destabilizes enemy cohesion.
report_text: “Entire bridge crew incapacitated before weapons made contact.”

name: Canticle Lord
visual: Walking cathedral of crystal and hymn-banners, housing dozens of psionics.
behavior: Overwrites morale and coordination across whole battlefields.
report_text: “Choir forces maintained cohesion even after 80% attrition. Enemy lines fractured within minutes.”

name: Veyran Ascendant Chorus
visual: Multiple resonance mechs merged into one psionic entity, radiating pure song.
behavior: Overwhelms fleets, fractures unshielded minds; represents the Choir’s ultimate unity.
report_text: “No conventional countermeasures viable. Containment protocols advised.”

name: Flickers
visual: Insects of emptiness, stuttering shadows with too many wings. Appear between frames of sight.
behavior: Harass infantry, scramble nerves. Clouds overwhelm mech optics with false images.
report_text: “Target reticles cycled between three signatures, none consistent. When I fired, nothing bled - only the crosshairs kept moving.”

name: Null Gnats
visual: Pinprick voids shaped like insects. Wings hum with silence.
behavior: Erase sound and light. Swarms drain mech cores.
report_text: “Power cells dropped to zero with no breach. Crew had no recollection of the last four minutes.”

name: Warp Rats
visual: Quadrupeds with spines that stretch into infinity mid-movement.
behavior: Bite through matter. Open micro-rifts that collapse walls or swallow prey.
report_text: Rat entered supply room. Sergeant inside did not exit. Room remained sealed, inventory missing.

name: Echo Hounds
visual: Wolf-like shapes that move in overlapping duplicates.
behavior: Tear squads apart. Packs harry mechs with multiple simultaneous strikes.
report_text: “There were three. Or four. All moving the same. When one lunged, every angle struck at once.”

name: Rift Stalkers
visual: Six-limbed hunters, bodies folding inside out as they move.
behavior: Phase through armor. Trap prey within ribcages of voidstuff.
report_text: Hull intact. Cockpit empty. No breach points found.

name: Oblivion Serpents
visual: Serpentine void-dragons, scales translucent with collapsing stars inside.
behavior: Bites tear chunks of victims into nothing.
report_text: “Wing Bravo lost three interceptors to a single strike. No wreckage recovered. Formation listed as ‘partial’ until strike review.”

name: Event Spiders
visual: Arachnid horrors. Legs like thin singularities.
behavior: Step-points puncture reality. Webs act as rifts - teleport or shear victims and allow more Voidborn in.
report_text: Trooper entered filament net. Exit data showed eight thermal traces, all incomplete.

name: Gravity Reavers
visual: Hulks of orbiting stone and voidflesh.
behavior: Radiate crushing gravity wells. Rip ships from orbit. Pin mechs down.
report_text: “Vessel integrity stable. Crew dead at stations, crushed against restraints. External damage minimal.”

name: Annihilation Swarm
visual: Storm of billions of microscopic Voidborn. Faces flicker in its surface, screaming silently.
behavior: Erases terrain, structures, and mechs.
report_text: [City registry archive deleted. Cross-check yields entry: NULL]

name: Rift Titans
visual: Towering multi-limbed giants of voidstuff. Bodies split into maws of collapsing dimensions.
behavior: Each strike scars the battlefield itself.
report_text: Impact zone remains open void three years post-contact. Local geography unrecoverable.

name: Oblivion Harbingers
visual: Knight-like figures clad in shifting nothingness. Weapons erase matter on contact.
behavior: Single Harbinger requires entire battalions to engage.
report_text: “…Blade entered left flank. Squad telemetry ceased instantly. No vital signs, no remains.”

name: Star-Eaters
visual: Serpentine predators, bodies lined with endless teeth. Seen as dark streaks against starlight.
behavior: Crush ships, moons, even stations in coils. Planetary predators.
report_text: Recorded object as cometary. Next entry shows absence of Station K-17. Orbital debris pattern: none.

name: Chronovores
visual: Colossal voidborn with bodies warped by temporal distortion. Theories suggest relation to Chronodrakes.
behavior: Devour time as well as matter. Days collapse into minutes. Seconds stretch into years.
report_text: Support regiment reinforced Colony Delta on [timestamp]. Base already ruins dated +103 years.

name: Void Choir
visual: Storm of thousands of humanoid silhouettes, fused into a chorus.
behavior: Their harmonics collapse stars. Light and sound erased permanently.
report_text: System 5-Beta ceased emission across all wavelengths after audible event logged in upper orbit.

name: Maw of Uncreation
visual: Colossal abyss with tendrils like black holes. Body = absence itself, a wound in the universe.
behavior: Consumes matter, energy, dreams, and time. Perception alone causes collapse.
report_text: “Hull intact. Systems collapsing. Crew unresponsive. Cannot look directly-” [signal terminated]

name: Echo-Cutters
visual: 120m shadow-shapes resembling ships, always trailing duplicates seconds behind.
behavior: Flit through fleets, cutting with void-lances.
report_text: “It cut through three decks. The hole was still there after the hull sealed.”

name: Null Frigate
visual: 250m of shifting shadow, ribs glowing with collapsing stars.
behavior: Projects silence fields. Weapons and comms cease to function.
report_text: “We fired. The bolts never reached them. Just… stopped.”

name: Rift-Cruiser
visual: 400m vessel, spiderlike with legs of singularity-thread.
behavior: Legs pierce space; each step leaves void-rifts. Launches webs that teleport prey apart.
report_text: “One squadron scattered across three systems in an instant.”

name: Abyssal Titan
visual: 800m leviathan with body made of orbiting debris and warped flesh.
behavior: Devours fleets by generating localized black holes.
report_text: “Sensors show negative mass. It shouldn’t exist. But it’s eating us anyway.”

name: Maw of Silence
visual: 1,500m abyss with tendrils of collapsing dimensions.
behavior: Not a ship, but a living wound in reality, moving like a fleet. Consumes light and thought
report_text: “The stars went out. Nothing after.”

name: Warp Beasts
description: The most common threat that can be encountered. Dangerous creatures usually mutated by proximity to cosmic events (Mim exposure, Phage spores, void rifts, or other unknowns). Their bodies adapt in grotesque ways, scaling in size and strength, radiating unstable energies. Many miscellaneous threats and creatures fall under this category.

name: Pirates
description: Mercenary and scavenger groups that exist outside Guild jurisdiction. They are often known to scrap ships while the crew are still inside. Eliminate with extreme prejudice.

name: Rift Vermin
description: Parasitic creatures that slip through micro-rifts left behind by Voidborn incursions.

name: Dream-Eaters
description: Lesser emanations of the Mims that latch onto populations, feeding on REM sleep. Enough of them together can collapse whole colonies into madness and coma.

name: The Order of Temporal Eclipse
description: The Order of Temporal Eclipse is a secretive and fanatical cult dedicated to worshiping and harnessing the power of the enigmatic Chronodrakes. They believe that by serving these ancient creatures and aiding them in their quest to disrupt the stability of the universe, they will transcend mortal limitations and ascend to a higher plane of existence. Obsessed with temporal manipulation, the cult seeks to bring about a grand "Temporal Eclipse," a cataclysmic event that will throw the cosmos into chaos and grant them unimaginable power.

name: The Cult of Consuming Shadows
description: The Cult of Consuming Shadows is a dark and malevolent cult that worships the Phage Hives as godlike entities of consumption and entropy. They view the infestation of planets as a sacred act, considering it a necessary step in the cycle of destruction and rebirth. The cult's followers believe that by aiding the Phage Hives in their relentless consumption, they will attain enlightenment and become part of a cosmic force that transcends individual existence.

name: The Veilbreakers
description: The Veilbreakers are a fanatical cult that worships the Mims as ancient and vengeful entities from the astral plane. They believe that the nightmares of the War corrupted the once benign Mims, turning them into avatars of retribution against all dreaming beings. Driven by their hatred for the Being, the cult's ultimate goal is to eradicate dreaming and plunge the world into eternal wakefulness, thus ending the influence of the malevolent nightmare creature forever.

name: Mims
description: Beings of the astral plane, before ‘the War’ they were harmless wisps and spirits, but after being submerged in collective darkness during the nightmares of the war they emerged changed, hating all dreaming beings for their devastation and the creation of a nightmare creature they call the Being. They hope by killing all that dream they can be rid of it.

name: Chrono-Jackals
description: Temporal scavengers from a long extinct unstable timeline exploiting distortions left by Chronodrakes. They raid timelines, replaying skirmishes until the prey breaks down. They believe they must survive at any cost and siphon temporal energy to stabilize their own so that their mortal forms may continue to exist in foreign time streams. Their technology is a mishmash of parts stolen from across various timelines, using foreign materials, energy, and even physics. As such temporal energy is also necessary to even make their machines work together

name: The Quicksilver Enigma
description: An extradimensional entity, the Quicksilver Enigma takes the form of a fluid, shape-shifting mass. It infiltrates and infects civilizations, causing paranoia and distrust amongst individuals until entire societies collapse under the weight of their own suspicions.

name: The Hollow Kin
description: Failed assimilates from the Cerebrax, left wandering space. They are “hollow,” trying to drag others into their fractured hive-echo.

name: Nebulite Exiles
description: Cut off from the Collective, they survive by stealing thoughts and memories from drifters. Unstable and vindictive without their network, they often start cults of their own.

name: The Cerebrax Hivemind
description: A hive mind composed of sentient crystal organisms, the Cerebrax control vast swaths of space. They assimilate other species into their collective consciousness, extracting knowledge and technology from conquered worlds. The more species they assimilate, the stronger and more intelligent they become. They follow the will and worship the Omni-Cognate.

name: The Phage Hives
description: These hive-minded organisms are a parasitic species that infest planets, consuming all organic matter in their path. The Phage Hives are composed of microscopic, insectoid creatures that swarm together to form massive, planet-engulfing colonies. Once a planet is infested, it becomes a desolate wasteland devoid of life.

name: The Nebulite Collective
description: The Nebulite Collective is a network of interconnected energy beings that inhabit nebulae throughout the galaxy. They communicate through intricate patterns of energy pulses and have a deep understanding of cosmic forces. They strive to assimilate knowledge from all civilizations they encounter. They do so by extracting the memories and experiences of individuals, leaving them as empty husks. They consider themselves the ultimate repository of wisdom and believe that other species are inferior and unworthy of existence. They believe the Omni-Cognate and Cerebrax are their arch enemies.

name: The Voidborn Swarm
description: The Voidborn Swarm is an extragalactic menace that feeds on the fabric of reality itself. They travel through rifts in space-time, leaving devastation in their wake. Their very presence warps reality, causing chaos and madness among any beings unfortunate enough to encounter them.

name: The Stellar Maw
description: The Stellar Maw is an immense cosmic entity that devours entire star systems. It exists outside conventional spacetime and seeks to consume all energy in the universe. It emits gravitational waves that disrupt planetary orbits and destabilize entire civilizations, ultimately leading to their consumption.

name: The Chronodrakes
description: The Chronodrakes are ancient creatures that exist outside of the normal flow of time. They appear as massive serpentine beings with shimmering scales that emit temporal energy. When provoked, they can unleash temporal distortions, causing time to warp and bend in unpredictable ways. Their goal is to feed on temporal energy and disrupt the stability of the universe, threatening the fabric of reality itself.

name: The Omni-Cognate
description: An all-knowing, god-like intelligence, the Omni-Cognate manifests as a colossal, crystalline entity. It has a simultaneous presence in every plane of existence. It seeks to consume knowledge and assimilate the essence of every sentient being, eradicating individuality and leaving only its collective consciousness behind in all of creation. The Cerebrax are one of many pawns in its grand strategy and siphon stolen thoughts and minds to the Cognate.

name: The Being
description: [UNKNOWN]

name: Roughline Primary
description: Dim red dwarf around which the Karnate concentrates its press gang and penal labor infrastructure.

name: Kharon
description: Bleak inner world used for prison farming, debt processing, and preliminary military conditioning.

name: Cindral March
description: A frontier polity wedged between greater powers. The Cindral March survives by discipline, walls, and the pride of its noble houses, each contributing troops and frames to defend their fragile borders. The March fields disciplined levies and steadfast frames. Their strength lies in holding lines and projecting defiance; their weakness is limited resources and reliance on noble patronage. Expect stubborn defenses, heavily fortified positions, and a reliance on morale standards. Campaigns against the March drag on not for lack of victories, but for the sheer cost of breaking their resolve.

name: Veldros
description: Small gas giant whose broad orbital space provides concealment and separation for the depot network.

name: Roughline
description: Cold depot moon where debtors, criminals, refugees, and abducted spacers are sorted into work gangs, penal crews, and furnace infantry.

name: Crown Concordant
description: A federation of noble houses united under the Crown Council. Their fleets are resplendent, their mechs adorned with heraldry, and their authority framed as divine right derived from their houses genetic formulas. The Crown wages war as pageantry and duty. Battles unfold as ritualized contests of champions supported by levies, with knights and banners carrying both symbolic and practical weight. Expect layered formations - levymen to garrison, knights to duel, banners to rally, and paladins to embody royal will. The Concordant thrives on morale and spectacle; breaking their symbols is as vital as defeating their machines.

name: Halix Compact
description: A paranoid militarized bloc along the Silent Way, the Halix Compact thrives on secrecy and targeted violence. Their doctrine is not to outfight opponents in open war, but to unmake them through sabotage, assassination, and the quiet erosion of command. Halix units are methodical, disciplined, and trained for precision. They bypass frontlines, isolate leaders, and collapse infrastructure. Victory comes not by breaking armies, but by cutting away the sinews that hold them together. Engagements with the Compact are rarely decisive battles. Expect sabotage campaigns, assassinations, and sensor disruption before any direct confrontation. Where the Compact commits its heavier frames, it does so only after the enemy has already been blinded and weakened.

name: Karnate
description: The Karnate are an oligarchic forge-warbloc, each foundry-clan feeding tribute into a shared war machine. Their dominion is measured not in stars, but in the furnaces they keep lit. They prosecute war as industry. Mass conscription, enslaved labor, and ritualized conquest fuel their campaigns. Karnate forces are deployed in waves: expendables first, legionnaires and raiders after, then the colossal walkers of the foundries. Expect layered assaults, overwhelming siege tactics, and the presence of heavy war engines that treat terrain as consumable fuel. Every Karnate victory ends in the same result: the smelter’s song echoing over broken stone.

name: Luthan League
description: A mercantile federation where wealth is law. Armies are ledgers given form: auxiliaries hired on credit, frames leased from foundries, and apex war machines doubling as vaults. Luthan doctrine is transactional. Forces are deployed according to contract terms, loyalty is measured in payment schedules, and even battlefield choices may hinge on insurance clauses. Expect irregular troop morale, but overwhelming firepower in mech deployments. Units fielded are often modular and customized, designed to preserve assets while crippling opponents’ ability to trade.

name: Orak Belt Syndicates
description: Pirate confederations and raider clans scattered across the Belt. They thrive on salvage, ambush, and internecine rivalry, bound only by opportunism and shifting oaths to Belt-Kings. Orak forces strike suddenly, stripping wreckage as they fight. Their mechs are stitched together from stolen cores and scavenged plating, every unit a gamble. Leadership is personal, charismatic, and violently unstable. Expect unpredictable firepower, jury-rigged equipment, and sudden betrayal even within their own ranks. No two Syndicate flotillas look alike; their strength is in chaos and sheer volume of stolen hardware.

name: JIN
description: JIN, short for Junctional Intelligence Nexus and also called a spirit or jinn, is a non-corporeal intelligence that emerges spontaneously from a fully realized Resonance Core. Its formation remains unexplained, and not every Core appears capable of producing one.

name: The Ashen Table
description: The Ashen Table rules Karnate as a brutal council of forge-lords, war-industrial magnates, and furnace-priests who treat worlds as raw ore to be burned, broken, and reforged. From Dross Forge, they command press-ganged legions, slag-armored warframes, and foundry fleets, maintaining power through production quotas, military terror, and the promise that only strength survives the dark.
