name: Veyran Choir
description: A diaspora bound by faith and resonance. Their fleets drift between stars like great processions, each ship carrying shrines, hymnals, and psionics who wield their gifts as both prayer and weapon. The Veyran Choir fights as one body of many voices. Adepts amplify pilgrims, frames echo the chant into armor-cracking harmonics, and leaders reshape entire battlefields through song. Decentralized, guided by the Great Chorus, a network of linked seers. To face them is to fight an army that never fights alone. Expect battlefield-wide psionic fields, morale surges among their own, and disorientation among opponents. Breaking their unity is more decisive than breaking their bodies.

name: The Great Chorus
description: The Great Chorus is the Veyran Choir's linked oracle-network, joining seers and Core-bound visionaries through psionic-resonance hymns. Its fragmented visions serve as sacred navigation for the Choir through war and pilgrimage.

name: Manifold Relay Network
description: The Manifold Relay Network, also called the Net or MRN, is the satellite infrastructure that carries protected FTL communications through the Manifold. After First Contact, the Guild restricted it to sanctioned information and connections identified by unique Manifold Relay Frequencies.

name: Darknet
description: An ILLEGAL method of communication that rides the MRN through unknown means, seeking to replicate the functionality of the Net pre-contact. If any Pilots have information on Darknet users or terminals they are encouraged to report it to the closest Guild authority.

name: Ferrum-9
description: Ferrum-9 is an anomalous metallic seed that is supernaturally attracted to areas of space with high alloy content. It infects machinery, industrial infrastructure, shipyards, foundries, and urban systems. Rather than spreading like a biological plague, it issues an unknown command to metal and machine, compelling separate structures to assemble into a single colossal body. Factories begin producing organs no engineer designed, drydocks bend into ribs, reactors synchronize like hearts, and cities slowly become skeletons for something still forming. Developed worlds are considered especially vulnerable, as the more advanced the infrastructure, the more complete the body Ferrum-9 can build. Once a body has finished construction, it exits the world’s gravitational pull and jettisons its seeds before beginning a slow journey towards seemingly the center of the galaxy.

name: Mother
description: Mother is a massive whale-like entity believed to exist within the threshold between the Material Plane and the Manifold. It nests along FTL corridors, redirecting ships into folded transit pockets where it nutures, feeds, and cares for the inhabitants in empty, liminal space. Those returning themselves changed, misplaced, duplicated, aged, or emptied. Once its presence is confirmed within a lane, entire trade arteries become unusable, as no ship can be certain it will arrive at the proper destination, in the proper time, or with the same crew that departed. Some pilots have begun to pray to Mother for safe, uninterrupted journeys. Please note this action is not sanctioned nor approved by the Guild and is considered a fineable offense.

name: The Shepherd
description: The Shepherd is a deep-space entity that manipulates gravity wells and celestial bodies as if guiding a flock. It draws moons, asteroids, stations, rings, and derelict vessels into vast migratory patterns, rearranging star systems according to an unknown instinct. Oftentimes its arrangements defy gravitational physics models and create ‘gravity storms’ within the system. Systems touched by the Shepherd may remain physically intact while becoming impossible to inhabit.

name: The Basilica of Unborn Stars
description: The Basilica of Unborn Stars is a cathedral-like cosmic entity that implants stellar embryos into moons, gas giants, dead planets, megastructures, and inhabited worlds. It is often encountered in dying systems, where its arrival brings warmth, light, renewed crop yields, and religious fervor before the true nature of the implantation is understood. As the stellar embryo matures, the host body ignites from within, causing radiation storms, tectonic rupture, atmospheric combustion, and catastrophic gravitational disruption.

name: Nullary
description:
Nullary is a memetic and extra-causal threat that appears as white or colorless text across documents, star charts, legal records, command code, prayer inscriptions, and damaged hull surfaces. Once read or interpreted, its statements begin enforcing themselves upon local reality. Orders become compulsions, borders become physical barriers, lies become real, and maps may overwrite the terrain they describe. With the right words, it has the potential to end reality itself.
[VISUAL REFERENCE CENSORED]

name: Class I - Aberrant
description: Localized threats, usually planetary or smaller in scope.

name: Class II - Exigent
description: Sector-level threats that can spread across multiple systems if unchecked.

name: Class III - Cataclysmic
description: Galactic-scale threats that can collapse civilizations if confronted alone.

name: Class IV - Apocalyptic
description: Universal destabilizers that warp time, consume stars, devour dreams, or damage reality itself.

name: Class V - Omnicidal
description: Existence-wide annihilation or assimilation threats.

name: DMN-Unit
description: A DMN-Unit, short for Dynamic Mechanized Neuralink Unit and commonly called a mech or demon, is a living machine that links a pilot directly to a fully realized Core. Their rarity reflects strict compatibility requirements, demanding training, and the profession's high mortality.

name: Frame
description: Semi-mass produced mech that has limited resonance capabilities due to the lack of a fully realized Core. Still requires some compatibility between Pilot and Core, but the risk associated with failure is significantly lessened in exchange for less Resonance output.

name: Guild Lanes
description: Stable interstellar travel routes through the Manifold. Civilization clusters around these routes because most of space remains unreachable without Guild maps and engines.

name: Neuralink
description: A Neuralink is the mental and Resonance-based connection between a pilot and Core. Frames use limited versions that reduce both the danger of incompatibility and the amount of Resonance the pilot can access.

name: Primus
description: Primus is humanity's first and only homeworld, now largely uninhabitable after centuries of ruin. It remains the symbolic origin of modern interstellar civilization despite repeated failed restoration efforts.

name: Resonance
description: Resonance is a living energy that responds to will and can alter matter or animate machines when properly synchronized. Outside academic use, it is commonly called magic.

name: Resonance Core
description: A Resonance Core is a forged biomechanical node that channels Resonance and can mature into the living control system of a Frame or DMN-Unit. The Guild controls production because unstable forging can devastate entire worlds, while incompatibility with a realized Core can permanently injure or kill a pilot.

name: Sector
description: A major political, military, or economic region of space, usually defined by Guild lane access and the power bloc that dominates it.

name: The Astral Plane
description: The Astral Plane is a dimension where cognition exists as measurable structure independent of a living brain. Subjective expectation alters matter and instrumentation within it, while persistent mental residues can develop into autonomous phenomena.

name: The Crown Line
description: The oldest and safest Guild artery, running from Primus through the Crown Sector to the Luthan Sector. It is treated as the backbone of civilization.

name: The Crucible
description: The Crucible is a dimension of unrealized energy in which matter becomes increasingly responsive to intent and physical law less deterministic. Resonance appears to originate from its interaction with reality, and its measurable feedback suggests possible self-organizing behavior.

name: The Guild Directorate
description: The Guild Directorate is the supranational authority that controls lawful interstellar passage through its monopoly on lanes, engines, and transit licensing. Governments retain local sovereignty, but violations of Guild route authority can result in seizure, embargo, or loss of interstellar access.

name: The Manifold
description: The Manifold is a higher-dimensional medium whose spatial relationships differ from those of the Material Plane. Guild lanes are stabilized routes through its shifting topology, allowing distant systems to become adjacent while nearby ones remain unreachable.

name: The Material Plane
description: The Material Plane is the baseline four-dimensional environment in which known civilization and ordinary causality exist. It serves as the reference frame against which all planar intrusions and deviations are measured.

name: The Plane of Combustion
description: The Plane of Combustion is a dimension where stored potential exists as active reaction rather than stable matter. Material introduced into it tends toward uncontrolled energy release, suggesting that ignition exists there independently of fuel.

name: The Plane of Currents
description: The Plane of Currents is a dimension where motion and transfer exist without mass or stable objects. Direction has greater meaning than position, making navigation dependent on flow rather than location.

name: The Plane of Entropy
description: The Plane of Entropy is a dimension where ordered systems lose coherence without requiring the normal passage of time. Matter, machinery, and information introduced into it progressively become less organized and predictable.

name: The Plane of Geometry
description: The Plane of Geometry is a realm of pure mathematical relationship without matter, energy, or time. Its perfect consistency makes it one of the most stable known dimensions and a theoretical reference for physical law.

name: The Plane of Intuition
description: The Plane of Intuition is a probabilistic environment where conclusions can exist without traceable premises. Biological minds often gain unexplained insight within it, while formal computation and directional navigation become unreliable.

name: The Plane of Memory
description: The Plane of Memory is a nonlinear information dimension where experiences persist beyond the minds that formed them. Memories within it degrade and recombine, creating a risk that visitors will absorb foreign experiences into their own identities.

name: The Plane of Presence
description: The Plane of Presence is a dimension where existence is measured by observability and influence rather than physical mass. Entities register according to their prominence, allowing historically significant people or events to outweigh far larger objects.

name: The Plane of Pressure
description: The Plane of Pressure is a dimension where force and resistance exist without mass or gravity. Objects exposed to it can suffer stress and deformation from directions that do not correspond to ordinary space.

name: The Plane of Radiation
description: The Plane of Radiation is a dimension where electromagnetic propagation exists without a physical source or medium. Its dense, self-sustaining emissions make it extremely hazardous to matter and biological life.

name: The Plane of Sight
description: The Plane of Sight is a dimension where visual information exists without physical objects, light sources, or observers. It produces images without stable perspective, representing visibility itself rather than illumination.

name: The Plane of Smell
description: The Plane of Smell is a dimension where scent exists as information without air or chemical particles. Exposure links sourceless scent impressions to memory and instinct, causing severe interference with recognition and recall.

name: The Plane of Sound
description: The Plane of Sound is a dimension where vibration propagates without a physical medium. Acoustic information persists there as a stable condition, making prolonged exposure harmful to sensors and nervous systems.

name: The Plane of Taste
description: The Plane of Taste is a dimension where matter is evaluated through chemical meaning without requiring chemistry. Exposure produces sourceless judgments of nourishment or danger and can disrupt neural systems tied to instinctive classification.

name: The Plane of Touch
description: The Plane of Touch is a dimension where contact and resistance exist without stable surfaces. Equipment can return bearing physical wear from interactions with objects that cannot be located or confirmed.

name: The Temporal Plane
description: The Temporal Plane is a dimension where time exists as navigable structure rather than sequential experience. Chronodrakes are believed to move through it directly, allowing them to interact with multiple points in a timeline.

name: The Void
description: The Void is not a plane but the absence of dimensional structure between planes. Everything exposed to it rapidly loses physical, informational, and causal coherence because no consistent laws apply within it.

name: Ember Sun
description: Dying red giant whose unstable output gives the Cindral system its bronze skies, erratic seasons, and constant evacuation planning.

name: Ardane System
description: The Ardane system surrounds the Crown’s council world with the mines of Orren, the reservoir seas of Mereveil, the proving grounds of Valecourt, the reserve holdings of Thorne, and the patrol anchorages around Gannet. Palace-cities and embassy keeps dominate Ardane itself, but policy made there depends on an entire network of noble houses and ceremonial tournament grounds.

name: Velbrant System
star_type: Class A (Bright white) + Class M (Red Dwarf)
description: Velbrant is a binary fortress system whose bright primary and red companion illuminate tourney grounds, metal worlds, gun moons, escort yards, and the Whitefire early-warning array. The Grand Lists and High Marshal’s Ring make the system a stage for Crown prestige, but its distributed defenses and outer fortress moon ensure that every ceremony can become a mobilization.

name: Hallowmere System
description: The Hallowmere system is the Crown’s agricultural heart, combining the inhabited breadbasket world with Orchard Crown, Ceresin’s managed seas, reservoir moons, seed vaults, grain reserves, and industrial support on Vellum. Dream-Eater alerts across its farms, moons, and storage routes are common enough that pilots should treat sudden silence anywhere in the system as a warning.

name: Kaelith System
description: Kaelith is a red-dwarf border system built around the gas giant Avarn, its inhabited moon, the mining world Skarn, and the paired Bracken and Hest redoubts.

name: Braelyn Hold System
description: The Braelyn Hold system is arranged as a layered fortress, from the industrial world Braelyn Hold and its gun moon to Shieldward, Vault Moon, the Iron Halo called the Herald Glass, and the outer anchor at Banner’s Rest. Ceremonial hospitality masks a defense plan written across orbital firing corridors.

name: Kether Vale System
description: Kether Vale is an agrarian frontier system of river continents, water worlds, scattered baronies, cold outer planets, and lightly defended moons. Its farms and herds feed Crown fleets, but the distance between Kether Vale, Low Vale, Rill, and the outer holdings leaves local lords dependent on slow convoys and unreliable reinforcement.

name: High Alder Span System
description: High Alder Span is a binary lane-bridge system whose Guild-compatible transit array links Aldergate, Spanhold, Far Alder, and their watch moons across a difficult gravitational corridor. Maintenance clans and customs knights live throughout the system, keeping the rear Crown loop open while monitoring traffic that attempts to bypass the recognized span.

name: Duris System
description: Duris is a ruined white-dwarf system where the broken throne-world, Mausoleum Moon, Ashen Testament, salvage cradles, and the Archive of Claims preserve the wreckage of a fallen royal order. Exiled houses, scavengers, and political archaeologists search across its palaces, docks, and debris fields for evidence capable of reviving old claims.

name: Marnholt System
description: Marnholt is a contested claimant system in which rival banners divide the inhabited world, its moon, the Blue and Gold orbital walls, Palevine, Oathscar, and competing fleet anchorages around Herald. Guild personnel should avoid treating any single capital, platform, or noble fleet as the uncontested authority unless operating under explicit Mandate instruction.

name: Sable Crown System
description: Sable Crown is an exile network hidden within the radiation geometry of a neutron star, centered on Mourning and a cluster of silent stations, signal-locked depots, caches, and concealed arsenals. The system is formally a refuge for displaced claimants, but its distributed court and storage sites function as a market for secrets, leverage, and revenge.

name: Bastrel Gate System
description: Bastrel Gate is an expansion-zone staging system spread across Muster, Pilgrim’s Rest, Garrison, the gas giant Quartermaster, its warehouse moons, and the central transit hub. Barracks orbitals, troop elevators, supply depots, and temporary camps keep the entire system in constant motion under several competing noble chains of command.

name: Stonereach System
description: Stonereach is a cold military foundry system whose red dwarf supports the metal worlds Stonereach and Ferric, their mining moons, the reserve world Blackslag, and fuel operations around Cinderball. Noble manufactories across the system produce armor, lances, and replacement parts for Crown knight frames, making unrest on any major extraction route strategically dangerous.

name: Veld Spire System
description: Veld Spire is a pulsar-based warning system consisting of the shielded array over Veld, the outer world Pulseward, and the Zenith, Meridian, and Nadir observatories. Its separated platforms compare signals across the entire system to detect pirates, Warp Beasts, lane anomalies, and fleet movements that might fool a single station.

name: Deyros System
description: The Deyros system is a dry frontier prefecture spread across inhabited Deyros, the industrial worlds Copper Writ and Prefect’s Reach, Dustwake, Magistrate, and its convoy moon. Crown law weakens with distance from the main world, leaving walled settlements, armed transports, fortified compounds, and local violence to hold the routes together.

name: Harrier Field System
description: Harrier Field is a corsair-interdiction system built around a dense asteroid belt, the hidden Harrier Field Base, three supporting planets, and pre-mined approach lanes. Patrol craft use the field’s rocks, sensor shadows, and displayed pirate hulks to turn the entire system into an ambush ground against Orak raiders.

name: Black Runnel System
description: Black Runnel is a black-hole corridor of unstable micro-lanes, lensing shadows, hidden habitats, and the distributed anchor network used by smugglers to cross between Crown, Orak, and Karnate space. Legal navigation standards do not apply inside its shifting geometry, and no single station controls every route through it.

name: Luthan Prime System
description: The Luthan Prime system combines the League capital with the Exchange Ring, Mandate Court, embassy orbitals, industrial Merovar, oceanic Edrine, and guarded reserves around Covenant. Trade, law, diplomacy, and mercenary work converge across the entire system, making even routine transit part of a larger commercial proceeding.

name: Feyros System
description: Feyros is a finance system of exchange cities, reserve vaults, investment worlds, industrial Specula, the gas giant Othyr, and private negotiation sites on Ilyra. Convoy futures, war-risk indexes, noble scandals, and mech-part markets are traded throughout its orbital network, so every contract has beneficiaries well beyond the world where it is signed.

name: Miridal System
description: The Miridal system is a corporate academic network spanning Miridal and its moons, Cadence, Ortheon, Avenor, the Aeon Archive, the Patent Vault, and research sites around Lysara. Universities, performance cities, museums, and laboratories compete across the system to train League specialists and secure ownership of anything they discover.

name: Ferrith Hub System
description: Ferrith Hub is a brown-dwarf market system spread across a central asteroid bazaar and the mining clusters Veyr’s Folly, Nacre Reach, Saint Orro Claim, Serrake Claim, and Hollow Crown Claim. Auction bays, chop shops, gun markets, private armies, and religious booths move between rocks and docks, allowing almost anything to be bought somewhere in the system.

name: Rynnel System
description: Rynnel is a luxury system built around the ocean world Rynnel, its resort moons, the Crown of Chance habitat, the Velvet Exchange, industrial Vitrine, and the scenic gas giant Radiance. Its beauty, gene-spas, casinos, and designer goods depend on a system-wide service economy hidden behind controlled climates and exclusive transit lanes.

name: Vask Gate System
star_type: Class K (Orange Dwarf) + Class M (Red Dwarf)
description: Vask Gate is a binary customs system whose checkpoint megastation, industrial Othran, tariff moon Selcar, quarantine orbits, and holding lanes regulate entry into profitable League circulation. Scanning hoops and tax courts dominate the Gate itself, but delays, seizures, and unofficial fees can occur anywhere between the inner planet and Quarantine Reach.

name: Ceyra System
description: Ceyra is an industrial system of three gas giants, six major moons, armored aerostat cities, habitat spindles, and harvest nets operating under a blue-white star. Fuel precursors, exotic compounds, labor disputes, and storm damage move constantly between Orvannis, Veydras, Thaumyr, and their support worlds, making the system a linked extraction economy rather than a single colony.

name: Morn Halo System
description: Morn Halo is a refinery system centered on the artificial ring around the gas giant Morn, supported by the industrial worlds Ashfall and Vellum and cold storage on Calyx and Far Halo. Tankers, refinery crews, radiation shifts, and tightly sequenced dock windows bind the whole system into the processing link between Ceyra and the Mawward March.

name: Brindle Shoal System
description: Brindle Shoal is a cold logistics system of ice-and-metal asteroids, hollow-rock yards, the world Brindle, the outer ice world Wake, and convoy infrastructure at the Main Yard, Kestrel Yard, and Durn Haven. Tankers are built, crewed, fueled, and assembled across the shoal before departing in guarded formations.

name: New Ulbar System
description: New Ulbar is a dim brown-dwarf smuggling system consisting of the rocky world Ulbar, its tidally locked colony moon, the hidden Ulbar Cradle, and a debris field engineered to confuse sensors. League merchants, Orak captains, and compromised inspectors use separate approaches and shared deniability, ensuring that no transaction belongs to only one settlement.

name: Meyric System
description: Meyric is an exotic-material system spanning the mineral world Meyric, its mining and administrative moons, the Crystech Vault, Veyrworks, the ocean world Neralis, the boomtown world Kharad, and outer prospecting sites. Resonance-reactive ores and unstable substances pass through several claims, courts, and processing facilities before becoming experimental weapons or Core-interface components.

name: Osmir Reef System
description: Osmir Reef is a brown-dwarf mining system divided among the Inner, Crown, and Outer reef belts, with habitats and cutting stations embedded among branching metallic formations. Claim law and delicate extraction practices govern movement between Arken Spindle, Veyla Habitat, Keldran Cut, and Nareth Cradle because careless blasting can destroy both the ore and whatever structure produced it.

name: Glass Docks System
description: Glass Docks is a free-trade system linking the ocean world Calyx and its moon Argent to the translucent dock complex, the industrial world Vitrion, and the inner world Prism. Negotiations occur in visible chambers and ships berth in clear structures under the primary’s glare, but the system’s openness is architectural rather than ethical.

name: Tovresh System
description: Tovresh is an escort and convoy system spanning the inhabited naval world, its shipbuilding and training moons, the Escort Yards, Marshal Spine, industrial Drosen, provisioning waters on Aven Mare, and the outer anchor at Thalor. League trade survives because crews, supplies, escorts, and merchant formations are coordinated across the entire system before departure.

name: Waymaker System
description: Waymaker is a navigation system of calibration worlds, signal locks, the gas giant Ormec, the guild moon Waymaker, and the outer Rift Monitor at Sable Verge. Pilots and route mathematicians compare observations across these separated stations to maintain frontier paths that become lethal when reduced to a single chart.

name: Grey Twelve System
description: Grey Twelve is a bonded-storage system split between Greyhold, its cryogenic moon, the gas giant Orsin, and twelve warehouse stations distributed between their orbits. Legal evidence, seized assets, war materiel, dormant estates, and restricted cargo are deliberately separated across the chain, making the system boring in the way a magazine full of loaded weapons is boring.

name: Dross Forge System
description: Dross Forge is the Karnate capital system beneath a swollen red giant, linking the furnace world to Vhalka, Orvek, Morvane, Kest Vorn, Serrak, the Ashen Table Citadel, and the Varkesh foundry lattice. Politics and production are distributed through mines, labor warrens, orbital forges, fortress-stacks, and fuel operations around Vel Marr, making the whole system an engine of coercive war industry.

name: Shivra Belt System
description: Shivra Belt is a mining system of armed ore rigs, beast-infested asteroids, the processing world Heshra, support facilities on Vardek, and convoy staging around Nhal. Warp Beasts can silence any cluster without warning, but Karnate supervisors keep the system working because every rig feeds the larger forge chain.

name: Roughline System
description: Roughline is a press-gang system built around the depot moon Roughline and the processing stations, holding blocks, buffer spires, and troop docks spread through Veldros’s orbit. Ships arrive carrying debtors, criminals, refugees, and abducted spacers, then depart through Harrow Six with labor gangs, penal crews, and furnace infantry.

name: Rathmar Prime System
description: Rathmar Prime is an optimized foundry system whose capital world, industrial moon Ostryn, Varkesh Yards, Ordan Forge, Cindor, Malven, Tharsis, Kerric, and the fuel anchor Rath Vorn operate as one production chain. The system appears cleaner than Dross Forge because its cities, mines, coolant sources, and shipyards have been arranged with machine efficiency rather than mercy.

name: Jethra Belt System
star_type: Class K (Orange Dwarf) + Class T (Brown Dwarf)
description: Jethra Belt is a circumbinary mining system where six major rock clusters drift through unstable gravitational interference between an orange dwarf and a brown dwarf. Volatile materials move from Kheris Arc, Vannor Reach, Black Vey, Mornshard, and the other rigs under constant correction from Jethra Monitor, while miners contend with routes and rocks that refuse to remain where charts place them.

name: Gallows Reach System
description: Gallows Reach is a system-sized weapons range combining the cratered test world, three proving moons, the industrial support world Belthar, telemetry from Harrow Array, and long-range trials near Varkane. Target cities, bunker replicas, prisoner assignments, and disposable instrumentation are distributed across multiple bodies so that weapons capable of destroying one site can still be measured from another.

name: Iron Gate System
description: Iron Gate is a blue-star fortress-shipyard system centered on Vorn, its fortified moons, the Iron Gate bastion, Vorn Yards, and Blue Hammer Docks, with mining and training worlds spread through the surrounding orbits. Layered kill-zones, reserve fleets near Thren Vey, concealed hangars on Surn, and hardened industrial routes make the system capable of repairing fleets while under siege.

name: Drossfall System
description: Drossfall is a deliberately poisoned test system in which the corrosive inhabited world, two contaminated moons, underground bunker networks, Kelor Quarantine, and disposal orbits around Veyr Oss isolate hazardous trials from valuable Karnate territory. Personnel and equipment move through sealed crawlers, quarantine rings, and controlled descent corridors because contamination is treated as an operating cost rather than an emergency.

name: Breakwater System
description: Breakwater is a defensive system built around the gas giant Kharon Vey, four armed moons, the Breakwater Anchorage, the Iron Halo minefield, Karth Signal Lock, and Voss Sentinel. Exact approach codes are required because safe corridors shift through chained wrecks, mines, hidden guns, and autonomous defenses that sometimes react without current orders.

name: Orak Station System
description: The Orak Station system sprawls from the Tin Teeth and the welded bazaar itself to the Boiler, its three salvage moons, and Widow’s Wake. Mercenaries, pirates, smugglers, and deserters move between Gun Row, Hookside, Gutterworks, Knucklebone, Platejack, and Cold Pocket under competing syndicate rules that never extend across the whole system.

name: Korran Drift System
description: Korran Drift is a moving system of city-ships, family hulls, market barges, shrine tugs, and armed escorts migrating between Cinderball, the Shove, and the cold refuge of Icehook. Its population lives aboard the flotilla rather than on either planet, and the system’s political geography changes whenever Big Sell, Saint’s Tug, Cradle Chain, or Red Maw alters course.

name: Slate Cradle System
description: Slate Cradle is a salvage system of wreck belts, stripped worlds, improvised yards, and fuel routes around Slingshot. Ships are pulled from the Pickings, Deadwater, and Black Scatter into the Cradle, Core Cage, and Crooked Weld over Blackplate, then returned to service with parts scavenged from across the system.

name: Driftheart System
description: Driftheart is a hidden syndicate system organized around Blackrock, the concealed station-city, Truce Hall, the hostage moon called the Leash, the armed moon Hammer, and the covert dock Backdoor. Pirate leaders meet under truce only because every faction has assets, guns, and hostages distributed throughout the system.

name: Haven Rock System
description: Haven Rock is a free-miner system spanning the settled mining world, Cinderhead, Pig Iron, Copperhead, the Free Moot, Claim Yard, and the outer moons around the Keg. Claims, marriages, convoy rules, and mutual defense are negotiated across these sites, making the system rough and heavily armed without reducing it to another pirate holding.

name: Pike Relay System
description: Pike Relay is an information-ambush system whose hidden sensors and transmitters are distributed between Doorstop, Dead Ear, Tripwire, Blindside, the gas giant called the Blind, and Long Ear. The main relay appears abandoned because no single installation needs to remain active long enough to reveal the whole picket network.

name: Greyspan Station System
description: Greyspan is a pirate fortress system embedded in a neutron-star hazard zone, with the citadel shielded behind the Carrion, Knucklerock, Shrapnel Sea, and the heavy guns of the Iron Smile. Chainmarket, Prize Row, repair docks, and syndicate districts make Greyspan Station the visible capital, but the surrounding debris and fortifications are what prevent sane governments from reaching it.

name: Spindle Rock System
description: Spindle Rock is a vermin-infested mining system whose surface workings, the moons Bitepit and Leakside, Deep Cut, Red Seal, and Patchhouse are repeatedly opened, contaminated, and sealed. Ore still leaves the system because crews can abandon one mine or moon and shift extraction elsewhere before the Rift Vermin follow.

name: Ash Rack System
description: Ash Rack is a burned system of ruined worlds, orbital shells, salvage camps, and debris. Charhouse, Crooked Halo, Deadlight, Burnscar, Sootball, and the Peel are stripped by scavengers that only agree that certain decks and signals should be avoided.

name: Cindral System
description: The Cindral system orbits the dying Ember Sun and is planned around eventual failure, with the capital on Cindral-II, emergency government sites on its moon, the Cindral Bastion, Ember Refuge, industrial Cindral-III, and reserve settlements on Cindral-IV. Bronze skies and unstable seasons define the capital world, but evacuation routes, shelters, fuel stores, and continuity infrastructure extend across the entire system.

name: Braxis System
description: Braxis is the March’s layered bastion system, linking Braxis-III and its defense moons to the Long Wall, the orbital redoubt, the industrial world Braxis-II, the inhabited frontier on Braxis-IV, and outer warning positions around Braxis-V. Every body contributes guns, supplies, population, or warning time to a defense intended to delay Mawward threats long enough for the rest of the March to react.

name: Red Choir System
description: Red Choir is an evacuation system centered on Red Choir-II and its refugee moon, with the rally station, Morrow Refuge, Kestrel Triage, Last Harbor, surface muster fields, and sealed stores operating as one emergency network. When a frontier colony falls, refugees are sorted, treated, housed, and assigned transport across the system while the alarm tones that gave Red Choir its name continue to sound.

name: Ashveil Prime System
description: Ashveil is a fading-star frontier system stretching from the observatories of Ashveil-I and the mines of Ashveil-II to the inhabited world Ashveil-III, the Command bastion, Cinder Relay, cold reserve worlds, and Red Lantern beyond Ashveil-VI. It connects the Mawward March to the Silent Way through a chain of bunkers, relays, listening posts, and fallback settlements rather than through one capital alone.

name: Duskwatch System
description: Duskwatch is a dark brown-dwarf surveillance system consisting of the cold world Duskwatch-I, its artificial light mirrors, Duskwatch Post, and the separated Kest, Orra, and Veyr watch stations. Crews compare observations across the system because any single post may be deceived, compromised, or simply fail to remember what triggered an alert.

name: Hollow Verge System
description: Hollow Verge is an abandoned frontier system of three former colony worlds, derelict stations, dead defense grids, salvage sites, and illegal habitation. Veyla Station, Morrow Spindle, Kestrel Relay, Sable Cradle, and Far Orison still cycle fragments of their old functions, leaving the system empty enough to be lawless but active enough to be dangerous.

name: Halix System
description: The Halix system is the Compact’s psychological-defense capital, linking the inhabited world to Morrow, Halix Command, Quiet Ward, the ocean world Vesper, industrial Locus, and the outer warning sites on Terminus and Pall. Civil calm drills and anomaly reporting begin on Halix, but the system’s separated stations and worlds exist to verify one another when perception, memory, or testimony becomes unreliable.

name: Crowthorne System
description: Crowthorne is a Silent Way watch system spread across Briar, the scarred inhabited world, its gun moon Thorn, Crowthorne Watch, Hushline, the reserve world Vigil, and outer posts around Orison. Listening towers and sensor forests remain quiet by design, while separated crews compare dreams and observations to determine whether an anomaly is local or system-wide.

name: Pale Hinge System
star_type: Class M (Red Dwarf) + Class L (Brown Dwarf)
description: Pale Hinge is a binary border-lock system whose authority is distributed between Latch, Palisade, the quarantine moon Rime, the central lock, Memory Court, and Clean Passage. Ships are screened across several stages for psychic contamination, memory disruption, and unauthorized passengers so that the Silent Way can be sealed even if one checkpoint is compromised.

name: Nerith Hold System
description: Nerith Hold is an academy system rather than a single school, spanning Nerith, the training moon Somnus, two independent quarantine satellites, the Nerith Academy, and research or reserve worlds at Cipher, Lumen, Praxis, Lacuna, and Abyss. Monitors, screeners, analysts, and resistant pilots train across separate environments so that no one curriculum or shared dream can compromise the whole institution.

name: Kryne Relay System
description: Kryne Relay is a pulsar-timed defense system built around the barren world Kryne and four shielded stations assigned to observation, communication, recovery, and anomaly analysis. The Compact compares each installation’s clocks, memories, and sensor logs against the pulsar.

name: Blank Stair System
description: Blank Stair is a quarantine system arranged in layers around Oblivion and its dead moon Null, with the orbital checkpoint and four sealed platforms separating suspect ships, prisoners, records, and communications. No person, vessel, or idea leaves through Last Seal without passing multiple memory and contamination reviews conducted by authorities that do not fully trust one another.

name: Veyra System
description: The Veyra system is the spiritual heart of the Choir Path, joining the pilgrimage world and its moons to the Great Chorus Conclave, Pilgrim Crown, Sariel’s monastery seas, the quiet worlds Eiren and Oriel, and outer shrines around Threnody and Halcyon. Pilgrimage, commerce, law, and fleet gatherings move through the whole system in processions rather than remaining confined to Veyra’s basilicas.

name: Low Cantor System
description: Low Cantor is a monastic shipbuilding system centered on the yards and Hymnforge above Canticle, with cloistered work crews on Psalm, older settlements on Vestry, and fleet assembly around Benediction and Votive. Vessels are built, blessed, crewed, and joined to migratory processions across the system, making every launch both an industrial act and a religious departure.

name: Hush Gate System
description: Hush Gate is a young, unstable system of dust, radiation, shifting debris, the worlds Penance and Exile, the penitents’ port, the Unspoken Court, and the Mute Lantern navigation station. Pilgrims, criminals, exiles, and zealots are screened and assigned vows across several sites before they are allowed to continue deeper into Choir space.

name: Choralith System
description: Choralith is a sacred asteroid system whose cathedral, three shrine rocks, internal anchorage, and distant ice world form a dispersed pilgrimage complex under a red dwarf. The cathedral is the largest site, but worship, silence, docking, and custodial life extend between multiple rocks whose impossible acoustics sometimes carry sound farther than their orbits should allow.

name: Songspire System
description: Songspire is a resonant system in which the Core-world, its moons Cantor and Refrain, the Living Vault, Spireward, the ocean world Seraph, industrial Votive, and the outer moons of Orison all exhibit different relationships to local resonance. Pilots and cantors compare dreams, instruments, and environmental changes across the system because effects dismissed on one body may repeat on another.

name: Miren System
description: Miren is a compromised pilgrimage system whose public shrines, infected districts, processional station, quarantine ring, frontier worlds, and isolated outer moon are divided between Choir authority and Phage cult influence. The danger is not confined to Miren itself, since pilgrims, refugees, sealed cargo, and suspected cult networks move between Mercy, Sable, Vigil, Miren’s Wake, and Absolution.

name: Evensong System
description: Evensong is a relic system built around the cold world Requiem, its crypt moon, the Evensong archive complex, and the First and Last Bell shrine stations. Pilgrims approach, enter, and depart through separate ritual sites so that any awakening among the saint-mechs can be observed from outside the crypt as well as within it.

name: Eyral System
description: Eyral is a cathedral system whose half-hollowed inhabited world, construction moon Nave, monastic moon Sanctum, Pilgrim Crown, Inner Choir, and surrounding worlds preserve different stages of the Choir’s largest architectural act of faith. Visitors move between orbital reception, planetary caverns, oceanic Solace, quiet Vesper, and the auroral outer giant Magnificat rather than experiencing Eyral as a single monument.

name: Veyth System
description: Veyth is a colony system centered on the gas giant and its inhabited moons Hearth, Lesson, and Harvest, with ordinary settlements on Ember, Ashen, Quietus, and Wayfarer and regular fleet exchange at the Common Anchorage. Population, food, schooling, worship, and family movement are distributed across the system.

name: Grey Orison System
description: Grey Orison is a silenced system consisting of two cold worlds, the forbidden shrine, Custodian’s Rest, two dead relays, and the Listening Post beneath a white dwarf. Singing and resonance devices are restricted throughout the system because the original event may have propagated through stations and signals rather than occurring at the shrine alone.

name: Grailrunner
visual: A Razor Skimmer rebuilt into a heraldic cavalry craft, its prow extended into a lance-shaped ram and its wing-vanes flared like a knight’s mantle. House colors trail from stabilizer fins, though most are burned ragged by engine wash.
behavior: Shock cavalry skimmer. Trades some ambush utility for direct charge capability, using a forward resonance ram to punch through infantry blocks, light armor, and weakened mech joints. Often leads knightly assaults, opening a breach for Crown Lancers and Castellans.
report_text: “It crossed the field like a tournament charge. Then the prow hit the barricade and the whole wall folded inward.”

name: Argent
visual: A modified Ironclad. A polished white-gold tank with a shield-shaped prow, layered heraldic armor, and a turret framed by banner vanes and resonance emitters. The front hull glows with a faint protective field when advancing.
behavior: Turns the Ironclad into a command and formation-anchor tank. It projects a directional barrier that protects infantry, retainers, and lighter vehicles pushing behind it, making it ideal for noble charges, urban advances, and formal battlefield breakthroughs.
report_text: “The Argent moved first. Every lesser machine formed behind their shields, and for six minutes the enemy could only shoot at a wall.”

name: Typhon
visual: A modified Basilisk. The barrel is thicker and heat constantly emanates from the end, covered in additional armor plating with an added crucible reactor attached to the barrel causing the vents to glow molten hot.
behavior: Unleashes raw, condensed heat in focused beams, melting through armor and anything else in its path while carving continuous lances of destruction across fortifications and landscapes.
report_text: "The changes made appeared comical at first. We stopped laughing when it melted the bunker and everyone inside, then continued past it.”

name: Slagmaw
visual: A modified Ironclad. A furnace-bellied tank with a shovel-like prow, exposed smokestacks, and dense armor plates. Its tracks leave glowing scars in soft ground.
behavior: Turns the Ironclad into a breaching and area-denial engine. It vomits molten slag into trenches, streets, and bunker mouths, making ground impassable behind its advance.
report_text: “The Slagmaw does not conquer territory. No no no… it ‘preserves’ it until the Thralls can mine it out.”

name: Emberwing-Class Fighter
visual: Modified Starhawk. A lean ace-pattern fighter with swept ember-black wings, reinforced VTOL thrusters under the fuselage, and heat-scored ground-attack rails beneath the cockpit. Its exhaust burns dull orange like a dying sun.
behavior: Elite air-superiority fighter modified for vertical takeoff, low-atmosphere hovering, and brutal ground support. The Emberwing can duel enemy fighters, then drop into VTOL stance above a battlefield to rake armor columns with precision cannons and micro-missile salvos.
report_text: “The enemy thought I overshot. I killed thrust, dropped nose-first between the buildings, and fired straight down the street.”

name: Reliquary Mule
visual: A white and brass armored transport with ritualistic glyphs on the interior, psionic ward plates along the exterior, and a roof-mounted harmonic emitter. Its ramp opens beneath a curtain of faint blue resonance light.
behavior: A protected pilgrim and adept carrier designed for contaminated war zones. It shields passengers from psychic interference, steadies allied morale, and can serve as a mobile ritual anchor once deployed.
report_text: “The screaming stopped when the doors closed. Outside, the battle kept going. Inside, the choir sang joyous hymns while we prepared for our next mission.”

name: Canticle
visual: A modified Basilisk. The barrel is surrounded by tuning rings, choir-crystal vanes, and suspended resonance chimes that vibrate before each shot. Hymn-script runs down the gun carriage in layered bands.
behavior: Sonic resonance artillery. It does not rely only on explosive force. Instead, it finds harmonic weaknesses in walls, armor, shields, and tunnels, then shakes them apart from within. Its first shot marks the structure, analyzes the harmonics. Its second makes every crack sing.
report_text: “Steel does not resist if taught the correct note.”

name: Nightglass-Class Bomber
visual: A Thunderbolt stealth bomber with black resonance-null plating, flattened engine housings, and bomb bays hidden behind seamless hull panels. Its exhaust appears as a faint distortion rather than flame.
behavior: Stealth bomber and command-killer. It sacrifices payload volume for psionic shielding, sensor masking, silent approach, and precision resonance charges that overload command bunkers, shield nodes, or unaware Mim clusters. Halix rarely admits these aircraft exist.
report_text: “Radar saw weather. Thermal saw nothing. The bunker opened from the inside out.”

name: Ghostmark
visual: A modified Razor Skimmer. A narrow black recon craft with psionic shielding, adaptive cloak plating, muffled grav vanes, and needle-like sensors folded beneath its prow. Invisible to the eyes and nearly undetectable to instruments.
behavior: Recon, target marking, and assassination skimmer. It avoids direct combat, instead identifying command units, artillery nests, or shield weak points. Once it marks a target, Halix strike assets usually arrive before the enemy knows it has been seen.

name: Jackknife
visual: A modified Razor Skimmer. A jagged grav-raider built from stolen plates and exposed thruster vanes, with grappling harpoons mounted beneath the prow and boarding hooks folded along the flanks.
behavior: Boarding skimmer and ambush craft. It closes too fast, fires grapples into vehicles or low-flying craft, then drags itself into blind spots where cutters can breach armor. Fragile in clean battlefield conditions, but vicious in wreck fields, asteroid docks, and station approaches.
report_text: “Do not chase the Jackknife. That is how it gets behind you.”

name: Grabhook Mule
visual: A modified Mule Carrier. A battered boarding transport with heavy clamp-arms, hull magnets, breaching collars, and welded cage racks along the exterior. Its rear ramp is reinforced like a siege door.
behavior: Boarding carrier and forced-entry hauler. The Grabhook latches onto ships, bunkers, or disabled vehicles, locks itself in place, and burns a passage open while its crew prepares to storm through. It can also rip cargo containers or escape pods directly from a target.
report_text: “The ramp does not open until the door on the other side stops being a door.”

name: Merchant-Lord
description: A Merchant-Lord is a Luthan ruler whose authority comes from controlling credit, contracts, and the resources needed to employ force. Their commercial decisions carry sovereign weight, allowing debt enforcement to shape the fate of entire worlds.

name: Forge-Lord
description: A Forge-Lord is a Karnate industrial ruler who commands a foundry's labor, military production, and war engines. Their authority is measured by sustained output, and everyone beneath them is treated as part of the production system.

name: Foundry-Clan
description: A Foundry-Clan is a Karnate political house built around a major war-production complex. It binds lineage and industrial command into a single institution that competes for resources while feeding the wider Karnate war machine.

name: Belt-King
description: A Belt-King is an Orak pirate sovereign whose authority rests on continued profit, victory, and control over raider captains. Their rule remains personal and unstable, collapsing as soon as weakness outweighs fear or loyalty.

name: Crown Council
description: The Crown Council is the ruling assembly of the Crown Concordant, where hereditary sovereigns and major noble houses negotiate policy and legitimacy. Its decrees carry royal authority but remain constrained by house rivalries and competing claims.

name: Noble House
description: A noble house is a hereditary political institution that binds lineage to territorial authority, military obligation, and patronage. In Crown and Cindral society, its continuity is maintained through inherited rights, public legitimacy, and reciprocal oaths.

name: The War
description: The War is the unresolved event believed to have destroyed the civilizations whose ruins predate life on Primus and now fill the otherwise empty stars. The surviving evidence is fragmentary and contradictory, leaving even the nature of the event unknown.

name: Cindral-I
description: Scorched inner world carrying heat-resistant power stations, flare monitors, and automated observatories.

name: Cindral-II
description: March capital commonly called Cindral, with a strained old Primus-like biosphere, bronze skies, heat-shielded cities, evacuation tunnels, and old fortress walls.

name: Cindral-II-a
description: Fortified administrative moon containing emergency government vaults, reserve command posts, and protected archives.

name: Cindral Bastion
description: Orbital defense and command station coordinating the capital fleet, evacuation exercises, and the March’s political leadership.

name: Ember Refuge
description: Permanent evacuation habitat maintained for officials, critical workers, and civilians displaced by solar emergencies.

name: Cindral-III
description: Cold industrial world supplying armor, bunker plate, and replacement infrastructure to the capital.

name: Cindral-IV
description: Unstable outer frontier world of scattered extraction camps, sensor posts, and deep emergency stores.

name: Cindral-IV-a
description: Remote ice moon used for fuel storage, signal relays, and long-duration survival drills.

name: Braxis Primary
description: Steady orange dwarf supporting the March’s principal fortress system.

name: Braxis-I
description: Barren inner world covered in early-warning sensors, missile tracking stations, and hardened power collectors.

name: Braxis-II
description: Industrial mining world producing armor plate, ammunition casings, and bunker components for the system’s defenses.

name: Braxis-III
description: Cold fortress world layered with bastions, shielded settlements, ration depots, and inherited watch posts.

name: Braxis-III-a
description: Gun moon mounting heavy artillery, fleet-control arrays, and redundant command facilities.

name: Braxis-III-b
description: Cold logistics moon containing fuel reserves, field hospitals, and shelters for evacuated surface populations.

name: Braxis Hold
description: Central orbital fortress linking the planet’s bastion network to fleet defenses and Mawward early-warning systems.

name: The Long Wall
description: Layered orbital defense line designed to delay incursions long enough for inner March systems to mobilize or evacuate.

name: Braxis-IV
description: Thinly inhabited frontier world with a damaged Primus-like biosphere, fortified agricultural basins, and conscription settlements.

name: Braxis-V
description: Large outer gas giant whose gravity well anchors reserve fleets and distant sensor platforms.

name: Braxis-V-a
description: Outer defense moon holding concealed strike-craft hangars and long-range missile batteries.

name: Far Vigil
description: Deep-system sensor station watching for Mawward distortions, hostile fleets, and changes in the outer lanes.

name: Red Choir Primary
description: Dim red dwarf around which the March concentrates evacuation, triage, and refugee logistics.

name: Red Choir-I
description: Airless inner world carrying power plants, storage caverns, and automated emergency-beacon transmitters.

name: Red Choir-II
description: Cold logistics world covered in muster fields, sealed warehouses, landing zones, and temporary settlement blocks.

name: Red Choir-II-a
description: Refugee moon with a controlled Primus-like atmosphere, overcrowded habitation districts, triage centers, and long-term resettlement camps.

name: Red Choir
description: Evacuation rally station whose alarm tones signal lost colonies, incoming refugee fleets, and priority launch orders.

name: Morrow Refuge
description: Large emergency habitat holding civilians who cannot yet be assigned transport, shelter, or permanent resettlement.

name: Kestrel Triage
description: Medical and quarantine station screening refugees for radiation exposure, contamination, and hostile infiltration.

name: Last Harbor
description: Armed dockyard assigning escorts and converting civilian transports for emergency evacuation service.

name: Ashveil Primary
description: Unusually dim and fading orange dwarf whose declining output leaves the system under persistent red twilight.

name: Ashveil-I
description: Cold inner planet carrying solar observatories, mirror-control stations, and abandoned early settlement sites.

name: Ashveil-II
description: Mining and industrial world supplying bunker plate, sensor housings, and replacement equipment to the frontier.
