description: Sealed orbital and surface control network isolating infected cargo, crews, and equipment.

name: Patchhouse
description: Repair and decontamination dock stocked with breach foam, traps, and emergency hull patches.

name: Ash Rack Primary
description: Orange dwarf illuminating a damaged system whose former outpost was destroyed and never fully reclaimed.

name: Burnscar
description: Scorched inner planet covered in wrecked batteries, impact fields, and abandoned emergency shelters.

name: Ash Rack
description: Ruined outpost world with a damaged Primus-like biosphere, burned settlements, salvage camps, and unanswered evidence of a system-wide attack.

name: Charhouse
description: Charred orbital shell containing salvage, sealed decks, dead defense systems, and areas avoided by local crews after dark.

name: Crooked Halo
description: Partially collapsed dock ring used by scavengers despite failing rotation and unreliable pressure seals.

name: Deadlight
description: Ruined station segment that still receives power and broadcasts internal announcements from inaccessible decks.

name: Sootball
description: Outer world of frozen dust, failed settlements, and wreckage from ships that attempted to flee the original disaster.

name: The Peel
description: Ruined orbital structures and broken defense platforms scattered across the outer system.

name: Veyra Primary
description: Stable yellow star at the spiritual heart of the Choir Path, surrounded by pilgrimage traffic and the seasonal anchorages of the migratory fleet.

name: Caelus
description: Warm inner world of ochre uplands, wind-cut basins, scattered hermit settlements, and observatories maintained by minor devotional orders.

name: Veyra
description: Holy pilgrimage world with a flourishing Primus-like biosphere, resonant basilicas, public chant plazas, shrine-cities, and roads joining sites associated with old Core miracles.

name: Vespertine
description: Temperate moon of terraced pilgrim towns, hospice monasteries, and open-air choirs that sing through the long dusk.

name: Choirglass
description: Pale moon whose naturally resonant caverns are used for vigils, mass recitations, and the testing of sacred instruments.

name: Great Chorus Conclave
description: Orbital assembly hall where linked seers, senior cantors, fleet elders, and shrine delegations deliberate through formal chorus.

name: Pilgrim Crown
description: Ring of docks, hostels, markets, and reliquary chapels receiving pilgrims before they descend to the holy world.

name: Sariel
description: Blue ocean world dotted with monastery islands, floating shrines, and quiet communities that rarely interact with the larger pilgrimage circuit.

name: Eiren
description: Gray mountain world with old mining scars, abandoned settlements, and several modest Choir enclaves built around surviving wells.

name: Oriel
description: Cold world of luminous glaciers and narrow habitable valleys visited by pilgrims seeking solitude rather than revelation.

name: Threnody
description: Compact gas giant with pale bands and a broad family of minor moons, used as a visual landmark by arriving fleet processions.

name: Reliquary
description: Remote ice moon holding sealed relic vaults, forgotten pilgrimage shelters, and several chapels maintained by rotating custodians.

name: Halcyon
description: Quiet outer world of blue ice, sparse stations, and long intervals without visitors beyond a few contemplative orders.

name: Low Cantor Primary
description: Long-lived orange dwarf around which the Choir maintains monastic shipyards and several permanent fleet anchorages.

name: Canticle
description: Dark metallic world whose orbital yards draw upon old mines and reclaimed hull stock without covering the planet in heavy settlement.

name: Low Cantor Yards
description: Monastic shipyards where crews chant during welds, carve hymn-script into hull ribs, and prepare vessels to serve as homes, temples, and future reliquaries.

name: Hymnforge
description: Smaller sacred forge producing Choir-pattern mechs, ceremonial armor, and replacement components for the migratory fleet.

name: Psalm
description: Airless moon occupied by cloistered work crews, drydock monasteries, and archives of shipbuilding liturgy.

name: Vestry
description: Dry world of broad salt flats, isolated settlements, and abandoned launch fields from earlier periods of Choir migration.

name: Benediction
description: Large amber gas giant whose upper atmosphere supplies fuel to the yards and whose orbit provides room for mass fleet assemblies.

name: Votive
description: Cold moon covered in memorial cairns and retired hull sections left by crews before beginning long pilgrimages.

name: Processional Anchorage
description: Wide orbital assembly zone where Choir flotillas reorganize, exchange passengers, and depart in carefully timed processions.

name: Hush Gate Primary
description: Young unstable star surrounded by radiation storms, dust, and the unfinished debris of planetary formation.

name: Penance
description: Volcanically active world with an unstable crust, thin toxic atmosphere, and austere settlements built into shielded ravines.

name: Hush Gate
description: Deliberately uncomfortable port where pilgrims, criminals, exiles, and zealots take vows of silence, service, or separation before entering deeper Choir space.

name: The Unspoken Court
description: Inspection and adjudication station where arrivals are screened, assigned sponsors, and separated from the wider pilgrim population.

name: Exile
description: Unstable outer world repeatedly reshaped by impacts, cryovolcanism, and shifting debris rings.

name: Dust Choir
description: Thick protoplanetary debris field whose charged particles produce low radio tones interpreted by some pilgrims as an unfinished hymn.

name: Mute Lantern
description: Navigation station guiding vessels through the dust while communicating almost entirely through coded light.

name: Choralith Primary
description: Dim red dwarf illuminating a sparse system whose sacred sites are carved from asteroids rather than planets.

name: First Shrine
description: Hollowed shrine rock containing a single resonant chamber and a small custodial community.

name: Choralith Cathedral
description: Vast asteroid-cathedral of low-gravity chapels, plasma-lit naves, sealed crypts, and impossible acoustics that carry whispers across kilometers.

name: Second Shrine
description: Roughly carved shrine asteroid visited by crews seeking blessings before entering the cathedral’s deeper chambers.

name: Third Shrine
description: Remote shrine rock where speech is restricted and pilgrims communicate through gesture, breath, and written chant notation.

name: Crypt Anchorage
description: Protected docking hollow within the cathedral asteroid, large enough to shelter several Choir vessels at once.

name: Choralith
description: Uninhabited outer ice world visible from the cathedral as a pale wandering light and used only for occasional resource collection.

name: Songspire Primary
description: Bright white star bathing the system’s resonant worlds and moons in hard, shifting light.

name: Aureole
description: Hot inner world of glass plains, mineral ridges, and abandoned survey camps where resonance once produced unreliable instrument readings.

name: Songspire
description: Resonant world with a strained ancient Primus-like biosphere, luminous resonance seams rising through the crust, tuned buildings, and a constant low atmospheric hum.

name: Cantor
description: Moon of resonant stone where pilots, cantors, and mech crews conduct synchronized training beneath open vacuum shields.

name: Refrain
description: Small habitable moon of scattered settlements and forests whose growth patterns subtly change around major Choir festivals.

name: The Living Vault
description: Orbital repository containing resonance fragments, sacred interface components, and records of pilots whose mechs developed unusual dreams.

name: Spireward
description: Monitoring station mapping changes in planetary resonance and warning when local harmonics begin affecting memory or perception.

name: Seraph
description: Warm ocean world of archipelagos, storm belts, and small devotional colonies that have developed distinct regional chants.

name: Votive
description: Dark mineral world with sparse settlements and several abandoned attempts to reproduce Songspire’s resonance artificially.

name: Orison
description: Large gas giant surrounded by brilliant auroras and used as a meeting place for pilgrim ships that avoid the crowded inner system.

name: Liturgy
description: Bright ice moon with a few sealed monasteries and long-abandoned resonance experiments beneath its surface.

name: Echo
description: Outer moon where communications are often returned with subtle timing errors and unfamiliar background voices.

name: Miren Primary
description: Orange dwarf supporting a troubled pilgrimage colony whose public sanctity conceals deep internal corruption.

name: Miren
description: Holy colony with a damaged Primus-like biosphere, public shrines under constant observation, fortified strongholds, sealed districts, and undercities occupied by Phage cults.

name: Mercy
description: Moon of quarantine monasteries, military observation posts, and refugee settlements evacuated from compromised districts.

name: Miren Processional
description: Orbital pilgrim station still receiving arrivals despite repeated warnings that the colony is unsafe.

name: The Closed Choir
description: Isolation station holding infected pilgrims, suspected cult members, and biological samples under armed Choir supervision.

name: Sable
description: Dark mineral world with scattered towns, old extraction sites, and several communities that have cut contact with Choir authorities.

name: Vigil
description: Cold frontier world supporting watch stations, isolated monasteries, and growing numbers of displaced colonists.

name: Miren's Wake
description: Pale gas giant used as an outer-system anchorage by vessels unwilling to approach the infected colony directly.

name: Absolution
description: Outer moon containing sealed reliquaries, burial vaults, and a small order that refuses all visitors from Miren.

name: Evensong Primary
description: Cold brown dwarf surrounding the saint-mech crypts in deep darkness broken only by station lamps and reactor glow.

name: Requiem
description: Cold world of basalt plains, buried shelters, and scattered custodial settlements supporting the crypt moon.

name: Evensong
description: Saint-mech crypt moon holding ancient frames believed to retain echoes of holy pilots and battles remembered through ritual song.

name: Evensong Crypt
description: Buried and orbital crypt complex where relic mechs are preserved, touched by pilgrims, and awakened only under disputed ceremonial authority.

name: First Bell
description: Shrine station receiving pilgrims, recording vows, and preparing visitors for entry into the crypts.

name: Last Bell
description: Quiet outer shrine station where pilgrims reflect after leaving the crypt and where custodians watch for relic-related anomalies.

name: Eyral Primary
description: Stable yellow star supporting the Choir’s greatest permanent architectural undertaking.

name: Threshold
description: Warm inner world of eroded plateaus, abandoned settlements, and isolated pilgrim shelters.

name: Eyral
description: Half-cathedral world with a modified Primus-like biosphere, natural continents on one hemisphere, and sacred geometric scars opening into immense inhabited caverns on the other.

name: Nave
description: Moon used as a construction camp, quarry, and orbital staging ground during the cathedral-world’s centuries of excavation.

name: Sanctum
description: Small habitable moon of monasteries, gardens, and communities established by workers who never returned to the surface.

name: Eyral Crown
description: Orbital reception and procession complex through which most visitors enter the cathedral hemisphere.

name: Inner Choir
description: Deep planetary archive preserving architectural liturgies, excavation records, and the names of those lost during construction.

name: Solace
description: Ocean world with quiet island settlements and long traditions of hosting exhausted pilgrims after journeys through Eyral’s interior.

name: Measure
description: Dense rocky world with scattered extraction scars and little permanent population.

name: Vesper
description: Cold world of long twilight, wind-carved ridges, and small communities founded by contemplative sects.

name: Magnificat
description: Large gas giant whose auroras are visible from Eyral and incorporated into several major processional calendars.

name: Cantus
description: Outer moon occupied by a few shrines and a listening order that records fluctuations in the giant’s radio emissions.

name: Veyth Primary
description: Dim red dwarf supporting the Choir’s most ordinary and populous collection of family colonies.

name: Ember
description: Warm dry world of modest settlements, caravan routes, and old farming experiments that never became fully self-sufficient.

name: Veyth
description: Large red-banded gas giant around which the principal chant-colony moons orbit.

name: Hearth
description: Primary family colony with a stable Primus-like biosphere, broad agricultural valleys, schools, rehearsal halls, and dense multigenerational towns.

name: Lesson
description: Cooler colony moon known for academies, youth choirs, pilot training, and long communal apprenticeships.

name: Harvest
description: Oceanic colony moon producing food, medicinal cultures, and water for nearby settlements and passing fleet vessels.

name: Common Anchorage
description: Busy fleet anchorage where families transfer between ships and colonies without the solemnity expected at major pilgrimage sites.

name: Ashen
description: Dark mineral world with scattered work camps, old towns, and no single institution important enough to dominate local life.

name: Quietus
description: Cold world of sparse settlements, long winters, and communities known for reserved forms of chant and worship.

name: Wayfarer
description: Outer ice world used occasionally by passing flotillas but otherwise inhabited by only a few isolated families.

name: Grey Orison Primary
description: Faint stellar remnant whose cold light falls across a system where resonance and song are treated as dangerous.

name: Grey Orison
description: Airless inner world marked by old landing sites, sealed structures, and warning beacons that transmit only visual code.

name: Silenced Shrine
description: Shrine complex where singing, amplified speech, and resonance devices are forbidden following an event removed from most Choir records.

name: Custodian's Rest
description: Small low-noise habitat supporting the shrine’s custodians and the rare pilgrims permitted to remain overnight.

name: Dead Relay One
description: Unpowered relay station whose antennae occasionally move despite the absence of functioning control systems.

name: Orison
description: Cold outer world of gray ice, shallow canyons, and abandoned survey camps.

name: Dead Relay Two
description: Silent outer relay whose last surviving logs record an unexplained harmonic pattern and an order to cease all transmission.

name: The Listening Post
description: Minimal observation platform monitoring the system for unauthorized resonance, unexpected power signatures, and returning signals.

name: The Exodus
description: The Exodus is the mass evacuation event from Primus that occured nearly 1000 years ago. It was a time of chaos and death, before Guild licesned FTL travel and Manifold Engines.

name: Shrike-Class Gunship
visual: Broad-winged gunship with a narrow armored fuselage, recessed weapon mounts, and heat-dampened engines. Matte plating and sensor-baffling surfaces let it approach beneath most detection systems.
behavior: Close air support, covert insertion, and low-altitude strike operations.

name: Manifold Engine
description: A Manifold Engine is a Guild-built FTL drive that moves a vessel through charted corridors in the Manifold. Because the medium's geometry shifts continuously, deviation from an approved lane can strand, scatter, or destroy a ship.

name: Pelagos Union
description: The Pelagos Union was a democratic maritime federation whose economy and identity centered on ocean settlement and food production. The Phage consumed its territory, and all surviving lanes remain under quarantine. [LANE ACCESS REVOKED]

name: Damasine Rift
description: The Damasine Rift is the permanent Voidborn breach left at the center of the former Damasine Hegemony after its final attempt to collapse the opening failed. Its boundaries continue to degrade local reality, and all approaching Guild lanes have been severed.

name: Damasine Hegemony
description: The Damasine Hegemony was an authoritarian naval empire whose provincial rulers retained autonomy in exchange for taxes and military service. Its territory was erased by the Voidborn, leaving a permanent rift and severed lanes. [LANE ACCESS REVOKED]

name: Ilyr Consortium
description: The Ilyr Consortium was a decentralized commercial alliance that connected resource-rich systems with little shared law or culture. The Stellar Maw consumed its territory, and all former routes are closed. [LANE ACCESS REVOKED]

name: Psionics
description: Psionics are rare cognitive abilities associated with prolonged Resonance exposure but generated through an unknown mechanism distinct from Resonance itself. Natural cases are uncommon, while artificial induction often causes severe neurological damage, leaving the origin of the phenomenon unresolved.

name: Asterion Assembly
description: The Asterion Assembly was a federal industrial republic with strong local governments and one of the largest navies outside Guild control. Mim forces overran its systems, and the Guild revoked all lane access. [LANE ACCESS REVOKED]

name: Tyren
description: Tyren was a hereditary officer-state that paired centralized military rule with functioning civilian institutions. The Cerebrax assimilated its territory and incorporated its military knowledge into the Hivemind. [LANE ACCESS REVOKED]

name: Uldren Combine
description: The Uldren Combine was an industrial federation whose power rested on immense independent manufacturing capacity. The Cerebrax assimilated its population and turned its foundries against the remaining defense worlds. [LANE ACCESS REVOKED]

name: Serevine Republic
description: The Serevine Republic was a prosperous parliamentary state known for competent administration and a large professional navy. The Quicksilver Enigma destroyed its institutional trust, and its former territory remains quarantined. [LANE ACCESS REVOKED]

name: Tervan Covenant
description: The Tervan Covenant was a defensive alliance whose members retained separate governments while sharing a navy and foreign policy. Repeated Chrono-Jackal incursions left its former territory temporally unstable and inaccessible. [LANE ACCESS REVOKED]

name: Vannic Commonwealth
description: The Vannic Commonwealth was a stable parliamentary federation already strained by declining stellar output in its outer systems. The Basilica of Unborn Stars destroyed its inhabited worlds by igniting them from within. [LANE ACCESS REVOKED]

name: Taloran Directorate
description: The Taloran Directorate was a centralized technocratic state whose legitimacy rested on maintaining reliable infrastructure and public security. The Shepherd destabilized the gravitational structure of its systems, forcing the Guild to revoke access. [LANE ACCESS REVOKED]

name: Aurelian Synod
description: The Aurelian Synod was a federation of secular governments and religious institutions known for diplomacy and refugee relief. Nebulite harvesting erased its collective memory, and the former territory remains closed. [LANE ACCESS REVOKED]

name: Nacre Union
description: The Nacre Union was a decentralized manufacturing confederation built around cooperative production and strong local identity. Phage infestation and subsequent Voidborn incursions destroyed the Union, leaving its systems quarantined. [LANE ACCESS REVOKED]

name: Needle-Class Interceptor
visual: Narrow spindle-shaped craft with recessed engines, dark sensor plating, and an oversized communications array along its spine.
behavior: Long-range scout and courier. Observes enemy movements, carries priority dispatches, and withdraws before heavier ships can respond.
report_text: “Contact confirmed beyond the lane marker. The Needle delivered its report six hours before our own sensors found them.”

name: Lantern-Class Corvette
visual: Lean hull dominated by folding sensor masts and luminous detection vanes. Weapon mounts are small and widely spaced.
behavior: Fleet picket and reconnaissance ship. Detects ambushes, surveys unstable lanes, and extends the sensor range of larger formations.
report_text: “Lantern Three saw the raiders before they cleared the debris field. The convoy had already turned by the time they opened fire.”

name: Viper-Class Corvette
visual: Low-profile hull with angular heat sinks and paired torpedo tubes running nearly its entire length.
behavior: Torpedo ambusher. Hides near stations, debris fields, or lane exits before striking larger vessels at close range.
report_text: “No drive flare. No targeting lock. Just two torpedoes appearing out of the wreckage beneath us.”

name: Aegis-Class Frigate
visual: Broad wedge-shaped hull surrounded by clustered point-defense turrets. Its armor is thin except around engines and ammunition stores.
behavior: Dedicated fleet screen. Intercepts missiles, drones, and strike craft before they can reach carriers or capital ships.
report_text: “The sky between us and the carrier became solid gunfire. Nothing larger than scrap reached the flight deck.”

name: Veil-Class Frigate
visual: Smooth dark hull broken by antenna ridges and rotating resonance dishes. Its engine wake disperses into a faint haze rather than a bright trail.
behavior: Electronic warfare frigate. Scrambles targeting systems, creates false contacts, and conceals allied movements behind sensor interference.
report_text: “Tracking identified twelve cruisers. Visual confirmation found one frigate and empty space.”

name: Harpoon-Class Frigate
visual: Heavy forward hull fitted with grappling launchers, breaching clamps, and armored boarding tubes.
behavior: Capture and interdiction vessel. Disables engines, anchors fleeing ships, and delivers boarding teams into crippled targets.
report_text: “The clamps struck before the engines finished dying. Forty seconds later, their marines were cutting through the inner hatch.”

name: Longbow-Class Cruiser
visual: Slender cruiser built around a spinal resonance lance. Auxiliary gun decks sit far behind the reinforced prow.
behavior: Long-range artillery ship. Cripples priority targets before the main battle line closes, but performs poorly when surrounded.
report_text: “Range control called the shot impossible. The Longbow fired anyway. Enemy drive output ceased eight seconds later.”

name: Manticore-Class Cruiser
visual: Thick-backed hull covered in sealed missile cells. Its armored flanks unfold into layered launch racks during combat.
behavior: Missile cruiser. Saturates formations with guided ordnance and forces enemy point defenses to choose which threats to stop.
report_text: “Point defense eliminated four hundred contacts. The remaining eighty-seven were enough.”

name: Citadel-Class Cruiser
visual: Tall central superstructure surrounded by armored command decks, communications towers, and projecting resonance vanes.
behavior: Fleet coordination vessel. Directs squadrons, strengthens communications, and maintains formation cohesion during confused engagements.
report_text: “Comms failed across the formation, but every ship still received the Citadel clearly. The line never broke.”

name: Spearhead-Class Carrier
visual: Blunt armored carrier with forward-opening hangars and rows of atmospheric landing craft secured beneath its hull.
behavior: Planetary assault carrier. Delivers mechs, troops, and ground vehicles directly into defended landing zones.
report_text: “The prow entered the atmosphere under fire. Its first mech reached the ground before the carrier finished burning through the clouds.”

name: Atlas-Class Support Carrier
visual: Bulky segmented hull carrying detachable fuel tanks, ammunition vaults, and replacement components beneath an armored spine.
behavior: Fleet replenishment ship. Refuels vessels, replaces expended ordnance, and keeps extended campaigns supplied away from established ports.
report_text: “The fleet arrived empty. Six hours beside the Atlas and every magazine, tank, and launch rack was full again.”

name: Eclipse-Class Battlecruiser
visual: Long predatory hull with oversized engines and weapon batteries concentrated around its narrow prow.
behavior: Capital hunter. Uses superior speed to isolate cruisers and carriers, destroys them quickly, and disengages before dreadnoughts can respond.
report_text: “The Eclipse crossed our firing line, killed the carrier, and was already outside lance range when the escorts turned.”

name: Monolith-Class Dreadnought
visual: Enormous slab-sided vessel surrounded by layered armor belts, shield emitters, and dense point-defense towers.
behavior: Defensive fleet anchor. Protects nearby vessels, absorbs concentrated fire, and turns strategically important positions into nearly immovable fortresses.
report_text: “We spent nine hours trying to move it from the gate. The Monolith did not alter course by a single degree.”

name: Cistern-Class Freighter
visual: A reinforced central spine surrounded by rows of spherical storage tanks. Emergency bulkheads divide the vessel into dozens of sealed sections.
behavior: Transports fuel, water, industrial gases, and other volatile cargo between systems. Commonly travels in heavily guarded convoys.
report_text: “One tank ruptured and froze half the hull. The remaining compartments held long enough to save the colony.”

name: Wayfarer-Class Liner
visual: Long utilitarian hull lined with compact habitation blocks and rotating gravity sections. Exterior decoration is limited to registry markings and destination banners.
behavior: Mass passenger and colony transport. Carries thousands in austere conditions on routes too dangerous or unprofitable for luxury liners.
report_text: “There were twelve of us to a compartment and one window on the entire deck. Nobody complained when the new sun appeared.”

name: Wrecker-Class Barge
visual: Open-framed vessel fitted with cutting arms, magnetic cranes, storage cages, and clamps large enough to hold broken warships.
behavior: Salvage and recovery platform. Retrieves wrecks, stranded mechs, and damaged vessels from battlefields before pirates or scavengers arrive.
report_text: “The cruiser was split through the middle. The Wrecker brought back both halves and sixteen survivors.”

name: Prospector-Class Barge
visual: Industrial hull wrapped around drills, refinery drums, ore grinders, and detachable mining craft.
behavior: Mobile extraction platform. Mines asteroids and small moons, processes raw material, and supplies isolated colonies or fleet foundries.
report_text: “The rock entered the forward grinders at dawn. By the next shift, the refinery was loading usable alloy.”

name: Hadran
description: Hadran was a bureaucratic federation governed through elected ministries and a large professional civil service. Nullary erased the state from reality, and its former systems remain under memetic quarantine.

name: Ferrith War
description: The Ferrith War began when the Luthan League tried to impose tariffs and inspection rights on Kestrel merchant routes near Ferrith. The settlement opened Ferrith to League access while preserving Kestrel control over several independent routes.

name: Deyros War
description: The Deyros War grew from repeated Orak raids into a sustained campaign across Deyros and Harrier Field. Crown forces destroyed several anchorages but failed to eliminate the mobile syndicate fleets, leading to the fortified patrol network that still defines the region.

name: Braxis Border War
description: The Braxis Border War began when Damasine expansion entered systems claimed by the Cindral March. Cindral retained Braxis Hold but lost several outer colonies, leaving the frontier militarized until the Hegemony's destruction.

name: Pelagos Trade War
description: The Pelagos Trade War was fought over League attempts to control Pelagos food exports and shipping insurance. Pelagos preserved its commercial independence but granted League firms preferred access to major markets.

name: Shivra War
description: The Shivra War began when Karnate attempted to seize mineral systems supporting Uldren heavy industry. Karnate secured the Shivra Belt but failed to overcome the Combine's ability to replace its losses.

name: Veyra Corridor War
description: The Veyra Corridor War grew from disputes over pilgrimage authority and taxation along a shared religious route. Its settlement divided administration of the corridor between Aurelian and Veyran authorities.

name: Taloran-Halix Border War
description: The Taloran-Halix Border War began over Compact surveillance stations near Directorate traffic routes and mutual accusations of reconnaissance. The settlement divided the frontier into monitored exclusion zones.

name: Asterion Civil War
description: The Asterion Civil War began when Karnate-backed separatists seized industrial stations within Assembly territory. Asterion preserved its core systems, but Karnate annexed several resource worlds and emerged with a larger fleet.

name: Red Vale War
description: The Red Vale War was a Karnate attempt to seize frontier systems controlling Cindral ore routes. Karnate captured the outer systems but abandoned the offensive after severe losses against entrenched March defenses.

name: Ilyr Mining War
description: The Ilyr Mining War began when the Luthan League asserted ownership over newly surveyed deposits inside Consortium territory. The settlement established shared extraction rights while leaving compensation claims unresolved.

name: Seldran War
description: The Seldran War was a sector-wide Crown civil war triggered by the collapse of Seldran's royal succession and the intervention of outside houses supporting rival claimants. The intervening powers withdrew without establishing a stable government, leaving House de Noctixuan as the nominal authority over a divided realm.

name: Second Braxis War
description: The Second Braxis War was a Damasine invasion intended to break the Cindral March and secure the Mawward approaches. Repeated sieges failed to produce a decisive victory, leaving both powers weakened before the destruction of the Hegemony.

name: Vannic Tariff War
description: The Vannic Tariff War began as a dispute over transit fees and escalated into convoy seizures and limited naval combat. Vannic secured reduced tariffs in exchange for League oversight at selected ports.

name: Greyspan War
description: The Greyspan War was a Crown-Cindral attempt to destroy the pirate state centered on Greyspan Station. Coalition losses forced a withdrawal before the citadel fell, leaving Greyspan damaged but independent.

name: First Core War
description: The First Core War was a struggle for control of early Resonance Core sites and production methods, fought with unstable prototypes and sabotage. First Contact forced the major powers into a ceasefire, though many Core facilities remained disputed.

name: Asterion Refugee Crisis
description: The Asterion Refugee Crisis began when Halix closed Silent Way checkpoints to civilians fleeing early Mim attacks and Assembly escorts tried to force passage. Asterion redirected the refugees rather than continue the fighting, deepening the isolation that preceded its destruction.

name: Miren Intervention
description: The Miren Intervention began when Halix demanded inspections of Veyran ships after evidence of cult activity and contamination. The dispute ended with joint screening stations established outside the system.

name: Vask Gate Conflict
description: The Vask Gate Conflict began when Orak raiders seized bonded cargo vessels awaiting League inspection. Retaliatory strikes ended the fighting within weeks but disrupted trade throughout the Ferrith Sector.

name: Silent Way War
description: The Silent Way War began when Halix closed parts of the corridor during Mim scares and Veyran flotillas continued moving pilgrims and refugees through the restricted systems. A genuine Mim incursion forced Halix, Veyran, and Cindral forces to end the war and cooperate.

name: Drossfall Campaign
description: The Drossfall Campaign followed Halix accusations that Karnate was conducting unsafe Resonance experiments near the Silent Way. Karnate resistance turned the dispute into raids and sabotage around quarantine infrastructure without escalating into a full invasion.

name: Greyspan Intervention
description: The Greyspan Intervention was a second coalition attempt to suppress pirate attacks from the Greyspan citadel. The blockade ended when rising external threats forced Crown and Cindral fleets to redeploy.

name: Eyral Standoff
description: The Eyral Standoff began when Crown explorers claimed an ancient Frame that Veyran authorities considered sacred. After eleven days at combat readiness, the Crown withdrew rather than challenge the Choir blockade.

name: Second Crown-Karnate War
description: The Second Crown-Karnate War grew from frontier raids into the largest post-contact conflict between surviving human powers. Heavy losses and external attacks ended the war without territorial resolution.

name: Haven Rock Conflict
description: The Haven Rock Conflict began when League-backed companies tried to enforce debt claims against independent miners. Luthan security forces withdrew after Orak syndicates supported the local resistance.

name: Pale Hinge Crisis
description: The Pale Hinge Crisis began when Halix detained a Veyran pilgrim flotilla after failed memory screenings. The confrontation ended without combat when the affected ships accepted extended quarantine.

name: Breakwater War
description: The Breakwater War followed repeated Karnate incursions into restricted space that Cindral interpreted as preparations for invasion. Three years of fleet action changed no borders but drove both factions to expand their fortifications.

name: Black Runnel Raids
description: The Black Runnel Raids are an ongoing series of Crown and Luthan operations against smugglers using the corridor, answered by Orak attacks on trade and customs traffic. The participants continue the conflict without formally recognizing it as a war.

name: The Asterion War
description: The Asterion War was the first full-scale Mim invasion, using direct attacks and cognitive manipulation to destroy the Assembly's ability to trust its own forces. Asterion's final defense ended after six days of continuous combat, when every remaining transmission collapsed into a single repeating distress call.

name: The Tervan War
description: The Tervan War was a Chrono-Jackal campaign repeatedly restarted from earlier points in the conflict, allowing each assault to exploit knowledge stolen from previous versions. Tervan destroyed the temporal siphons in several timelines but failed in the surviving one, leaving contradictory debris fields that later attracted Chronodrakes.

name: The Serevine Civil War
description: The Serevine Civil War began after the Quicksilver Enigma infiltrated the Republic and turned reasonable security measures into competing purges and civil conflict. The surviving government destroyed its own capital after concluding that neither its institutions nor evacuation ships could be trusted.

name: The Uldren Assimilation
description: The Uldren Assimilation was a war of industrial attrition against Cerebrax forces that converted captured personnel and infrastructure into extensions of the Hivemind. Uldren's own foundries eventually produced the fleets that destroyed its remaining defense worlds.

name: The Tyren Assimilation
description: The Tyren Assimilation began when Cerebrax forces crossed from former Uldren territory and reorganized under commands attributed to the Omni-Cognate. Tyren's leadership died defending the capital, and its military knowledge was absorbed into later Cerebrax formations.

name: The Consumption of Pelagos
description: The Consumption of Pelagos began when Phage contamination spread through relief traffic and reached the Union's ocean worlds. Twelve years of containment ended with synchronized planetary blooms that consumed the remaining population and evacuation fleets.

name: The Erasure of Nacre
description: The Erasure of Nacre began as a successful war against the Phage until massed Resonance weapons opened dimensional fractures across the theater. Voidborn incursions and renewed infestation overwhelmed the Union before evacuation could be completed.

name: The Aurelian War
description: The Aurelian War was a sixteen-year resistance against Nebulite harvesting that stripped worlds of personal and institutional memory. The surviving population retained routine skills but no longer remembered the Synod, their families, or the war.

name: The Unmaking of Vannic
description: The Unmaking of Vannic began when the Basilica of Unborn Stars implanted stellar embryos in Commonwealth worlds under the appearance of restoring a dying system. Vannic territory is now a field of malformed stars burning where inhabited planets once existed.

name: The Erasure of Damasine
description: The Erasure of Damasine was a retreating war against a Voidborn breach that widened with every engagement and consumed the structure of occupied systems. The Hegemony's final attempt to collapse the original fracture destroyed its remaining fleet but left the breach intact.

name: The Evacuation of Ilyr
description: The Evacuation of Ilyr was a mass civilian withdrawal conducted as the Stellar Maw destabilized every major Consortium system. Fewer than one percent of registered citizens escaped, and many surviving fleets were later lured back by false distress signals.

name: The Hadran Incident
description: The Hadran Incident began when a Nullary statement erased a transport from reality and spread through the federation's records. On the eighth day, a final transmission declared that Hadran had always been empty, leaving no surviving evidence to contradict it.

name: The Bread Bell
description: A large, sentient, resonance artifact. The artifact resembles an ancient bell of old Primus, covered in oxidized copper and inscribed with unknown glyphs written in an indecipherable alien language. The bell itself has proven impervious to all tested means of destruction; high yield explosives, ship-grade resonance canons, and even Voidborn exposure. Instead, when it is struck it emits a deep gonging noise that carries even in the vacuum of space. Any living thing that hears it is instantaneously and immediately transformed into an archaic old Primus electrical kitchen appliance made for heating up individual slices of bread. Even listening to a recording of the sound is enough to transform the listener. Discussions have been had on utilizing this artifact as a weapon, however this has proven to be impractical if not impossible as the bell with occasionally ring unprompted or spontaneously teleport to a new terrestrial location seemingly at random.

name: Courtesy Phone
description: An antique red rotary telephone from old Primus that manifests in abandoned buildings, derelict ships, sealed bunkers, and other locations where no functioning communications infrastructure remains. The telephone will ring continuously until answered. A calm voice on the other end identifies itself only as “Assistance” and asks whether the listener requires help. Any request spoken into the receiver is fulfilled immediately, regardless of scale or physical possibility. Requests for food have buried colonies beneath billions of ration packs. Requests for rescue have teleported settlements into the interiors of inhabited stations. Requests to destroy an enemy have resulted in entire bloodlines being retroactively removed from history. Once the request has been fulfilled, Assistance asks the caller to return the favor, giving a request in return. Those that fail to complete said favor are reported missing within the hour and whatever previous request was made is undone. If this object is observed, it is to be reported to the nearest Guild authority immediately. Do not interact.

name: House de Aurelong
heraldry: A radiant golden dragon coiled around a star on a field of white.
description: House de Aurelong rules the Crown Sector and traditionally presides over the Crown Council as the Concordant's principal advocate of unity and legitimate succession. Its influence rests on diplomacy and control of chivalric legitimacy rather than direct rule over the other dukes.

name: House di Solming
description: The military lords of Velbrant, descended from fortress commanders and tournament marshals. They maintain the Grand Lists, Whitefire Array, and several of the Crown’s most prestigious knight academies.

name: House de Cereslin
description: The agricultural dynasty of Hallowmere. Its wealth comes from grain reserves, seed vaults, managed oceans, and the power to decide which sectors receive food during shortages.

name: House da Ruberwei
description: A hardened border family based in Kaelith. Known for their patrol fleets and a deep resentment of nobles who speak confidently about frontiers they have never visited.

name: House di Valeming
heraldry: A silver shield on a deep green field, displaying a rising sun.
description: House di Valeming rules the Althoren Sector through a deeply feudal network of minor baronies bound by service obligations. It supports de Aurelong leadership while resisting central control, and its greatest vulnerability is the narrow lane network connecting its scattered agricultural holdings.

name: House de Noctixuan
heraldry: A black field with a pale crescent moon, with faint silver stars scattered across the background.
description: House de Noctixuan is the nominal ruler of the divided Seldran Sector and the custodian of its succession records. By controlling the evidence of legitimate lineage, it turns genealogy into political authority while rival claimants remain unable to form a stable government.

name: House da Ferruwei
heraldry: A crimson field displaying a flaming hammer, with golden sparks scattering outward like small stars.
description: House da Ferruwei governs the Bastrel Sector as the Crown's principal frontier military-industrial power. Its authority grew by converting unpaid wartime debts into territorial and political control, making the Concordant increasingly dependent on Ferruwei production.

name: House de Limeshan
heraldry: A divided field of ash gray and dark blue, crossed by a jagged white lightning bolt.
description: House de Limeshan governs the exposed Deyros frontier, where weak central authority and constant raiding require permanent military readiness. Its rule rests on patrols and rapid retaliation, earning it a reputation for severity among the safer interior houses.

name: Crown Sector
description: The Crown Sector is the political and ceremonial center of the Concordant, linking Ardane’s council chambers and noble estates with Velbrant’s fortress infrastructure, Hallowmere’s agricultural reserves, and Kaelith’s border defenses. Diplomacy, food production, and military prestige are concentrated close enough that instability in any one system quickly affects the entire Concordant.

name: Althoren Sector
description: Althoren is a fortified agrarian corridor connecting Braelyn Hold, Kether Vale’s farms, and the transit infrastructure of High Alder Span. The sector supplies food and strategic depth to the Crown interior, but its scattered baronies and dependence on a single lane bridge make reinforcement slower than its military planners prefer.

name: Seldran Sector
description: Seldran is a politically fractured region of ruined dynasties. Duris preserves the remains of a fallen royal order, Marnholt continues to divide itself among competing banners, and Sable Crown provides displaced nobles with the intelligence and resources needed to keep old disputes alive.

name: Bastrel Sector
description: Bastrel is the Concordant’s principal expansion and mobilization sector. Armies, knight frames, supplies, and threat reports move constantly through the region, often under several noble commands whose authority overlaps during major deployments.

name: Deyros Sector
description: Deyros is a violent frontier sector. Deyros provides the settlements and civil authority, Harrier Field hunts Orak raiders, and the Black Runnel allows smugglers and hostile fleets to bypass the borders both systems are intended to defend.

name: Luthan Sector
description: The Luthan Sector is the administrative and commercial center of the League. Law, finance, diplomacy, research, and mercenary contracting are so tightly connected that decisions made in one system are often owned, insured, or litigated in another.

name: Ferrith Sector
description: Ferrith is a market-facing sector where the improvised commerce of Ferrith Hub, the luxury industries of Rynnel, and the inspections of Vask Gate represent different stages of the same trade network. Goods may enter through tightly controlled customs facilities, be financed or resold in asteroid bazaars, and ultimately reach the private resorts and high-status markets that generate much of the sector’s profit.

name: Ceyra Sector
description: Ceyra is a fuel and logistics sector built around atmospheric extraction, refinery infrastructure, tanker construction, convoy assembly, and the unofficial commerce of New Ulbar.

name: Meyric Sector
description: Meyric is the League’s principal exotic-material and specialist manufacturing region. Valuable substances move through competing claims, laboratories, courts, and free-trade chambers before becoming experimental weapons, frame components, or private intellectual property.

name: Tovresh Sector
description: Tovresh organizes the movement and protection of League commerce through its escort yards, navigator guilds, signal stations, and massive warehouses.

name: Karnate Sector
description: The Karnate Sector is the regime’s political and industrial heart, joining the furnace worlds and ruling citadels of Dross Forge to Shivra’s hazardous mining operations and the press-gang infrastructure of Roughline. Raw material, labor, and weapons flow through the sector as parts of a single production system.

name: Rathmar Sector
description: Rathmar is a heavily optimized military-production sector. Materials mined under dangerous conditions are refined into war materiel and tested against disposable cities, fortifications, and assigned populations before entering active service.

name: Ironfall Sector
description: Ironfall forms Karnate’s fortified strategic reserve, combining the siege shipyards, weapons laboratories, and the layered defenses. Fleets can be repaired, experimental equipment tested, and approaches sealed behind minefields without exposing the more valuable industrial systems deeper within Karnate territory.

name: Orak Sector
description: The Orak Sector is a mobile and loosely governed center of mercenary trade, salvage, ship repair, and nomadic habitation. Orak Station provides the largest common marketplace, Korran Drift carries communities that refuse permanent settlement, and Slate Cradle keeps their fleets operational by rebuilding vessels that most would classify as wreckage.

name: Drail Sector
description: Drail is a politically unstable sector where pirate leadership, independent mining communities, and covert intelligence networks coexist without a single officially recognized government. It is considered to be under Orak control.

name: Greyspan Sector
description: Greyspan is a hostile salvage and fortress region centered on the neutron-star defenses of Greyspan Station, with Spindle Rock’s infested mines and Ash Rack’s burned ruins occupying the surrounding routes. Pirate power is strongest near the citadel, but much of the sector belongs in practice to scavengers, vermin, and automated defenses.

name: Cindral Sector
description: The Cindral Sector is the administrative and defensive core of the March, connecting the declining capital system to the fortress network at Braxis Hold and the infrastructure of Red Choir. Government continuity, military efforts, and civilian survival are distributed between the three so that the loss of any single system does not immediately destroy the March.

name: Ashveil Sector
description: Ashveil is a thinly held frontier sector linking the Mawward March to the Silent Way through observation stations, reserve settlements, and abandoned colonial infrastructure.

name: Halix Sector
description: The Halix Sector is the Compact’s primary civil and psychological defense region, joining the government and verification infrastructure of Halix to the watch stations of Crowthorne and the layered checkpoint system at Pale Hinge. Information is deliberately compared between systems so that hallucinations, compromised testimony, or altered memories cannot pass unchallenged through a single authority.

name: Kryne Sector
description: Kryne is the Compact’s specialist containment and analysis sector. Personnel, evidence, ships, and ideas move through separate institutions designed to observe one another as closely as they observe the threats under study.

name: Veyran Sector
description: The Veyran Sector forms the primary entrance to the Choir Path, linking the pilgrimage centers of Veyra with the monastic shipyards of Low Cantor and the penitential checkpoints of Hush Gate. Pilgrims and fleet communities are screened at the frontier, transported in vessels that are treated like sacred objects, and drawn toward the shrines and processions of the Choir’s spiritual heart.

name: Choral Sector
description: Choral is the Choir’s most spiritually powerful and internally dangerous sector. Sacred relics, resonance research, and cult activity overlap throughout the sector, making it a center of faith that must also be treated as a potential containment region.

name: Eyral Sector
description: Eyral contains both monumental and ordinary sides of Choir civilization. Pilgrimage, domestic life, and culture is sustained as much by settled families and working colonies as by its greatest sacred sites.

name: Pelion Sector
description: Pelion contains a loose chain of ancient red dwarfs surrounded by metal-poor rocky worlds, frozen moons, and tidally locked planets with little usable atmosphere. Several independent ice-mining settlements operate beneath the crust of Pelion Reach, supported by a rotating habitat that serves as the sector’s only dependable market and repair port.

name: Tianlu Sector
description: Tianlu is a young stellar region dominated by hot blue-white stars, intense ultraviolet radiation, and massive gas giants that formed before stable terrestrial worlds could develop. Automated observatories track the rapid evolution of its stars, though their data is collected remotely because long-term habitation would require shielding and maintenance costs far beyond the sector’s practical value.

name: Far Meridian Sector
description: The systems of Far Meridian are separated by unusually wide interstellar distances, leaving only two weak Guild-compatible routes through the region. A handful of independent refueling stations survive by servicing survey ships and long-range prospectors, with months of travel separating one inhabited installation from the next.

name: Shenzhou Drift
description: Shenzhou Drift consists primarily of rogue planets, failed stars, and cold objects moving between recognized systems without a common stellar center. Most bodies retain only thin frozen atmospheres or subsurface layers of exotic ice, and their changing positions make permanent lane infrastructure impractical.

name: Dorian Sector
description: Dorian’s low-mass stars possess numerous rocky planets, though most are too small to retain atmosphere or surface water. Independent communities inhabit sealed cylinders above the mineral world Corda, exporting precision metals through a cooperative port whose council rejects outside sovereignty and limits permanent immigration.

name: Anthelion Sector
description: Anthelion is dominated by eccentric binary and trinary systems whose planets experience severe orbital variation, periodic atmospheric loss, and unpredictable bombardment from displaced debris. Surveys have identified several resource-rich worlds, but none offers a stable environment for settlements that must operate for generations rather than mining seasons.

name: Rimeward Sector
description: Rimeward is a cold region of dim stars, ice giants, frozen terrestrial worlds, and moons warmed only by tidal stress. Small independent settlements occupy geothermal caverns beneath the moon Varin, where local cooperatives harvest volatiles and biological compounds from a deep subsurface ocean.

name: Cresset Sector
description: Cresset contains several white dwarfs surrounded by stripped planetary cores, irradiated debris belts, and the remnants of worlds consumed during their stars’ natural expansion. The region contains valuable heavy elements, though radiation exposure, limited fuel sources, and violent debris environments have prevented permanent extraction.

name: Nanshi Shoals
description: Dense asteroid families and partially formed planetary systems fill the Nanshi Shoals, where young stars remain surrounded by dust, rubble, and unstable orbital clusters. Independent prospectors maintain temporary camps inside larger asteroids, relocating whenever collisions, orbital shifts, or exhausted claims make their current holdings untenable.

name: Vesper Plain Sector
description: Vesper Plain occupies a broad region of unusually low stellar density containing only scattered brown dwarfs and isolated red stars. Its systems lack concentrated mineral deposits, habitable planets, and convenient route junctions, leaving the sector as a long navigational void between more useful territories.

name: Yanshen Sector
description: A powerful magnetar dominates Yanshen, saturating the surrounding systems with periodic radiation bursts and magnetic disturbances capable of disabling insufficiently shielded vessels. No stable planets orbit close to the central star, while the outer systems contain little beyond cold gas giants and irregular moons.

name: Caradene Sector
description: Caradene contains several temperate worlds whose atmospheres are chemically incompatible with human life, requiring sealed settlements despite otherwise moderate climates. The independent colony of New Caradene occupies a chain of elevated habitats above a dense chlorine sea and survives through pharmaceutical exports, atmospheric chemistry, and strict control of imported population.

name: Lumen Verge
description: Lumen Verge lies inside a thick interstellar dust cloud that obscures local stars, weakens long-range observation, and interferes with optical navigation. The few planetary systems identified within the cloud are cold and underdeveloped, with low solar output and no known worlds capable of supporting open settlement.

name: Qilin Reach
description: Qilin Reach contains several large ocean worlds covered beneath hundreds of kilometers of high-pressure ice. Independent research habitats operate around the moon Xiang, studying extremophile ecosystems and pressure-formed minerals while relying on imported food, machinery, and reactor fuel.

name: Pavan Sector
description: Most Pavan systems contain gas giants, small airless moons, and little accessible heavy industry. The independent station Pavan Cross functions as a neutral transfer point for explorers, religious travelers, and long-distance freight crews, supported by docking fees rather than local production.

name: Helian Waste
description: Helian Waste consists of old, low-metallicity stars formed before heavier elements became common in the region. Their systems contain gas, ice, and small mineral-poor bodies, offering little material for industry and almost no planetary environments worth the cost of settlement.

name: Pelion Reach System
description: Pelion Reach is a dim red-dwarf system centered on the frozen moon Nemea, where independent mining settlements occupy geothermal caverns beneath several kilometers of ice. The rotating habitat Lantern Wheel serves as the sector’s main market, repair yard, and meeting place for communities too small to maintain separate heavy industry.

name: Red Cairn System
description: Red Cairn contains three tidally locked rocky worlds orbiting an ancient, metal-poor star, none of which possesses a stable atmosphere. The innermost planet exposes unusual mantle formations along its permanent twilight band, drawing geological expeditions despite the absence of commercially valuable deposits.

name: Tianlu Crown System
description: Tianlu Crown is a young blue-white star surrounded by massive gas giants, radiant dust rings, and several scorched planetary embryos still undergoing heavy bombardment. Remote observatories use the system to study early planetary formation, transmitting data through hardened relay buoys positioned far beyond the primary’s worst radiation.

name: Baixing System
description: Baixing is a hot binary system whose two stars strip material from one another and produce irregular ultraviolet flares. Its outer gas giant possesses an enormous ring system visible across several astronomical units, though the radiation environment prevents anything more permanent than automated monitoring stations.

name: Meridian Cross System
description: Meridian Cross is the only reliable junction between Far Meridian’s two weak Guild-compatible routes. Its central refueling station, Crossway, supports long-range prospectors, survey vessels, and independent couriers through fuel cracking, hull repair, and rented cryogenic storage.

name: Last Measure System
description: Last Measure is a cold red-dwarf system whose outer moon hosts a small navigational community responsible for maintaining the final calibrated beacon before the sector’s longest transit gap. The settlement survives on route fees and emergency assistance, with most residents belonging to families who have maintained the beacon for generations.

name: Shenzhou Anchor System
description: Shenzhou Anchor is a failed star that has captured several rogue planets into wide, unstable orbits. The largest body carries a deep layer of exotic ice beneath a nitrogen crust, making it a useful reference point for navigators even though no permanent installation operates there.

name: Heiyu Cluster
description: Heiyu Cluster is a temporary association of six rogue worlds traveling along similar vectors through interstellar space. Their relative positions change slowly enough to permit periodic survey missions, but the cluster will disperse over the next several thousand years.

name: Corda System
description: Corda is a mineral system of small rocky worlds and airless moons surrounding a stable red dwarf. Sealed cylindrical habitats above Corda-II house the sector’s largest independent population, supported by precision-metal workshops and a cooperative port that tightly controls permanent immigration.

name: Finecut System
description: Finecut is an asteroid-rich system whose independent workshops specialize in low-volume components, surgical instruments, and high-tolerance machine parts. Its settlements are distributed among hollowed rocks and linked by scheduled freight tugs rather than permanent passenger routes.

name: Anthelion Triple System
star_type: Class F (White) + Class K (Orange Dwarf) + Class M (Red Dwarf)
description: Anthelion is a trinary system whose shifting stellar alignments produce severe seasonal extremes across its surviving planets. The resource-rich world Anthelion-IV repeatedly loses portions of its atmosphere during close orbital passages, preventing any permanent settlement from surviving without constant reconstruction.

name: Skewglass System
star_type: Class K (Orange Dwarf) + Class M (Red Dwarf)
description: Skewglass contains a rocky planet trapped in a highly eccentric orbit around a close binary pair. Its surface alternates between centuries of deep freeze and brief periods of intense melting, leaving vast glass plains where mineral-rich floods repeatedly evaporate.

name: Varin System
description: Varin is a cold gas-giant system whose tidally heated moon contains a deep subsurface ocean and extensive geothermal caverns. Independent cooperatives operate beneath the ice, harvesting biological compounds and volatile chemicals while maintaining strict limits on drilling near native ecosystems.

name: Pale Hearth System
description: Pale Hearth is a brown-dwarf system centered on a modest refueling colony built inside the hollowed moon Cask. The settlement processes hydrogen and deuterium from surrounding ice bodies, supplying isolated communities that cannot afford regular League tanker service.

name: Cresset Remnant System
description: Cresset Remnant surrounds a white dwarf with the exposed cores of several planets destroyed during the star’s expansion. Heavy metals are abundant across the debris belts, but intense radiation and high-velocity fragments make permanent extraction uneconomical.

name: Sable Core System
description: Sable Core contains a dense metallic planet whose outer layers were stripped away when its star entered the giant phase. The remaining world rotates rapidly and produces a magnetic field strong enough to interfere with navigation throughout the inner system.

name: Nanshi Crown System
description: Nanshi Crown is a young orange-star system surrounded by dense asteroid families and several partially formed worlds. Independent prospectors maintain mobile camps inside the larger rocks, while the station Crown Camp serves as a temporary exchange for claims, fuel, and collision forecasts.

name: Lantern Shoal System
description: Lantern Shoal is an unstable protoplanetary system where glowing dust clouds and frequent impacts make optical navigation unusually difficult. A chain of independent beacon stations marks the safest passages, relocating whenever orbital changes render their previous positions unsafe.

name: Vesper Null System
description: Vesper Null consists of a solitary brown dwarf with two cold gas giants and a sparse family of irregular moons. It is chiefly notable as a navigational landmark in a region where comparable reference points may be several light-years apart.

name: Candle End System
description: Candle End is a dying red dwarf orbited by a single frozen terrestrial world and a distant debris ring. The star emits too little energy to support practical settlement, though its predictable output makes the system useful for calibrating long-range instruments.

name: Yanshen System
description: Yanshen is dominated by a magnetar whose periodic bursts saturate the surrounding region with radiation and magnetic interference. Its few surviving planets follow distant, distorted orbits, and all observation is conducted through expendable probes launched between flare cycles.

name: Black Reed System
description: Black Reed lies near the outer edge of Yanshen’s magnetic influence and contains a cold gas giant with a long chain of narrow, irregular moons. Their mineral composition is unremarkable, but their orbital motion provides useful data on the magnetar’s long-term gravitational effects.

name: New Caradene System
description: New Caradene orbits a temperate yellow star and contains several worlds with dense, chemically hostile atmospheres. Elevated sealed habitats above Caradene-II’s chlorine seas form the sector’s largest colony, exporting pharmaceuticals, industrial catalysts, and atmospheric-processing expertise.

name: Palisade Sea System
description: Palisade Sea contains a warm ocean world beneath an atmosphere rich in sulfur compounds and corrosive aerosols. Independent researchers occupy shielded platforms above the cloud layer, studying extremophile life and testing materials intended for hostile-atmosphere construction.

name: Lumen Deep System
description: Lumen Deep is embedded within the densest portion of the sector’s interstellar dust cloud, leaving its red dwarf almost invisible beyond the system boundary. Its planets are cold, dark, and difficult to survey, with navigation dependent on radio beacons deployed by temporary scientific expeditions.

name: Blindstar System
description: Blindstar contains a dim brown dwarf surrounded by frozen moons and dust-darkened debris. The system is notable for a broad region of electrically charged particles that distort optical and radar returns without posing any direct biological threat.

name: Xiang System
description: Xiang is an ocean-world system whose inhabited research habitats orbit a tidally heated moon beneath hundreds of kilometers of high-pressure ice. Scientists study extremophile ecosystems and unusual pressure-formed minerals while relying on imported food, reactor components, and replacement machinery.

name: Longwater System
description: Longwater contains two massive ocean worlds with deep atmospheres and no exposed land. Independent survey stations operate in high orbit, deploying pressure-resistant probes into the upper seas and recovering biological samples from depths unreachable by crewed vessels.

name: Pavan Cross System
description: Pavan Cross is a quiet gas-giant system whose primary station serves as a neutral transfer point for explorers, pilgrims, and long-distance freight crews. Its economy depends on docking fees, cargo exchange, basic repairs, and the continued willingness of larger powers to ignore it.

name: Aster Vale System
description: Aster Vale contains several small airless moons and a thin asteroid belt with modest deposits of industrial metals. A loose community of independent prospectors operates from the station Valehouse, using Pavan Cross for heavy repairs and external trade.

name: Helian Oldlight System
description: Helian Oldlight is an ancient, low-metallicity star surrounded by small gas worlds, frozen moons, and mineral-poor rocky bodies. The system offers an unusually clear example of planetary formation before heavy elements became common, making it scientifically valuable despite its negligible commercial worth.

name: Dust Testament System
description: Dust Testament contains a dim red star and a broad disk of fine silicate material that never accumulated into full planets. Automated surveys have found little iron, nickel, or other useful metals, leaving the system untouched except for occasional astronomical missions.

name: Pelion
description: An old, dim red dwarf whose low output leaves most of the system frozen.

name: Brontes
description: A tidally locked, metal-poor inner world with a narrow band of fractured basalt along its terminator.

name: Acastus
description: A cold blue gas giant whose deep atmosphere provides the system’s main source of hydrogen and deuterium.

name: Nemea
description: A frozen moon with a tidally heated subsurface ocean and geothermal caverns occupied by independent ice-mining settlements.

name: Thyrsus
description: A bright ice moon used for volatile extraction and long-term storage.

name: Dione
description: A small outer world covered by nitrogen frost and ancient impact basins.

name: Lerna Belt
description: A sparse outer belt of cometary bodies that supplies water and reaction mass to Lantern Wheel.

name: Red Cairn
description: An ancient, low-metallicity red dwarf with weak flaring and little remaining protoplanetary material.

name: Ashward
description: A tidally locked world whose dayside is a plain of dark volcanic stone and whose nightside holds permanent carbon-dioxide frost.

name: Cairnfall
description: A dry, cratered planet with no atmosphere and unusually low concentrations of iron and nickel.

name: Gloam
description: The system’s most geologically interesting world, exposing deep mantle material along a fractured twilight zone.

name: Ember Scatter
description: A thin ring of mineral-poor rubble left from bodies that never completed formation.

name: Tianlu Crown
description: A young blue-white primary producing intense ultraviolet radiation and a powerful stellar wind.

name: Scoria
description: A scorched planetary embryo with a partially molten surface and frequent impacts.

name: Yuhuo
description: A hot, airless world surrounded by a cloud of recently ejected debris.

name: Radiant Throne
description: A massive gas giant encircled by luminous dust and ice rings visible throughout the inner system.

name: Chime
description: A radiation-darkened moon whose surface ice fluoresces during stellar storms.

name: Luoxing
description: A young moon with ongoing cryovolcanism and a heavily fractured crust.

name: Azure Crown
description: A hot outer gas giant with bright ammonia clouds and a broad family of minor moons.

name: Tianlu Nursery
description: A broad outer region of dust, gas, and planetary embryos still undergoing active accretion.

name: Baixing A
description: The hotter member of a close binary pair, drawing material from its companion.

name: Baixing B
description: A bright white companion distorted by mass transfer and irregular ultraviolet flares.

name: Meltwake
description: A half-molten inner world whose surface is repeatedly resurfaced by stellar heating.

name: Luminous
description: A ringed gas giant with a reflective upper atmosphere and a magnetosphere intensified by the binary stars.

name: Shard
description: A bright moon whose exposed ice is steadily darkening under ultraviolet bombardment.

name: Bailu
description: A fractured moon containing deep deposits of hydrated minerals.

name: Far Lantern
description: A distant frozen world that spends much of its orbit beyond the binary’s strongest radiation.

name: Meridian
description: A stable orange dwarf used as the principal navigation reference for Far Meridian.

name: Gauge
description: A small inner world covered in long, parallel rift valleys used for gravimetric calibration.

name: Orison
description: A hydrogen-rich gas giant that supplies the Crossway refueling station.

name: Fuelwell
description: A volatile-rich moon with extensive automated cracking fields.

name: Marker
description: A dense moon carrying the system’s oldest long-baseline navigation reflectors.

name: Meridian Verge
description: A remote ice world marking the boundary beyond which local traffic separates into the sector’s two weak routes.

name: Splitline Belt
description: A narrow belt used as a visual and radar reference when calibrating outbound courses.

name: Last Measure
description: A quiet, cold red dwarf with predictable output and very weak flaring.

name: First Count
description: An airless inner planet covered in ancient impact scars and navigation monuments.

name: Hush
description: A dark transitional world with frozen volatiles trapped beneath a dusty crust.

name: Surveyor
description: A cold gas giant whose regular radio emissions support long-range calibration.

name: Testament
description: The inhabited outer moon carrying the final calibrated beacon before Far Meridian’s longest transit gap.

name: Pendulum
description: A narrow, elongated moon used to verify local orbital timing.

name: Final Mark
description: A remote frozen world beyond the beacon community and the last charted body in the system.

name: Shenzhou Anchor
description: A failed star whose weak gravity has captured several wandering bodies into wide, unstable orbits.

name: Wuding
description: A captured rogue world with a thick nitrogen crust and a deep layer of exotic ice.

name: Hanlu
description: A dark, slowly tumbling world whose orbit changes measurably over a human lifetime.

name: Luoyin
description: A cold captured gas giant moving on a steeply inclined orbit.

name: Anchorfall
description: A small moon likely captured with Luoyin and now undergoing tidal fracture.

name: Suixing
description: A newly captured rogue world on an orbit that may become unbound within several millennia.

name: Shenzhou Drift Belt
description: A shifting population of small captured objects that makes the outer system difficult to chart.

name: Black Jade
description: The largest body in the current cluster, covered in dark hydrocarbon frost.

name: Cold Court
description: A dense rogue world with a fractured crust and residual internal heat.

name: Silent Bowl
description: An airless world whose broad equatorial basin serves as a temporary survey landmark.

name: Night Pearl
description: A cold gas giant emitting more heat from contraction than it receives from any star.

name: Closed Lantern
description: A small frozen world surrounded by a temporary cloud of captured fragments.

name: Heiyu Last
description: A chemically active rogue world with a dense ammonia-rich atmosphere sustained by internal heating.

name: Corda
description: A stable red dwarf with low flare activity and a compact planetary system.

name: Corda-I
description: A small airless world used for thermal and vacuum testing.

name: Corda-II
description: The system’s industrial center, orbited by sealed cylindrical habitats and precision-metal workshops.

name: Spindle Rock
description: A small moon containing the original excavations used to construct Corda’s first habitats.

name: Copper Thread
description: A dense moon supplying copper, nickel, and trace industrial metals.

name: Corda-III
description: A broad, low-density world with few useful ores and extensive abandoned survey camps.

name: Fine Ore Belt
description: A narrow belt containing small but exceptionally pure deposits used by Corda’s workshops.

name: Corda-IV
description: An outer ice world used for water extraction and heat disposal.

name: Finecut
description: A quiet orange dwarf illuminating a dense inner asteroid complex.

name: Edge
description: A dry inner world with thin mineral seams and extensive automated test ranges.

name: Main Cut Belt
description: The principal inhabited region, containing hundreds of hollowed workshops and claim habitats.

name: Scalpel
description: A large belt body with high-grade cobalt and chromium deposits.

name: Gauge
description: A compact metallic body used for high-precision extraction and calibration work.

name: Nerathis System

name: Thass Vale System
