name: Destroyer
description: A destroyer is a dedicated warship built to kill other warships, especially corvettes, frigates, raiders, and missile platforms. It has more firepower than a frigate but less endurance, command capacity, and strategic independence than a cruiser.

name: Monitor
description: A monitor is a slow, heavily armed system-defense vessel built to guard planets, stations, gates, and fixed lanes. It carries oversized weapons for its size but lacks the range and speed for expeditionary campaigns.

name: Tender
description: A tender is a support vessel that maintains, repairs, refuels, and reloads other ships, mechs, fighters, or drones. Unlike a carrier, it is not defined by launching combat craft, but by keeping a fleet functional.

name: Transport
description: A transport moves troops, vehicles, mechs, prisoners, refugees, or colonists under practical conditions. It is less comfortable than a liner and more personnel-focused than a freighter.

name: Dropship
description: A dropship carries troops, mechs, or vehicles from orbit to a planetary surface under fire. It is smaller than a voidship and built around atmospheric entry, landing, and extraction.

name: Gunship
description: A gunship is a compact armed vessel used for patrol, escort, close support, and station defense. It is heavier than a shuttle or interceptor but not large enough to count as a true warship class like a corvette.

name: Fighter
description: A fighter is a small attack craft deployed from carriers, stations, or planetary bases. It threatens other small craft, screens fleets, and attacks vulnerable ship systems in groups.

name: Bomber
description: A bomber is a strike craft built to deliver torpedoes, bombs, or heavy ordnance against ships, stations, and surface targets. It is slower and less agile than a fighter but far more dangerous to large vessels.

name: Shuttle
description: A shuttle is a small utility craft for short-range movement between ships, stations, and planets. It is usually unarmed or lightly armed, but every major vessel depends on them.

name: Cutter
description: A cutter is a small patrol vessel used for inspections, pursuit, customs enforcement, and anti-smuggling operations. It sits below a corvette and is common around stations, ports, and controlled lane exits.

name: Command Ship
description: A command ship is built around communications, battlefield control, staff operations, and fleet coordination. It may be lightly armed for its size, but losing one can collapse an entire operation.

name: Ark
description: An ark is a mass-evacuation or long-duration survival vessel built to carry populations through catastrophic displacement. It is not necessarily a warship, but its loss can decide the fate of a culture or colony.

name: Battleship
description: A battleship is a heavy capital ship built for sustained line combat against other major warships. It carries heavy armor and broadside firepower, making it slower than a battlecruiser but more durable in prolonged fleet engagements.

name: Wardog-Class Destroyer
visual: Narrow armored hull with oversized forward guns, flared engine baffles, and dense point-defense mounts along the spine.
behavior: Warship killer. Hunts corvettes, frigates, raiders, and missile platforms before they can threaten larger fleet assets.

name: Redoubt-Class Monitor
visual: Short, heavy vessel with thick armor belts and a single oversized dorsal cannon. Its engines are small for its mass.
behavior: System-defense vessel. Guards planets, stations, gates, and fixed lanes but lacks the speed for long-range campaigns.

name: Waystone-Class Transport
visual: Long troopship with armored habitation blocks, vehicle clamps, and multiple reinforced docking ramps.
behavior: Military personnel carrier. Moves troops, prisoners, evacuees, vehicles, and support crews through contested space.

name: Hammerfall-Class Dropship
visual: Compact assault craft with heat-blackened plating, folding landing legs, and ventral mech clamps.
behavior: Orbit-to-surface insertion craft. Delivers mechs and infantry into defended landing zones under fire.

name: Ferry-Class Shuttle
visual: Plain utility craft with boxy passenger compartments, broad docking collars, and stubby maneuvering wings.
behavior: Short-range transfer craft. Moves crew, cargo, passengers, and officials between ships, stations, and planetary ports.

name: Writ-Class Cutter
visual: Small patrol hull with a bright registry beacon, inspection clamps, and a forward boarding collar.
behavior: Customs and enforcement craft. Pursues smugglers, boards suspicious traffic, and patrols controlled lane exits.

name: Throneglass-Class Command Ship
visual: Tall central command tower set into a protected hull, surrounded by signal masts, relay dishes, and armored operations decks.
behavior: Fleet command vessel. Coordinates formations, restores communications under interference, and keeps campaigns organized across multiple fronts.

name: Valiant-Class Battleship
visual: Broad armored capital ship with layered gun decks, heavy broadside batteries, and a reinforced prow.
behavior: Line-combat capital ship. Trades fire with cruisers, carriers, and other battleships during sustained fleet engagements.

name: Reliquary-Class Monitor
visual: Old fortress-hull built around a planetary bombardment array, with shrine-like armor plating and minimal maneuvering systems.
behavior: Fixed defense and deterrence platform. Holds key worlds or relic sites where withdrawal is not considered acceptable.

name: Blackthorn-Class Destroyer
visual: Angular hunter-killer hull with torpedo racks recessed behind armored shutters and a low sensor profile.
behavior: Fast attack destroyer. Screens battle groups, intercepts raiders, and finishes crippled ships before they escape.

name: Magistrate-Class Cutter
visual: Clean white-and-black patrol craft with exposed scanner fins, docking hooks, and a compact holding bay.
behavior: Typically used as an inspection vessel. Enforces manifests, licensing rules, quarantine orders, and travel restrictions near major ports.

name: Meridian-Class Liner
visual: Long passenger hull with stacked habitation decks, observation bands, and reinforced lifeboat spines.
behavior: Mass-route civilian transport. Carries workers, pilgrims, and displaced populations on scheduled interstellar lanes.

name: Pike-Class Interceptor
visual: Needle-nosed pursuit craft with rear-heavy engines and minimal crew space.
behavior: Fast interception vessel. Catches smugglers, scouts, couriers, and damaged raiders before they reach a lane exit.

name: Razorback-Class Battlecruiser
visual: Long armored hull with angled weapon blisters and oversized engine blocks.
behavior: Fast capital striker. Breaks cruiser formations and disengages before slower battleships can force a sustained exchange.

name: Rampart-Class Battleship
visual: Broad, heavily plated capital ship with layered armor belts and recessed broadside batteries.
behavior: Line-combat battleship. Holds formation under heavy fire and trades sustained volleys with other major warships.

name: Cannonade-Class Battleship
visual: Blocky gun platform with stacked turret decks and armored ammunition vaults.
behavior: Heavy fire-support battleship. Saturates enemy battle lines with repeated broadsides until screens collapse.

name: Iron Saint-Class Dreadnought
visual: Monumental fortress-hull with chapel-like armor ribs, siege lances, and armored command towers.
behavior: Strategic siege dreadnought. Anchors campaigns against fortress worlds, capital stations, and hardened fleet positions.

name: Reprisal-Class Destroyer
visual: Lean warship with forward torpedo tubes, compact armor, and dense point-defense clusters.
behavior: Attack destroyer. Hunts frigates, screens battle groups, and finishes crippled capital ships at close range.

name: Anchor-Class Monitor
visual: Short, armored defense ship with oversized station-keeping thrusters and a spinal lance mount.
behavior: Fixed-defense monitor. Guards orbital approaches, fortress moons, and stable lane exits where mobility is less important than firepower.

name: Brazier-Class Tender
visual: Industrial support hull with exterior repair arms, furnace decks, and open-frame resupply racks.
behavior: Fleet service tender. Repairs damaged armor, reloads ordnance, and keeps patrol groups active away from dockyards.

name: Yardlight-Class Tender
visual: Long maintenance vessel with floodlit gantries, modular drydock clamps, and drone service bays.
behavior: Mobile refit tender. Supports mechs, fighters, and small warships during extended deployments.

name: Hearth-Class Tender
visual: Broad logistics hull with protected fuel tanks, spare crew quarters, and emergency fabrication bays.
behavior: Campaign support tender. Keeps damaged ships operational when withdrawal to a formal yard is impossible.

name: Column-Class Transport
visual: Armored troopship with stacked barracks, vehicle holds, and broad side docking ramps.
behavior: Military transport. Moves infantry, vehicles, prisoners, and support crews through contested routes.

name: Holdfast-Class Transport
visual: Reinforced convoy vessel with internal mech cradles and separated pressure compartments.
behavior: Heavy transport. Carries garrison forces and replacement equipment to systems expected to remain under siege.

name: Anvilfall-Class Dropship
visual: Heat-blackened assault craft with blunt armor, folding landing legs, and underbelly mech clamps.
behavior: Heavy dropship. Delivers mechs into active combat zones and remains low long enough to recover survivors.

name: Kestrel-Class Dropship
visual: Compact atmospheric craft with swept wings, reinforced nose plating, and rear assault ramps.
behavior: Rapid insertion dropship. Moves infantry and light frames from orbit to ground before defenses fully track the descent.

name: Foxfire-Class Gunship
visual: Small armed craft with chin turrets, side missile pods, and bright engine wash.
behavior: Close-support gunship. Escorts dropships, suppresses landing zones, and protects exposed ground columns.

name: Rook-Class Gunship
visual: Squat patrol craft with heavy belly armor, rotating cannon mounts, and armored cockpit glass.
behavior: Station-defense gunship. Holds close orbits, patrols docking zones, and responds quickly to boarding threats.

name: Sparrow-Class Fighter
visual: Light single-seat craft with narrow wings and paired nose lasers.
behavior: Common fleet fighter. Screens carriers, intercepts bombers, and overwhelms isolated targets in groups.

name: Talon-Class Fighter
visual: Angular superiority fighter with split tail fins and high-output maneuvering thrusters.
behavior: Space-superiority fighter. Hunts enemy strike craft and clears approach lanes for bombers and dropships.

name: Claymore-Class Bomber
visual: Heavy strike craft with armored bomb bays and oversized torpedo hardpoints.
behavior: Anti-ship bomber. Delivers capital-grade ordnance against cruisers, carriers, and exposed station defenses.

name: Cinder-Class Bomber
visual: Broad atmospheric bomber with thermal shielding, ventral payload racks, and rear defense turrets.
behavior: Surface-attack bomber. Destroys fortifications, armor columns, and fixed infrastructure from low orbit or atmosphere.

name: Gull-Class Shuttle
visual: Plain transfer craft with rounded passenger cabin, docking collar, and short-range engines.
behavior: Civilian shuttle. Moves passengers and light cargo between ships, stations, and orbital ports.

name: Parcel-Class Shuttle
visual: Boxy utility shuttle with external cargo rails and reinforced loading doors.
behavior: Cargo shuttle. Handles routine transfers that are too small for freighters and too frequent for full transports.

name: Picket-Class Cutter
visual: Small enforcement vessel with sensor fins, boarding clamps, and a high-visibility registry beacon.
behavior: Patrol cutter. Performs inspections, escorts detained ships, and chases smugglers inside controlled traffic zones.

name: Relay-Class Command Ship
visual: Protected signal vessel covered in antenna masts, shielded comms dishes, and operations decks.
behavior: Communications command ship. Restores fleet coordination under jamming, Mim interference, or battlefield signal collapse.

name: Strategos-Class Command Ship
visual: Armored command hull with layered CIC decks, flag officer quarters, and redundant tactical arrays.
behavior: Fleet command ship. Directs multi-system operations and keeps dispersed task groups aligned during long campaigns.

name: Haven-Class Ark
visual: Massive evacuation vessel with protected habitation cylinders, hydroponic decks, and external lifeboat clusters.
behavior: Refugee ark. Carries displaced populations through prolonged crisis when no stable colony is available.

name: Tabernacle-Class Ark
visual: Vast white-and-brass survival ship with internal commons, shrine decks, schools, and medical wards.
behavior: Cultural ark. Preserves communities, records, and institutions during system collapse or forced evacuation.

name: Freighter
description: A freighter is a civilian or commercial vessel built to move cargo between systems. It is usually slow, lightly armed, and dependent on escorts when traveling through unsafe lanes.

name: Liner
description: A liner is a passenger vessel built to move civilians, pilgrims, colonists, officials, or refugees in large numbers. Its value is measured by capacity, endurance, route reliability, and survivability rather than combat power.

name: Barge
description: A barge is a heavy utility vessel built for bulk hauling, salvage, mining, construction, or industrial support. It is not designed as a warship, but its machinery and cargo capacity make it important to frontier operations and fleet logistics.

name: Interceptor
description: An interceptor is a small, fast vessel used for pursuit, scouting, courier work, and rapid response. It can threaten light craft, but it is not built for sustained fleet combat.

name: Corvette
description: A corvette is the smallest true warship class, built for patrol, interception, raiding, and close escort work. It is fast and inexpensive enough to operate independently, but too lightly built to survive against heavier fleet units.

name: Frigate
description: A frigate is a fleet escort with the endurance, sensors, and weapons needed to protect larger ships or patrol dangerous lanes. It usually screens against fighters, missiles, raiders, and boarding threats rather than dueling larger warships directly.

name: Cruiser
description: A cruiser is a major warship that can operate independently or serve as the backbone of a patrol group or battle group. It carries enough weapons, armor, and command systems to dominate smaller ships while remaining cheaper and more flexible than true capital ships.

name: Carrier
description: A carrier is a warship built around hangars, launch bays, and support facilities for fighters, drones, mechs, or assault craft. Large carriers are capital ships because their deployed forces can decide battles far beyond the reach of the carrier’s own guns.

name: Battlecruiser
description: A battlecruiser is a capital ship built for speed, reach, and heavy striking power. It is designed to hunt cruisers, carriers, and weakened fleet assets, but it is less suited to prolonged exchanges with dreadnoughts.

name: Dreadnought
description: A dreadnought is the heaviest standard capital ship, built for decisive fleet engagements, sieges, and strategic intimidation. It is slow and expensive, but its armor and firepower can anchor an entire campaign.

name: Capital Ship
description: A capital ship is not a hull class by itself, but a strategic category for the largest and most important fleet assets. In normal usage, the term applies to fleet carriers, battlecruisers, dreadnoughts, and unusually large cruisers or support vessels.

name: Late Primus Collapse
description: The Late Primus Collapse was the final pre-Exodus period in which war, ecological failure, and institutional decay reduced Primus to isolated city-states. Humanity began the Exodus only after the homeworld had already lost the capacity to recover.

name: Core Proliferation Crisis
description: The Core Proliferation Crisis began when unstable Resonance Cores spread faster than any institution could regulate them. The Guild ended the crisis by consolidating production and making access to safe Cores dependent on its approval.

name: First Contact
description: First Contact was the first public encounter between human civilization and the Mims, ending the Guild's ability to suppress evidence of alien life. The event permanently altered interstellar society and began the conditions that became the New Dark Age.

name: The New Dark Age
description: The New Dark Age is the post-First Contact era in which civilization survives under restricted communication, controlled information, and permanent threat conditions. Human space remains connected, but most colonies know little beyond their local Guild lanes.

name: Duke
description: Crown noble rank. Rules a whole sector.

name: Marquess
description: Crown noble rank. Commands a major frontier, fortress system, or strategic border region.

name: Count
description: Crown noble rank. Rules a system.

name: Viscount
description: Crown noble rank. Administers a major world or portion of a larger system.

name: Baron
description: Crown noble rank. Controls a continent on a major world, a moon, major fortress, or minor world.

name: Knight
description: Crown noble rank. Controls a minor city, settlement, or fortress on a world or moon.

name: Anax
description: Supreme commander of Cindral. An Anax is an Archon elected by the other Archons to lead the March during existential threats, major wars, frontier collapses, or multi-sector-wide emergencies.

name: Archon
description: Cindral Genos rank. An Archon is a noble house charged with the defense of an entire sector.

name: Polemarch
description: Cindral Genos rank. A Polemarch is a noble house charged with the defense of an entire star system.

name: Strategos
description: A Strategos is a Cindral noble rank granted to a house responsible for defending a major world or strategically important part of a system. The plural form is Strategoi.

name: Phylarch
description: Cindral Genos rank. A Phylarch is a noble house charged with the defense of a world, moon, or colony that doesn't quite deserve the attention of a Strategos.

name: Spartos
description: A Spartos is an earned Cindral founder-rank granted to an individual who receives a Kleros for extraordinary service and assumes responsibility for a defined civic population. The plural form is Spartoi.

name: Genos
description: A recognized Cindral noble lineage carrying a sanctioned Kleros. A Genos is both a family and a public defense institution, entrusted with protecting a defined population, world, system, or sector.

name: Kleros
description: A protected bio-engineering formula implanted into a Cindral noble lineage. Each Kleros has a documented medical profile, inheritance protocol, failure risk, and intended defensive purpose.

name: Leitourgia
description: The Cindral doctrine of public burden. Leitourgia holds that engineered advantage creates obligation, not entitlement, and that nobles possess their Kleros in order to protect those who do not.

name: Phylake
description: A protected charge entrusted to a Cindral noble house or honored protector. A Phylake may be a sector, system, world, moon, city, fortress, convoy population, shelter network, or settlement cluster.

name: Akleros
description: A condemned Cindral noble or house judged unworthy of its Kleros. The term is applied to those who abandon their charges, misuse their engineered advantages, or preserve their lineage at the expense of Cindral lives.

name: Genos Calystron
description: Genos Calystron coordinates the defense of Cindral Sector and its evacuation infrastructure. Its current head holds the emergency Anaxate, a mandate requiring the house to place the survival of the March above its own lineage.

name: Genos Melanthorne
description: Genos Melanthorne defends Ashveil Sector, the thinly held frontier connecting the Mawward March to the Silent Way. The house maintains observation networks, reserve settlements, relay chains, and abandoned colonial claims while training its commanders to distrust isolated reports and preserve distant populations that might otherwise disappear without warning.

name: Genos Aegesworth
description: Genos Aegesworth commands the defense of the Cindral System, including its capital world, emergency government sites, fortress moons, industrial reserves, and shelter networks beneath the failing Ember Sun. The house controls the practical machinery of survival, ensuring that heat shields, evacuation routes, buried armories, fuel reserves, and replacement ministries remain functional during a system-wide collapse.

name: Genos Orestwyck
description: Genos Orestwyck holds Braxis, the March's primary bastion system, where every station, moon, settlement, and defensive line exists to delay Mawward threats. Its commanders measure success through time purchased for evacuation and reinforcement, accepting the loss of individual fortifications so long as the wider defensive plan continues to function.

name: Genos Eirenhall
description: Genos Eirenhall safeguards Red Choir, coordinating its muster fields, refugee docks, triage vessels, emergency beacon towers, sealed stores, and civilian transport network. Its commanders are judged by the number of people successfully extracted and resettled rather than by territory held, and they are authorized to abandon any position once the population under their protection has been removed.

name: Genos Damarford
description: Genos Damarford defends Ashveil Prime, maintaining the frontier capital, command bastions, listening posts, reserve settlements, and relay chains that connect the Mawward March to the Silent Way. Its doctrine recognizes that Ashveil cannot defeat every threat it encounters, so its forces are organized to preserve communications, maintain fallback positions, and prevent isolated losses from becoming a sector-wide collapse.

name: Genos Nyctworth
description: Genos Nyctworth commands the surveillance network at Duskwatch, where separated stations compare observations to detect Maw activity, deep-space distortions, and unstable lane conditions. The house is known for exhaustive verification procedures and assumes that any single witness, sensor platform, or official record may have been deceived, compromised, or altered.

name: Genos Threnemere
description: Genos Threnemere retains responsibility for Hollow Verge despite the system's abandonment and the collapse of most formal government there. The house monitors surviving habitats, derelict stations, automated defenses, illegal settlements, and salvage operations while preserving the records needed to contain the system or reclaim it should the Cindral frontier ever advance again.

name: Guild Standard Calendar
description: The Guild Standard Calendar is derived from the civil calendar once used across old Primus. It provides a shared method of dating events between systems whose local years and day lengths may differ.

name: Proto-Manifold Drive
description: The Proto-Manifold Drive was the unstable faster-than-light technology used during the Exodus. Its enormous fuel requirements and poor navigational precision caused many colony vessels to become lost or stranded far from their intended destinations.

name: Silent Way
description: The Silent Way is a damaged Manifold corridor running from Ashveil through Halix territory. Persistent Mim activity has made the route one of the most heavily monitored passages in settled space.

name: Mawward March
description: The Mawward March is the frontier route extending from Luthan space into the Cindral sectors. Its lanes lead toward regions scarred by the Stellar Maw, leaving the Cindral March as the inner systems’ principal buffer.

name: Choir Path
description: The Choir Path is a pilgrimage route connecting Primus with the territories of the Veyran Choir. Shrines and wandering fleets gather along its length, giving the route immense religious importance.

name: Memetic Hazard
description: A memetic hazard is information that becomes dangerous when perceived or understood. Exposure may alter memory, compel behavior, or create a channel through which an outside intelligence can influence the mind.

name: Core Realization
description: Core Realization is the point at which a Core reaches full biological maturity and becomes independently stable. A realized Core is far more adaptable than a constrained industrial Core and may eventually develop a self-aware JIN.

name: Core Forging
description: Core Forging is the cultivation of Resonance-sensitive tissue into a functional Core. The Guild controls sanctioned forging because unauthorized alterations can produce unstable or unpredictable growth.

name: Crucible Core
description: A Crucible Core is a Resonance Core altered through Karnate methods to produce extreme heat and power. Its accelerated metabolism transforms nearby machinery and makes long-term stability difficult.

name: Temporal Energy
description: Temporal energy forms where the normal progression of time becomes distorted and can remain trapped after major chronal events. Harvesting it risks deepening the distortion and causing contradictory moments to manifest together.

name: Paradox Core
description: A Paradox Core sustains machinery by containing temporal contradictions that allow incompatible components to function together. Destroying it forces the machine into a single stable history, causing unsupported structures to disappear.

name: Crown Lineage Formula
description: A Crown Lineage Formula is a hereditary bioengineering sequence controlled by a recognized noble house and used to preserve traits associated with its dynasty. Unauthorized alteration or reproduction is treated as an attack on the house's legitimacy.

name: The Refugee Crisis
description: The Refugee Crisis began during the collapse of Asterion and has expanded with every later catastrophe. Most displaced people either enter exploitative Luthan labor systems or settle vulnerable frontier colonies outside the protection of major powers.

name: Infantry-Scale Exo-Organism
description: Infantry-scale exo-organisms can be engaged by individual soldiers or conventional ground units. They rarely threaten a warframe directly unless they attack through infestation or overwhelming numbers.

name: Titan-Scale Exo-Organism
description: Titan-scale exo-organisms possess enough mass or destructive power to engage warframes. Their appearance normally requires a mechanized response rather than ordinary infantry containment.

name: Ship-Scale Exo-Organism
description: Ship-scale exo-organisms are void-capable entities comparable to military spacecraft. They can survive prolonged exposure to space and threaten vessels without relying upon conventional weapons.

name: Planetary-Scale Exo-Organism
description: Planetary-scale exo-organisms are terrestrial units whose size and firepower exceed what a standard warframe can reasonably confront. Their appearance usually marks the end of conventional containment efforts and may result in permanent lane revocation.

name: Black Hole
description: A black hole is a collapsed mass whose gravity prevents light from escaping beyond its event horizon.

name: Class A (Bright white)
description: A Class A star is a hot white main-sequence star with a comparatively short lifespan and intense visible luminosity.

name: Class B (Blue white)
description: A Class B star is a massive blue-white star that burns rapidly and emits powerful ultraviolet radiation.

name: Class B (Blue-white)
description: A Class B star is a massive blue-white star that burns rapidly and emits powerful ultraviolet radiation.

name: Class F (White)
description: A Class F star is a bright white main-sequence star hotter and more massive than a yellow Class G star.

name: Class G (Yellow Sun like)
description: A Class G star is a stable yellow main-sequence star capable of remaining active for billions of years.

name: Class G (Yellow Sun-like)
description: A Class G star is a stable yellow main-sequence star capable of remaining active for billions of years.

name: Class K (Orange Dwarf)
description: A Class K star is a long-lived orange dwarf whose steady output makes it favorable for persistent planetary environments.

name: Class L (Brown Dwarf)
description: A Class L brown dwarf is a cool substellar body whose atmosphere contains dense clouds of mineral condensates.

name: Class M (Red Dwarf)
description: A Class M star is a dim red dwarf that burns slowly and can remain active for immense periods of time.

name: Class T (Brown Dwarf)
description: A Class T brown dwarf is a cold substellar body marked by methane-rich atmospheric absorption.

name: Magnetar
description: A magnetar is a neutron star whose extraordinarily powerful magnetic field produces violent radiation bursts.

name: Neutron Star
description: A neutron star is the ultradense remnant of a massive star compressed into a body only a few kilometers across.

name: Red Giant (M)
description: A Class M red giant is an aging star that has expanded into an enormous cool envelope after exhausting much of its core fuel.

name: T Tauri Star
description: A T Tauri star is a young and unstable star still contracting toward the main sequence while shedding powerful stellar winds.

name: White Dwarf
description: A white dwarf is the dense stellar remnant left after a low- or medium-mass star expels its outer layers.

name: Ammonia World
description: An Ammonia World is a cold planet whose surface environment or atmospheric chemistry is dominated by ammonia.

name: Atmosphere Planet
description: An Atmosphere Planet is a terrestrial world distinguished by a substantial gaseous envelope capable of shaping its climate and surface.

name: Class I Gas Giant
description: A Class I gas giant is a cold world whose upper atmosphere is covered by pale ammonia clouds.

name: Class II Gas Giant
description: A Class II gas giant is a temperate world whose visible atmosphere is dominated by reflective water-vapor clouds.

name: Class III Gas Giant
description: A Class III gas giant is a warm and largely cloudless world whose deeper atmosphere gives it a dark blue appearance.

name: Class IV Gas Giant
description: A Class IV gas giant is a hot world whose atmosphere contains broad alkali-metal absorption that gives it a dark coloration.

name: Class V Gas Giant
description: A Class V gas giant is an intensely heated world wrapped in luminous clouds of silicates and vaporized metals.

name: High Metal Content Planet
description: A High Metal Content Planet is a rocky world containing an unusually large proportion of metallic material within its crust and mantle.

name: Icy Planet
description: An Icy Planet is a cold terrestrial world whose surface is predominantly covered by frozen volatiles.

name: Metal Rich Planet
description: A Metal Rich Planet is a dense world composed primarily of metallic material rather than conventional silicate rock.

name: Rocky Ice Dwarf Planet
description: A Rocky Ice Dwarf Planet is a small rounded world composed of a mixture of stone and frozen volatiles.

name: Rocky Ice Planet
description: A Rocky Ice Planet is a terrestrial world whose surface and interior contain substantial amounts of both stone and frozen material.

name: Rocky Planet
description: A Rocky Planet is a terrestrial world with a solid surface composed primarily of silicate stone.

name: Water Giant
description: A Water Giant is a large planet containing a deep global ocean above an immense high-pressure water mantle.

name: Water World
description: A Water World is a terrestrial planet whose surface is almost entirely covered by liquid water.

name: Ammonia Moon
description: An Ammonia Moon is a natural satellite whose frozen surface or subsurface environment contains abundant ammonia.

name: Atmosphere Moon
description: An Atmosphere Moon is a natural satellite massive or active enough to retain a substantial gaseous envelope.

name: High Metal Content Moon
description: A High Metal Content Moon is a natural satellite containing an unusually large proportion of metallic material.

name: Icy Moon
description: An Icy Moon is a natural satellite whose surface is predominantly composed of frozen volatiles.

name: Metal Rich Moon
description: A Metal Rich Moon is a dense natural satellite composed primarily of metallic material.

name: Rocky Ice Moon
description: A Rocky Ice Moon is a natural satellite formed from a mixture of silicate rock and frozen volatiles.

name: Rocky Moon
description: A Rocky Moon is a natural satellite with a solid surface composed primarily of stone.

name: Water Moon
description: A Water Moon is a natural satellite containing a major liquid-water ocean either on its surface or beneath an icy crust.

name: Asteroid Belt
description: An Asteroid Belt is a broad orbital region populated by numerous rocky or metallic minor bodies.

name: Debris Belt
description: A Debris Belt is an orbital band of fragmented material produced by collisions or the destruction of larger bodies.

name: Dust-rich Debris Belt
description: A Dust-rich Debris Belt is a fragmented orbital region containing enough fine particulate matter to obscure sensors and scatter light.

name: Electrically Charged Debris Belt
description: An Electrically Charged Debris Belt is an orbital band whose particles carry persistent electrical charges capable of disrupting nearby systems.

name: Icy Asteroid Belt
description: An Icy Asteroid Belt is an orbital region populated by minor bodies composed largely of frozen volatiles.

name: Irradiated Debris Belt
description: An Irradiated Debris Belt is an orbital field whose constituent material has been saturated by dangerous levels of stellar or artificial radiation.

name: Protoplanetary Disk
description: A Protoplanetary Disk is a rotating field of gas and dust surrounding a young star from which planets may eventually form.

name: Scattered Ice Field
description: A Scattered Ice Field is a diffuse region of widely separated frozen bodies occupying distant and irregular orbits.

name: Asteroid Field
description: An Asteroid Field is a localized concentration of rocky minor bodies lacking a stable belt-like orbit.

name: Debris Field
description: A Debris Field is a dispersed cloud of wreckage or fragmented celestial material lacking a stable belt-like orbit.

name: High Metal Content Asteroid
description: A High Metal Content Asteroid is a minor body containing a substantial mixture of metallic ore and silicate rock.

name: Icy Planet Composition
description: An Icy Planet Composition body is a planetesimal formed primarily from frozen volatiles.

name: Rocky Asteroid
description: A Rocky Asteroid is a minor body composed predominantly of silicate stone.

name: Rocky Ice Planet Composition
description: A Rocky Ice Planet Composition body is a planetesimal containing comparable amounts of stone and frozen material.

name: Rocky Planet Composition
description: A Rocky Planet Composition body is a planetesimal composed primarily of silicate material suitable for terrestrial planet formation.

name: Aeon Archive
description: An Aeon Archive is a hardened repository intended to preserve knowledge across civilizational collapse or extreme spans of time.

name: Bastion Wall
description: A Bastion Wall is a heavily armed defensive installation positioned to block access to a strategic approach.

name: Blackspire
description: A Blackspire is a fortified command installation built for covert observation and secure military coordination.

name: Blood Dock
description: A Blood Dock is a brutal repair and processing facility associated with forced labor or the handling of biological war machinery.

name: Border Redoubt
description: A Border Redoubt is an isolated fortification tasked with maintaining control along a remote territorial frontier.

name: Buffer Spire
description: A Buffer Spire is a fortified station intended to delay an approaching threat long enough for nearby populations to respond.

name: Crystech Vault
description: A Crystech Vault is a sealed installation designed to contain Resonance-active crystal or recovered Cerebrax material.

name: Cultural Archive
description: A Cultural Archive is a protected repository preserving the history and identity of a specific population.

name: Drift Market
description: A Drift Market is a mobile or loosely anchored commercial installation serving transient frontier traffic.

name: Escort Yard
description: An Escort Yard is a military dock specialized in maintaining patrol craft and convoy-defense vessels.

name: Fabricator Yard
description: A Fabricator Yard is an industrial installation capable of manufacturing complex machinery from processed feedstock.

name: Foundry Lattice
description: A Foundry Lattice is an interconnected industrial complex built to process raw material across a distributed orbital structure.

name: Glass Docks
description: Glass Docks are high-capacity commercial berths distinguished by extensive transparent habitats and exposed docking galleries.

name: Gun Bazaar
description: A Gun Bazaar is a loosely regulated market devoted to the exchange of weapons and military technology.

name: Habitat Spindle
description: A Habitat Spindle is a rotating orbital settlement that produces artificial gravity through its motion.

name: Harvest Net
description: A Harvest Net is a distributed installation designed to collect valuable material from an atmosphere or diffuse orbital environment.

name: Helium Rich
description: A Helium Rich installation is a processing facility positioned near a resource source with unusually abundant helium reserves.

name: Iron Halo
description: An Iron Halo is a ring of armored installations surrounding a world or strategic orbital position.

name: Light Mirror Array
description: A Light Mirror Array is a coordinated formation of orbital reflectors used to redirect stellar illumination.

name: March Bastion
description: A March Bastion is a Cindral frontier fortress designed to support prolonged defense without outside reinforcement.

name: Mech Forge
description: A Mech Forge is an industrial installation equipped to grow, assemble, and maintain mechanized warframes.

name: Nomad Cradle
description: A Nomad Cradle is a mobile habitat and service installation built to support populations without a permanent planetary home.

name: Nomad Dock
description: A Nomad Dock is a flexible anchorage designed to resupply migratory fleets and transient communities.

name: Ore Spine
description: An Ore Spine is a reinforced extraction complex built directly around a major mineral deposit.

name: Penitent Dock
description: A Penitent Dock is a Veyran-controlled anchorage used to receive pilgrims undergoing religious service or punishment.

name: Pilgrim Ring
description: A Pilgrim Ring is an orbital habitat structured around the needs of religious travelers and ceremonial gatherings.

name: Quarantine Ring
description: A Quarantine Ring is an isolated orbital installation used to contain contaminated vessels or populations.

name: Refinery Crucible
description: A Refinery Crucible is a high-output industrial facility that converts difficult raw material through extreme heat and pressure.

name: Refuge Spire
description: A Refuge Spire is a fortified habitat intended to shelter displaced populations during prolonged emergencies.

name: Rift Monitor
description: A Rift Monitor is a sensor installation positioned to detect changes in a dimensional fracture.

name: Salvage Cradle
description: A Salvage Cradle is a processing installation where recovered wreckage is dismantled and repurposed.

name: Scrap Docks
description: Scrap Docks are rough industrial berths that repair vessels using salvaged and improvised components.

name: Sentinel Array
description: A Sentinel Array is a distributed network of defensive sensors and weapons guarding a strategic region.

name: Signal Lock
description: A Signal Lock is a hardened communications installation that controls long-range transmissions within its assigned region.

name: Silent Haven
description: A Silent Haven is a concealed anchorage engineered to suppress emissions and avoid detection.

name: Smuggler Cradle
description: A Smuggler Cradle is a hidden service installation supporting illicit cargo traffic and unregistered vessels.

name: Transit Hub
description: A Transit Hub is a major transfer installation positioned where shipping routes or passenger networks converge.

name: Void Observatory
description: A Void Observatory is a remote research installation dedicated to studying deep space and extranormal phenomena.

name: Warden Keep
description: A Warden Keep is a fortified military installation responsible for maintaining control over a strategic region.

name: Wreckyard
description: A Wreckyard is an orbital field or station where derelict vessels are stored for salvage and disassembly.

name: Crown Heraldry
description: Crown heraldry identifies both personal status and feudal allegiance. High-ranking knights bear individual arms marked by their liege’s heraldry, while lesser retainers use colors or modified arms derived from the house they serve.

name: Crown Vassalage
description: Crown vassalage is a formal bond in which a lesser noble or knight pledges service to a more powerful house in exchange for protection and patronage. The relationship becomes part of the vassal’s public identity and is commonly reflected in their heraldry.

name: Crown Succession
description: Crown titles may be inherited regardless of gender. Most houses favor either the eldest eligible heir or the family member considered most accomplished, depending on their individual succession customs.

name: Noble Wardship
description: Noble wardship places an heir under the protection and education of another house. It is uncommon and usually occurs only when the heir’s own family can no longer safely provide for them or as part of an exceptional political settlement.

name: Knightly Honorific
description: A knightly honorific is a ceremonial title granted when a knight is formally elevated, often describing a virtue, origin, or symbolic association.

name: Analog Media Culture
description: Guild restrictions on the Net have greatly reduced the distribution of digital entertainment. Most modern media is produced in physical formats, with surviving works from old Primus frequently restored or reproduced as cultural artifacts.

name: Conventional Transit
description: Conventional spacecraft can reach roughly two percent of light speed with sublight engines, although acceleration and deceleration prevent them from maintaining that velocity throughout most journeys. Planetary transportation is only moderately faster than that of old Primus and may be considerably slower in poorly developed systems.

name: Micro-Manifold Jump
description: A Micro-Manifold Jump is a precision transition used to cross a star system in hours rather than days. It consumes enough fuel that conventional sublight travel remains preferable when time is not critical.

name: Bioengineering
description: Bioengineering is the deliberate alteration of living tissue and heredity through advanced genetic and biomechanical methods. Reliable work is costly and tightly controlled; Crown and Cindral noble authority depends on proprietary formulas, while cheaper procedures often cause lasting instability.

name: Mutations
description: Mutations are increasingly common inherited traits caused by prolonged Resonance exposure and centuries of bioengineering. Most are minor physical variations, while innate psionic ability remains a rare and poorly understood expression.

name: Indentured Mercenaries
description: Indentured Mercenaries are Luthan soldiers bound to service by debts and employer-controlled contract costs. Though legally voluntary, these arrangements are often structured so that repayment and departure become effectively impossible.

name: Resonance Forging
description: Resonance Forging is the process of binding a fixed Resonance effect into a manufactured object through the regulation of a Core or DMN-Unit. The result performs a limited function but cannot adapt or develop as a true Core can.

name: MICRO-EXO-ORGANISM
description: A nonhuman organism below conventional infantry scale. The classification is based on its physical size and operational presence rather than its intelligence or biological complexity.

name: EXO-SHIP
description: A nonhuman entity capable of sustained travel and combat in space. The classification is determined by its function as a voidcraft rather than its construction or origin.

name: TITAN-EXO-VEHICLE
description: A nonhuman vehicle or mobile construct operating at Titan scale. It functions as an independent major battlefield asset.

name: PLANETARY-EXO-VEHICLE
description: A nonhuman vehicle or mobile construct operating at planetary scale. Its activity can determine the survival or long-term stability of an entire world.

name: Listener
description: A probationary adherent receiving instruction in Veyran doctrine and controlled Resonance use.

name: Cantor
description: An initiated member authorized to lead routine rites and communal chanting.

name: Resonant Adept
description: A trained practitioner permitted to channel psionic-resonance without supervision.

name: Chantkeeper
description: A senior Cantor responsible for preserving approved rites and local doctrine.

name: Hymnwright
description: A technical cleric trained to maintain Veyran machinery and Resonance systems.

name: Reliquarian
description: A custodian assigned to relic Cores and other restricted sacred objects.

name: Anchorite
description: A vowed cleric assigned to a permanent post or protected charge.

name: Hierophant
description: A recognized teacher whose doctrinal interpretations influence multiple choirs.

name: Chorus-Seer
description: A seer capable of receiving coherent visions through the Great Chorus.

name: Blackwake Family
description: An old Orak dynasty descended from the earliest pirate settlements in the Belt. Blackwake controls more territory than any other syndicate and takes a cut from most activity within its space.

name: Nine Knives
description: A coalition of independent crews operating under a single syndicate. Its branches remain heavily involved in raiding and mercenary work, with a notable presence in narcotics production and distribution.

name: Brass Hand
description: A commercially minded syndicate comfortable operating behind legitimate fronts. Crown and Luthan authorities suspect Brass Hand involvement in laundering, illegal salvage, fencing, and smuggling, but have failed to establish direct links.

name: Gravecoil
description: A primarily shipborne syndicate with few permanent holdings. Gravecoil commands arguably the largest fleet among the syndicates, though much of it consists of aging or heavily modified vessels.

name: Dog Chain
description: A younger syndicate formed from displaced populations and independent crews. Dog Chain is particularly active in contraband and narcotics trafficking, with a reputation for aggressive raiding and scavenging.

name: Iron Teeth
description: A militant syndicate descended from mercenary flotillas that settled around isolated mining communities. Iron Teeth crews regularly move between mercenary work and piracy while taking a cut of local mining profits.

name: Farreach Shipping Combine
description: The League’s largest cargo carrier, with fleets and depots spanning nearly every major lane. Farreach controls enough freight capacity to influence prices simply by changing where its ships are assigned. “Farther, Faster, Farreach.”

name: Vasker Naval Works
description: A warship builder that produces everything from escorts to capital vessels for governments and private fleets. Vasker is one of the few companies that holds direct Guild contracts for interstellar ships. “Security, Delivered.”

name: Meridian Ordnance Group
description: A weapons group supplying infantry arms, frame systems, and naval weaponry across civilized space. In addition to its own specialty items, it is one of the largest producers of Guild-standardized equipment. “The Standard of Peace.”

name: Greenmantle Agricultural
description: The largest food and agricultural technology corporation, with holdings across hundreds of inhabited worlds. Greenmantle controls enough food production to make entire governments depend on its supply contracts. “Your World, Our Harvest.”

name: Aurex Biologics
description: A pharmaceutical and genetic services company providing some of the most advanced medicine, medical technology, and gene-splicing procedures in the galaxy. Aurex also maintains private genetic archives valuable to governments and noble houses. “A Better You, A Better Tomorrow.”

name: Titan Foundry Group
description: The largest manufacturing conglomerate and a major producer of the machinery used to build other machinery. Titan supplies industrial equipment, vehicles, station components, and standardized infrastructure throughout the League, with some colonies built almost entirely from Titan-made equipment. “Titan-Built, Titan-Strong.”

name: Deepwell Extraction
description: The largest hard-mining corporation, operating extensive asteroid and planetary extraction networks. Deepwell produces enough raw material to materially affect the cost of shipbuilding and industry across multiple sectors. “Dig Deeper. Build Bigger.”

name: Ceyra Atmospheric Consortium
description: The largest gas-extraction corporation, built around harvesting planetary atmospheres and gas giants. Its tanker fleets supply industrial gases, feedstocks, and sublight fuel to much of the galaxy. “The Galaxy Runs on Ceyra.”

name: Waymaker Civil Group
description: The largest civil contracting firm in the galaxy, hired for major infrastructure projects throughout inhabited space. Waymaker routinely enters undeveloped systems before permanent governments or major commercial institutions are established. “Building the Future, Today.”
